The comparison group may be the general population from which the cohort is drawn, or it may be another cohort of persons thought to have had little or no exposure to the substance under investigation, but otherwise similar. variants.definition: If the file can be downloaded, URL to download the binary.

variants.name: drainsTo
variants.definition: The vasculature that the vein drains into.

variants.name: drug
variants.definition: A drug in this drug class.

variants.name: Drug
variants.definition: A chemical or biologic substance, used as a medical therapy, that has a physiological effect on an organism.

variants.name: drugClass
variants.definition: The class of drug this belongs to (e.g., statins).

variants.name: DrugClass
variants.definition: A class of medical drugs, e.g., statins. Classes can represent general pharmacological class, common mechanisms of action, common physiological effects, etc.

variants.name: DrugCost
variants.definition: The cost per unit of a medical drug. Note that this type is not meant to represent the price in an offer of a drug for sale; see the Offer type for that. This type will typically be used to tag wholesale or average retail cost of a drug, or maximum reimbursable cost. Costs of medical drugs vary widely depending on how and where they are paid for, so while this type captures some of the variables, costs should be used with caution by consumers of this schema's markup.

variants.name: DrugCostCategory
variants.definition: Enumerated categories of medical drug costs.

variants.name: DrugLegalStatus
variants.definition: The legal availability status of a medical drug.

variants.name: DrugPregnancyCategory
variants.definition: Categories that represent an assessment of the risk of fetal injury due to a drug or pharmaceutical used as directed by the mother during pregnancy.

variants.name: DrugPrescriptionStatus
variants.definition: Indicates whether this drug is available by prescription or over-the-counter.

variants.name: DrugStrength
variants.definition: A specific strength in which a medical drug is available in a specific country.

variants.name: drugUnit
variants.definition: The unit in which the drug is measured, e.g. '5 mg tablet'.

variants.name: duplicateTherapy
variants.definition: A therapy that duplicates or overlaps this one.

variants.name: Ear
variants.definition: Ear

variants.name: embedUrl
variants.definition: A URL pointing to a player for a specific video. In general, this is the information in the src element of an embed tag and should not be the same as the content of the loc tag. (previous spelling: embedURL)

variants.name: Emergency
variants.definition: A specific branch of medical science that is deals with the evaluation and initial treatment of medical conditions caused by trauma or sudden illness.

variants.name: employee
variants.definition: Someone working for this organization.

variants.name: encoding
variants.definition: A media object that encode this CreativeWork.

variants.name: Endocrine
variants.definition: A specific branch of medical science that pertains to diagnosis and treatment of disorders of endocrine glands and their secretions.

variants.name: endorsers
variants.definition: People or organizations that endorse the plan.

variants.name: EnrollingByInvitation
variants.definition: Enrolling participants by invitation only.

variants.name: epidemiology
variants.definition: The characteristics of associated patients, such as age, gender, race etc.

variants.name: episode
variants.definition: An episode of a TV/radio series or season

variants.name: estimatesRiskOf
variants.definition: The condition, complication, or symptom whose risk is being estimated.

variants.name: event
variants.definition: Upcoming or past event associated with this place or organization.

variants.name: evidenceLevel
variants.definition: Strength of evidence of the data used to formulate the guideline (enumerated).

variants.name: EvidenceLevelA
variants.definition: Data derived from multiple randomized clinical trials or meta-analyses.

variants.name: EvidenceLevelB
variants.definition: Data derived from a single randomized trial, or nonrandomized studies.

variants.name: EvidenceLevelC
variants.definition: Only consensus opinion of experts, case studies, or standard-of-care.

variants.name: evidenceOrigin
variants.definition: Source of the data used to formulate the guidance, e.g. RCT, consensus opinion, etc.

variants.name: ExercisePlan
variants.definition: Fitness-related activity designed for a specific health-related purpose, including defined exercise routines as well as activity prescribed by a clinician.

variants.name: expectedPrognosis
variants.definition: The likely outcome in either the short term or long term of the medical condition.

variants.name: expertConsiderations
variants.definition: Medical expert advice related to the plan.

variants.name: Eye
variants.definition: Eye

variants.name: FDAcategoryA
variants.definition: A designation by the US FDA signifying that adequate and well-controlled studies have failed to demonstrate a risk to the fetus in the first trimester of pregnancy (and there is no evidence of risk in later trimesters).

variants.name: FDAcategoryB
variants.definition: A designation by the US FDA signifying that animal reproduction studies have failed to demonstrate a risk to the fetus and there are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women.

variants.name: FDAcategoryC
variants.definition: A designation by the US FDA signifying that animal reproduction studies have shown an adverse effect on the fetus and there are no adequate and well-controlled studies in humans, but potential benefits may warrant use of the drug in pregnant women despite potential risks.

variants.name: FDAcategoryD
variants.definition: A designation by the US FDA signifying that there is positive evidence of human fetal risk based on adverse reaction data from investigational or marketing experience or studies in humans, but potential benefits may warrant use of the drug in pregnant women despite potential risks.

variants.name: FDAcategoryX
variants.definition: A designation by the US FDA signifying that studies in animals or humans have demonstrated fetal abnormalities and/or there is positive evidence of human fetal risk based on adverse reaction data from investigational or marketing experience, and the risks involved in use of the drug in pregnant women clearly outweigh potential benefits.

variants.name: FDAnotEvaluated
variants.definition: A designation that the drug in question has not been assigned a pregnancy category designation by the US FDA.

variants.name: featureList
variants.definition: Features or modules provided by this application (and possibly required by other applications).

variants.name: fileFormat
variants.definition: MIME format of the binary (e.g. application/zip).

variants.name: fileSize
variants.definition: Size of the application / package (e.g. 18MB). In the absence of a unit (MB, KB etc.), KB will be assumed.

variants.name: Flexibility
variants.definition: Physical activity that is engaged in to improve joint and muscle flexibility.

variants.name: followup
variants.definition: Typical or recommended followup care after the procedure is performed.

variants.name: foodWarning
variants.definition: Any precaution, guidance, contraindication, etc. related to consumption of specific foods while taking this drug.

variants.name: founder
variants.definition: A person who founded this organization.

variants.name: frequency
variants.definition: How often the dose is taken, e.g. 'daily'.

variants.name: function
variants.definition: Function of the anatomical structure.

variants.name: functionalClass
variants.definition: The degree of mobility the joint allows.

variants.name: Fungus

variants.name: Gastroenterologic
variants.definition: A specific branch of medical science that pertains to diagnosis and treatment of disorders of digestive system.

variants.name: Genetic

variants.name: Genitourinary

variants.name: Geriatric
variants.definition: A specific branch of medical science that is concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of diseases, debilities and provision of care to the aged.

variants.name: guideline
variants.definition: A medical guideline related to this entity.

variants.name: guidelineDate
variants.definition: Date on which this guideline's recommendation was made.

variants.name: guidelineSubject
variants.definition: The medical conditions, treatments, etc. that are the subject of the guideline.

variants.name: Gynecologic
variants.definition: A specific branch of medical science that pertains to the health care of women, particularly in the diagnosis and treatment of disorders affecting the female reproductive system.

variants.name: Head
variants.definition: Head

variants.name: Hematologic
variants.definition: A specific branch of medical science that pertains to diagnosis and treatment of disorders of blood and blood producing organs.

variants.name: Homeopathic
variants.definition: A system of medicine based on the principle that a disease can be cured by a substance that produces similar symptoms in healthy people.

variants.name: howPerformed
variants.definition: How the procedure is performed.

variants.name: identifyingExam
variants.definition: A physical examination that can identify this sign.

variants.name: identifyingTest
variants.definition: A diagnostic test that can identify this sign.

variants.name: imagingTechnique
variants.definition: Imaging technique used.

variants.name: ImagingTest
variants.definition: Any medical imaging modality typically used for diagnostic purposes.

variants.name: includedRiskFactor
variants.definition: A modifiable or non-modifiable risk factor included in the calculation, e.g. age, coexisting condition.

variants.name: increasesRiskOf
variants.definition: The condition, complication, etc. influenced by this factor.

variants.name: indication
variants.definition: A factor that indicates use of this therapy for treatment and/or prevention of a condition, symptom, etc. For therapies such as drugs, indications can include both officially-approved indications as well as off-label uses. These can be distinguished by using the ApprovedIndication subtype of MedicalIndication.

variants.name: Infectious
variants.definition: A specific branch of medical science that pertains to diagnosis and treatment of bacterial, viral, fungal and parasitic infections.

variants.name: infectiousAgent
variants.definition: The actual infectious agent, such as a specific bacterium.

variants.name: infectiousAgentClass
variants.definition: The class of infectious agent (bacteria, prion, etc.) that causes the disease.

variants.name: InfectiousAgentClass
variants.definition: Classes of agents or pathogens that transmit infectious diseases. Enumerated type.

variants.name: InfectiousDisease
variants.definition: An infectious disease is a clinically evident human disease resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents, like pathogenic viruses, pathogenic bacteria, fungi, protozoa, multicellular parasites, and prions. To be considered an infectious disease, such pathogens are known to be able to cause this disease.

variants.name: insertion
variants.definition: The place of attachment of a muscle, or what the muscle moves.

variants.name: installUrl
variants.definition: URL at which the app may be installed, if different from the URL of the item.

variants.name: intensity
variants.definition: Quantitative measure gauging the degree of force involved in the exercise, for example, heartbeats per minute. May include the velocity of the movement.

variants.name: interactingDrug
variants.definition: Another drug that is known to interact with this drug in a way that impacts the effect of this drug or causes a risk to the patient. Note: disease interactions are typically captured as contraindications.

variants.name: InternationalTrial
variants.definition: An international trial.

variants.name: isAvailableGenerically
variants.definition: True if the drug is available in a generic form (regardless of name).

variants.name: isProprietary
variants.definition: True if this item's name is a proprietary/brand name (vs. generic name).

variants.name: Joint
variants.definition: The anatomical location at which two or more bones make contact.

variants.name: labelDetails
variants.definition: Link to the drug's label details.

variants.name: LaboratoryScience
variants.definition: Laboratory science.

variants.name: legalStatus
variants.definition: The drug or supplement's legal status, including any controlled substance schedules that apply.

variants.name: LeisureTimeActivity
variants.definition: Any physical activity engaged in for recreational purposes. Examples may include ballroom dancing, roller skating, canoeing, fishing, etc.

variants.name: LifestyleModification
variants.definition: A process of care involving exercise, changes to diet, fitness routines, and other lifestyle changes aimed at improving a health condition.

variants.name: Ligament
variants.definition: A short band of tough, flexible, fibrous connective tissue that functions to connect multiple bones, cartilages, and structurally support joints.

variants.name: Longitudinal
variants.definition: Unlike cross-sectional studies, longitudinal studies track the same people, and therefore the differences observed in those people are less likely to be the result of cultural differences across generations. Longitudinal studies are also used in medicine to uncover predictors of certain diseases.

variants.name: Lung
variants.definition: Lung

variants.name: LymphaticVessel
variants.definition: A type of blood vessel that specifically carries lymph fluid unidirectionally toward the heart.

variants.name: map
variants.definition: A URL to a map of the place.

variants.name: MaximumDoseSchedule
variants.definition: The maximum dosing schedule considered safe for a drug or supplement as recommended by an authority or by the drug/supplement's manufacturer. Capture the recommending authority in the recognizingAuthority property of MedicalEntity.

variants.name: maximumIntake
variants.definition: Recommended intake of this supplement for a given population as defined by a specific recommending authority.

variants.name: mechanismOfAction
variants.definition: The specific biochemical interaction through which this drug or supplement produces its pharmacological effect.

variants.name: MedicalCause
variants.definition:
The causative agent(s) that are responsible for the pathophysiologic process that eventually results in a medical condition, symptom or sign. In this schema, unless otherwise specified this is meant to be the proximate cause of the medical condition, symptom or sign. The proximate cause is defined as the causative agent that most directly results in the medical condition, symptom or sign. For example, the HIV virus could be considered a cause of AIDS. Or in a diagnostic context, if a patient fell and sustained a hip fracture and two days later sustained a pulmonary embolism which eventuated in a cardiac arrest, the cause of the cardiac arrest (the proximate cause) would be the pulmonary embolism and not the fall.

Medical causes can include cardiovascular, chemical, dermatologic, endocrine, environmental, gastroenterologic, genetic, hematologic, gynecologic, iatrogenic, infectious, musculoskeletal, neurologic, nutritional, obstetric, oncologic, otolaryngologic, pharmacologic, psychiatric, pulmonary, renal, rheumatologic, toxic, traumatic, or urologic causes; medical conditions can be causes as well.

variants.name: MedicalCode
variants.definition: A code for a medical entity.

variants.name: MedicalCondition
variants.definition: Any condition of the human body that affects the normal functioning of a person, whether physically or mentally. Includes diseases, injuries, disabilities, disorders, syndromes, etc.

variants.name: MedicalConditionStage
variants.definition: A stage of a medical condition, such as 'Stage IIIa'.

variants.name: MedicalContraindication
variants.definition: A condition or factor that serves as a reason to withhold a certain medical therapy. Contraindications can be absolute (there are no reasonable circumstances for undertaking a course of action) or relative (the patient is at higher risk of complications, but that these risks may be outweighed by other considerations or mitigated by other measures).

variants.name: MedicalDevice
variants.definition: Any object used in a medical capacity, such as to diagnose or treat a patient.

variants.name: MedicalDevicePurpose
variants.definition: Categories of medical devices, organized by the purpose or intended use of the device.

variants.name: MedicalEntity
variants.definition: The most generic type of entity related to health and the practice of medicine.

variants.name: MedicalEnumeration
variants.definition: Enumerations related to health and the practice of medicine.

variants.name: MedicalEvidenceLevel
variants.definition: Level of evidence for a medical guideline. Enumerated type.

variants.name: MedicalGuideline
variants.definition: Any recommendation made by a standard society (e.g. ACC/AHA) or consensus statement that denotes how to diagnose and treat a particular condition. Note: this type should be used to tag the actual guideline recommendation; if the guideline recommendation occurs in a larger scholarly article, use MedicalScholarlyArticle to tag the overall article, not this type. Note also: the organization making the recommendation should be captured in the recognizingAuthority base property of MedicalEntity.

variants.name: MedicalGuidelineContraindication
variants.definition: A guideline contraindication that designates a process as harmful and where quality of the data supporting the contraindication is sound.

variants.name: MedicalGuidelineRecommendation
variants.definition: A guideline recommendation that is regarded as efficacious and where quality of the data supporting the recommendation is sound.

variants.name: MedicalImagingTechnique
variants.definition: Any medical imaging modality typically used for diagnostic purposes. Enumerated type.

variants.name: MedicalIndication
variants.definition: A condition or factor that indicates use of a medical therapy, including signs, symptoms, risk factors, anatomical states, etc.

variants.name: MedicalIntangible
variants.definition: A utility class that serves as the umbrella for a number of 'intangible' things in the medical space.

variants.name: MedicalObservationalStudy
variants.definition: An observational study is a type of medical study that attempts to infer the possible effect of a treatment through observation of a cohort of subjects over a period of time. In an observational study, the assignment of subjects into treatment groups versus control groups is outside the control of the investigator. This is in contrast with controlled studies, such as the randomized controlled trials represented by MedicalTrial, where each subject is randomly assigned to a treatment group or a control group before the start of the treatment.

variants.name: MedicalObservationalStudyDesign
variants.definition: Design models for observational medical studies. Enumerated type.

variants.name: MedicalProcedure
variants.definition: A process of care used in either a diagnostic, therapeutic, or palliative capacity that relies on invasive (surgical), non-invasive, or percutaneous techniques.

variants.name: MedicalProcedureType
variants.definition: An enumeration that describes different types of medical procedures.

variants.name: MedicalRiskCalculator
variants.definition: A complex mathematical calculation requiring an online calculator, used to assess prognosis. Note: use the url property of Thing to record any URLs for online calculators.

variants.name: MedicalRiskEstimator
variants.definition: Any rule set or interactive tool for estimating the risk of developing a complication or condition.

variants.name: MedicalRiskFactor
variants.definition: A risk factor is anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing or contracting a disease, medical condition, or complication.

variants.name: MedicalRiskScore
variants.definition: A simple system that adds up the number of risk factors to yield a score that is associated with prognosis, e.g. CHAD score, TIMI risk score.

variants.name: MedicalScholarlyArticle
variants.definition: A scholarly article in the medical domain.

variants.name: MedicalSign
variants.definition: Any physical manifestation of a person's medical condition discoverable by objective diagnostic tests or physical examination.

variants.name: MedicalSignOrSymptom
variants.definition: Any indication of the existence of a medical condition or disease.

variants.name: MedicalSpecialty
variants.definition: Any specific branch of medical science or practice. Medical specialities include clinical specialties that pertain to particular organ systems and their respective disease states, as well as allied health specialties. Enumerated type.

variants.name: MedicalStudy
variants.definition: A medical study is an umbrella type covering all kinds of research studies relating to human medicine or health, including observational studies and interventional trials and registries, randomized, controlled or not. When the specific type of study is known, use one of the extensions of this type, such as MedicalTrial or MedicalObservationalStudy. Also, note that this type should be used to mark up data that describes the study itself; to tag an article that publishes the results of a study, use MedicalScholarlyArticle. Note: use the code property of MedicalEntity to store study IDs, e.g. clinicaltrials.gov ID.

variants.name: MedicalStudyStatus
variants.definition: The status of a medical study. Enumerated type.

variants.name: MedicalSymptom
variants.definition: Any indication of the existence of a medical condition or disease that is apparent to the patient.

variants.name: MedicalTest
variants.definition: Any medical test, typically performed for diagnostic purposes.

variants.name: MedicalTestPanel
variants.definition: Any collection of tests commonly ordered together.

variants.name: MedicalTherapy
variants.definition: Any medical intervention designed to prevent, treat, and cure human diseases and medical conditions, including both curative and palliative therapies. Medical therapies are typically processes of care relying upon pharmacotherapy, behavioral therapy, supportive therapy (with fluid or nutrition for example), or detoxification (e.g. hemodialysis) aimed at improving or preventing a health condition.

variants.name: MedicalTrial
variants.definition: A medical trial is a type of medical study that uses scientific process used to compare the safety and efficacy of medical therapies or medical procedures. In general, medical trials are controlled and subjects are allocated at random to the different treatment and/or control groups.

variants.name: MedicalTrialDesign
variants.definition: Design models for medical trials. Enumerated type.

variants.name: medicineSystem
variants.definition: The system of medicine that includes this MedicalEntity, for example 'evidence-based', 'homeopathic', 'chiropractic', etc.

variants.name: MedicineSystem
variants.definition: Systems of medical practice.

variants.name: member
variants.definition: A member of this organization.

variants.name: memoryRequirements
variants.definition: Minimum memory requirements.

variants.name: Midwifery
variants.definition: Midwifery.

variants.name: MobileApplication
variants.definition: A mobile software application.

variants.name: MRI
variants.definition: Magnetic resonance imaging.

variants.name: MulticellularParasite
variants.definition: Multicellular parasite that causes an infection.

variants.name: MultiCenterTrial
variants.definition: A trial that takes place at multiple centers.

variants.name: Muscle
variants.definition: A muscle is an anatomical structure consisting of a contractile form of tissue that animals use to effect movement.

variants.name: Musculoskeletal
variants.definition: A specific branch of medical science that pertains to diagnosis and treatment of disorders of muscles, ligaments and skeletal system.

variants.name: MusculoskeletalExam
variants.definition: Musculoskeletal

variants.name: naturalProgression
variants.definition: The expected progression of the condition if it is not treated and allowed to progress naturally.

variants.name: Neck
variants.definition: Neck

variants.name: nerve
variants.definition: The underlying innervation associated with the muscle.

variants.name: Nerve
variants.definition: A common pathway for the electrochemical nerve impulses that are transmitted along each of the axons.

variants.name: nerveMotor
variants.definition: The neurological pathway extension that involves muscle control.

variants.name: Neuro
variants.definition: Neuro

variants.name: Neurologic
variants.definition: A specific branch of medical science that studies the nerves and nervous system and its respective disease states.

variants.name: NoninvasiveProcedure
variants.definition: A type of medical procedure that involves noninvasive techniques.

variants.name: nonProprietaryName
variants.definition: The generic name of this drug or supplement.

variants.name: normalRange
variants.definition: Range of acceptable values for a typical patient, when applicable.

variants.name: Nose
variants.definition: Nose

variants.name: NotYetRecruiting
variants.definition: Not yet recruiting.

variants.name: Nursing
variants.definition: Nursing.

variants.name: Observational
variants.definition: An observational study design.

variants.name: Obstetric
variants.definition: A specific branch of medical science that specializes in the care of women during the prenatal and postnatal care and with the delivery of the child.

variants.name: OccupationalActivity
variants.definition: Any physical activity engaged in for job-related purposes. Examples may include waiting tables, maid service, carrying a mailbag, picking fruits or vegetables, construction work, etc.

variants.name: OccupationalTherapy
variants.definition: Occupational therapy.

variants.name: Oncologic
variants.definition: A specific branch of medical science that deals with benign and malignant tumors, including the study of their development, diagnosis, treatment and prevention.

variants.name: OpenTrial
variants.definition: A trial design in which the researcher knows the full details of the treatment, and so does the patient.

variants.name: operatingSystem
variants.definition: Operating systems supported (Windows 7, OSX 10.6, Android 1.6).

variants.name: Optometic
variants.definition: Optometry.

variants.name: origin
variants.definition: The place or point where a muscle arises.

variants.name: originatesFrom
variants.definition: The vasculature the lymphatic structure originates, or afferents, from.

variants.name: Osteopathic
variants.definition: A system of medicine focused on promoting the body's innate ability to heal itself.

variants.name: OTC
variants.definition: Available over the counter.

variants.name: Otolaryngologic
variants.definition: A specific branch of medical science that is concerned with the ear, nose and throat and their respective disease states.

variants.name: outcome
variants.definition: Expected or actual outcomes of the study.

variants.name: overdosage
variants.definition: Any information related to overdose on a drug, including signs or symptoms, treatments, contact information for emergency response.

variants.name: overview
variants.definition: Descriptive information establishing the overarching theory/philosophy of the plan. May include the rationale for the name, the population where the plan first came to prominence, etc.

variants.name: PalliativeProcedure
variants.definition: A medical procedure intended primarly for palliative purposes, aimed at relieving the symptoms of an underlying health condition.

variants.name: parent
variants.definition: A parent of this person.

variants.name: partOfSystem
variants.definition: The anatomical or organ system that this structure is part of.

variants.name: Pathology
variants.definition: A specific branch of medical science that is concerned with the study of the cause, origin and nature of a disease state, including its consequences as a result of manifestation of the disease. In clinical care, the term is used to designate a branch of medicine using laboratory tests to diagnose and determine the prognostic significance of illness.

variants.name: PathologyTest
variants.definition: A medical test performed by a laboratory that typically involves examination of a tissue sample by a pathologist.

variants.name: pathophysiology
variants.definition: Changes in the normal mechanical, physical, and biochemical functions that are associated with this activity or condition.

variants.name: Pediatric
variants.definition: A specific branch of medical science that specializes in the care of infants, children and adolescents.

variants.name: PercutaneousProcedure
variants.definition: A type of medical procedure that involves percutaneous techniques, where access to organs or tissue is achieved via needle-puncture of the skin. For example, catheter-based procedures like stent delivery.

variants.name: performer
variants.definition: A performer at the event—for example, a presenter, musician, musical group or actor.

variants.name: permissions
variants.definition: Permission(s) required to run the app (for example, a mobile app may require full internet access or may run only on wifi).

variants.name: PET
variants.definition: Positron emission tomography imaging.

variants.name: PharmacySpecialty
variants.definition: Pharmacy.

variants.name: phase
variants.definition: The phase of the trial.

variants.name: photo
variants.definition: A photograph of this place.

variants.name: PhysicalActivity
variants.definition: Any bodily activity that enhances or maintains physical fitness and overall health and wellness. Includes activity that is part of daily living and routine, structured exercise, and exercise prescribed as part of a medical treatment or recovery plan.

variants.name: PhysicalActivityCategory
variants.definition: Categories of physical activity, organized by physiologic classification.

variants.name: PhysicalExam
variants.definition: A type of physical examination of a patient performed by a physician. Enumerated type.

variants.name: PhysicalTherapy
variants.definition: A process of progressive physical care and rehabilitation aimed at improving a health condition.

variants.name: physiologicalBenefits
variants.definition: Specific physiologic benefits associated to the plan.

variants.name: Physiotherapy
variants.definition: Physiotherapy.

variants.name: PlaceboControlledTrial
variants.definition: A placebo-controlled trial design.

variants.name: PlasticSurgery
variants.definition: A specific branch of medical science that pertains to therapeutic or cosmetic repair or re-formation of missing, injured or malformed tissues or body parts by manual and instrumental means.

variants.name: Podiatric
variants.definition: Podiatry.

variants.name: population
variants.definition: Any characteristics of the population used in the study, e.g. 'males under 65'.

variants.name: possibleComplication
variants.definition: A possible unexpected and unfavorable evolution of a medical condition. Complications may include worsening of the signs or symptoms of the disease, extension of the condition to other organ systems, etc.

variants.name: possibleTreatment
variants.definition: A possible treatment to address this condition, sign or symptom.

variants.name: postOp
variants.definition: A description of the postoperative procedures, care, and/or followups for this device.

variants.name: pregnancyCategory
variants.definition: Pregnancy category of this drug.

variants.name: pregnancyWarning
variants.definition: Any precaution, guidance, contraindication, etc. related to this drug's use during pregnancy.

variants.name: preOp
variants.definition: A description of the workup, testing, and other preparations required before implanting this device.

variants.name: preparation
variants.definition: Typical preparation that a patient must undergo before having the procedure performed.

variants.name: prescribingInfo
variants.definition: Link to prescribing information for the drug.

variants.name: PrescriptionOnly
variants.definition: Available by prescription only.

variants.name: prescriptionStatus
variants.definition: Indicates whether this drug is available by prescription or over-the-counter.

variants.name: PreventionIndication
variants.definition: An indication for preventing an underlying condition, symptom, etc.

variants.name: PrimaryCare
variants.definition: Primary care.

variants.name: primaryPrevention
variants.definition: A preventative therapy used to prevent an initial occurrence of the medical condition, such as vaccination.

variants.name: Prion
variants.definition: A prion is an infectious agent composed of protein in a misfolded form.

variants.name: procedure
variants.definition: A description of the procedure involved in setting up, using, and/or installing the device.

variants.name: procedureType
variants.definition: The type of procedure, for example Surgical, Noninvasive, or Percutaneous.

variants.name: processorRequirements
variants.definition: Processor architecture required to run the application (e.g. IA64).

variants.name: proprietaryName
variants.definition: Proprietary name given to the diet plan, typically by its originator or creator.

variants.name: Protozoa
variants.definition: Single-celled organism that causes an infection.

variants.name: Psychiatric
variants.definition: A specific branch of medical science that is concerned with the study, treatment, and prevention of mental illness, using both medical and psychological therapies.

variants.name: PsychologicalTreatment
variants.definition: A process of care relying upon counseling, dialogue, communication, verbalization aimed at improving a mental health condition.

variants.name: publicationType
variants.definition: The type of the medical article, taken from the US NLM MeSH <a href=http://www.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/pubtypes.html>publication type catalog.

variants.name: SuperficialAnatomy
variants.definition: Anatomical features that can be observed by sight (without dissection), including the form and proportions of the human body as well as surface landmarks that correspond to deeper subcutaneous structures. Superficial anatomy plays an important role in sports medicine, phlebotomy, and other medical specialties as underlying anatomical structures can be identified through surface palpation. For example, during back surgery, superficial anatomy can be used to palpate and count vertebrae to find the site of incision. Or in phlebotomy, superficial anatomy can be used to locate an underlying vein; for example, the median cubital vein can be located by palpating the borders of the cubital fossa (such as the epicondyles of the humerus) and then looking for the superficial signs of the vein, such as size, prominence, ability to refill after depression, and feel of surrounding tissue support. As another example, in a subluxation (dislocation) of the glenohumeral joint, the bony structure becomes pronounced with the deltoid muscle failing to cover the glenohumeral joint allowing the edges of the scapula to be superficially visible. Here, the superficial anatomy is the visible edges of the scapula, implying the underlying dislocation of the joint (the related anatomical structure).

variants.definition: The range of temporal applicability of a dataset, e.g. for a 2011 census dataset, the year 2011 (in ISO 8601 time interval format).

variants.name: yearlyRevenue
variants.definition: The size of the business in annual revenue.

variants.name: yearsInOperation
variants.definition: The age of the business.

variants.name: AcceptAction
variants.definition:
The act of committing to/adopting an object.

Related actions:

  • RejectAction: The antagonym of AcceptAction.

variants.name: AchieveAction
variants.definition: The act of accomplishing something via     previous efforts. It is an instantaneous action rather than an ongoing     process.

variants.name: Action
variants.definition: An action performed by a direct agent and indirect     participants upon a direct object. Optionally happens at a location     with the help of an inanimate instrument. The execution of the action     may produce a result. Specific action sub-type documentation specifies     the exact expectation of each argument/role.

variants.name: AddAction
variants.definition: The act of editing by adding an object to a collection.

variants.name: agent
variants.definition: The direct performer or driver of the action (animate or inanimate). e.g. *John* wrote a book.

variants.name: AgreeAction
variants.definition: The act of expressing a consistency of opinion with the object. An agent agrees to/about an object (a proposition, topic or theme) with participants.

variants.name: AllocateAction
variants.definition: The act of organizing tasks/objects/events by associating resources to it.

variants.name: AppendAction
variants.definition: The act of inserting at the end if an ordered collection.

variants.name: ApplyAction
variants.definition:
The act of registering to an organization/service without the guarantee to receive it. NOTE(goto): should this be under InteractAction instead?

Related actions:

  • RegisterAction: Unlike RegisterAction, ApplyAction has no guarantees that the application will be accepted.

variants.name: ArriveAction
variants.definition: The act of arriving at a place. An agent arrives at a destination from an fromLocation, optionally with participants.

variants.name: AskAction
variants.definition:
The act of posing a question / favor to someone.

Related actions:

  • ReplyAction: Appears generally as a response to AskAction.

variants.name: AssessAction
variants.definition: The act of forming one's opinion, reaction or sentiment.

variants.name: AssignAction
variants.definition: The act of allocating an action/event/task to some destination (someone or something).

variants.name: audience
variants.definition: The intended audience of the item, i.e. the group for whom the item was created.

variants.name: AuthorizeAction
variants.definition: The act of granting permission to an object.

variants.name: BefriendAction
variants.definition:
The act of forming a personal connection with someone (object) mutually/bidirectionally/symmetrically.

Related actions:

  • FollowAction: Unlike FollowAction, BefriendAction implies that the connection is reciprocal.

variants.name: BookmarkAction
variants.definition: An agent bookmarks/flags/labels/tags/marks an object.

variants.name: BorrowAction
variants.definition:
The act of obtaining an object under an agreement to return it at a later date. Reciprocal of LendAction.

Related actions:

  • LendAction: Reciprocal of BorrowAction.

variants.name: borrower
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The person that borrows the object being lent.

variants.name: BuyAction
variants.definition: The act of giving money to a seller in exchange for goods or services rendered. An agent buys an object, product, or service from a seller for a price. Reciprocal of SellAction.

variants.name: buyer
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The participant/person/organization that bought the object.

variants.name: CancelAction
variants.definition:
The act of asserting that a future event/action is no longer going to happen.

Related actions:

  • ConfirmAction: The antagonym of CancelAction.

variants.name: candidate
variants.definition: A sub property of object. The candidate subject of this action.

variants.name: CheckAction
variants.definition: An agent inspects/determines/investigates/inquire or examine an object's accuracy/quality/condition or state.

variants.name: CheckInAction
variants.definition:
The act of an agent communicating (service provider, social media, etc) their arrival by registering/confirming for a previously reserved service (e.g. flight check in) or at a place (e.g. hotel), possibly resulting in a result (boarding pass, etc).

Related actions:

  • CheckOutAction: The antagonym of CheckInAction.
  • ArriveAction: Unlike ArriveAction, CheckInAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the start of a previously reserved service.
  • ConfirmAction: Unlike ConfirmAction, CheckInAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the *start* of a previously reserved service rather than its validity/existance.

variants.name: CheckOutAction
variants.definition:
The act of an agent communicating (service provider, social media, etc) their departure of a previously reserved service (e.g. flight check in) or place (e.g. hotel).

Related actions:

  • CheckInAction: The antagonym of CheckOutAction.
  • DepartAction: Unlike DepartAction, CheckOutAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the end of a previously reserved service.
  • CancelAction: Unlike CancelAction, CheckOutAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the end of a previously reserved service.

variants.name: ChooseAction
variants.definition: The act of expressing a preference from a set of options or a large or unbounded set of choices/options.

variants.name: collection
variants.definition: A sub property of object. The collection target of the action.

variants.name: CommentAction
variants.definition: The act of generating a comment about a subject.

variants.name: CommunicateAction
variants.definition: The act of conveying information to another person via a communication medium (instrument) such as speech, email, or telephone conversation.

variants.name: ConfirmAction
variants.definition:
The act of notifying someone that a future event/action is going to happen as expected.

Related actions:

  • CancelAction: The antagonym of ConfirmAction.

variants.name: ConsumeAction
variants.definition: The act of ingesting information/resources/food.

variants.name: CookAction
variants.definition: The act of producing/preparing food.

variants.name: course
variants.definition: A sub property of location. The course where this action was taken.

variants.name: CreateAction
variants.definition: The act of deliberately creating/producing/generating/building a result out of the agent.

variants.name: DeleteAction
variants.definition: The act of editing a recipient by removing one of its objects.

variants.name: deliveryMethod
variants.definition: A sub property of instrument. The method of delivery

variants.name: DepartAction
variants.definition: The act of  departing from a place. An agent departs from an fromLocation for a destination, optionally with participants.

variants.name: diet
variants.definition: A sub property of instrument. The died used in this action.

variants.name: DisagreeAction
variants.definition: The act of expressing a difference of opinion with the object. An agent disagrees to/about an object (a proposition, topic or theme) with participants.

variants.name: DiscoverAction
variants.definition: The act of discovering/finding an object.

variants.name: DislikeAction
variants.definition: The act of expressing a negative sentiment about the object. An agent dislikes an object (a proposition, topic or theme) with participants.

variants.name: distance
variants.definition: A sub property of asset. The distance travelled.

variants.name: DonateAction
variants.definition: The act of providing goods, services, or money without compensation, often for philanthropic reasons.

variants.name: DownloadAction
variants.definition: The act of downloading an object.

variants.name: DrawAction
variants.definition: The act of producing a visual/graphical representation of an object, typically with a pen/pencil and paper as instruments.

variants.name: DrinkAction
variants.definition: The act of swallowing liquids.

variants.name: EatAction
variants.definition: The act of swallowing solid objects.

variants.name: EndorseAction
variants.definition: An agent approves/certifies/likes/supports/sanction an object.

variants.name: endorsee
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The person/organization being supported.

variants.name: endTime
variants.definition: When the Action was performed: end time. This is for actions that span a period of time. e.g. John wrote a book from January to *December*.

variants.name: entertainmentBusiness
variants.definition: A sub property of location. The entertainment business where the action occurred.

variants.name: ExerciseAction
variants.definition: The act of participating in exertive activity for the purposes of improving health and fitness

variants.name: exercisePlan
variants.definition: A sub property of instrument. The exercise plan used on this action.

variants.name: exerciseType
variants.definition: Type(s) of exercise or activity, such as strength training, flexibility training, aerobics, cardiac rehabilitation, etc.

variants.name: FilmAction
variants.definition: The act of capturing sound and moving images on film, video, or digitally.

variants.name: FindAction
variants.definition:
The act of finding an object.

Related actions:

  • SearchAction: FindAction is generally lead by a SearchAction, but not necessarily.

variants.name: FollowAction
variants.definition:
The act of forming a personal connection with someone/something (object) unidirectionally/asymmetrically to get updates polled from.

Related actions:

  • BefriendAction: Unlike BefriendAction, FollowAction implies that the connection is *not* necessarily reciprocal.
  • SubscribeAction: Unlike SubscribeAction, FollowAction implies that the follower acts as an active agent constantly/actively polling for updates.
  • RegisterAction: Unlike RegisterAction, FollowAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object.
  • JoinAction: Unlike JoinAction, FollowAction implies that the agent is interested in getting updates from the object.
  • TrackAction: Unlike TrackAction, FollowAction refers to the polling of updates of all aspects of animate objects rather than the location of inanimate objects (e.g. you track a package, but you don't follow it).

variants.name: followee
variants.definition: A sub property of object. The person or organization being followed.

variants.name: foodEstablishment
variants.definition: A sub property of location. The specific food establishment where the action occurreed.

variants.name: foodEvent
variants.definition: A sub property of location. The specific food event where the action occurred.

variants.name: fromLocation
variants.definition: A sub property of location. The original location of the object or the agent before the action.

variants.name: GiveAction
variants.definition:
The act of transferring ownership of an object to a destination. Reciprocal of TakeAction.

Related actions:

  • TakeAction: Reciprocal of GiveAction.
  • SendAction: Unlike SendAction, GiveAction implies that ownership is being transferred (e.g. I may send my laptop to you, but that doesn't mean I'm giving it to you).

variants.name: IgnoreAction
variants.definition: The act of intentionally disregarding the object. An agent ignores an object.

variants.name: InformAction
variants.definition: The act of notifying someone of information pertinent to them, with no expectation of a response.

variants.name: InsertAction
variants.definition: The act of adding at a specific location in an ordered collection.

variants.name: InstallAction
variants.definition: The act of installing an application.

variants.name: instrument
variants.definition: The object that helped the agent perform the action. e.g. John wrote a book with *a pen*.

variants.name: InteractAction
variants.definition: The act of interacting with another person or organization.

variants.name: InviteAction
variants.definition: The act of asking someone to attend an event. Reciprocal of RsvpAction.

variants.name: JoinAction
variants.definition:
An agent joins an event/group with participants/friends at a location.

Related actions:

  • RegisterAction: Unlike RegisterAction, JoinAction refers to joining a group/team of people.
  • SubscribeAction: Unlike SubscribeAction, JoinAction does not imply that you'll be receiving updates.
  • FollowAction: Unlike FollowAction, JoinAction does not imply that you'll be polling for updates.

variants.name: landlord
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The owner of the real estate property. Sub property of destination or participant?

variants.name: language
variants.definition: A sub property of instrument. The languaged used on this action.

variants.name: LeaveAction
variants.definition:
An agent leaves an event / group with participants/friends at a location.

Related actions:

  • JoinAction: The antagonym of LeaveAction.
  • UnRegisterAction: Unlike UnRegisterAction, LeaveAction implies leaving a group/team of people rather than a service.

variants.name: LendAction
variants.definition:
The act of providing an object under an agreement that it will be returned at a later date. Reciprocal of BorrowAction.

Related actions:

  • BorrowAction: Reciprocal of LendAction.

variants.name: lender
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The person that lends the object being borrowed.

variants.name: LikeAction
variants.definition: The act of expressing a positive sentiment about the object. An agent likes an object (a proposition, topic or theme) with participants.

variants.name: ListenAction
variants.definition: The act of consuming audio content.

variants.name: LoseAction
variants.definition: The act of being defeated in a competitive activity.

variants.name: loser
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The loser of the action.

variants.name: MarryAction
variants.definition: The act of marrying a person.

variants.name: MoveAction
variants.definition:
The act of an agent relocating to a place.

Related actions:

  • TransferAction: Unlike TransferAction, the subject of the move is a living Person or Organization rather than an inanimate object.

variants.name: object
variants.definition: The object upon the action is carried out, whose state is kept intact or changed. Also known as the semantic roles patient, affected or undergoer (which change their state) or theme (which doesn't). e.g. John read *a book*.

variants.name: oponent
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The oponent on this action.

variants.name: option
variants.definition: A sub property of object. The options subject to this action.

variants.name: OrderAction
variants.definition: An agent orders an object/product/service to be delivered/sent.

variants.name: OrganizeAction
variants.definition: The act of manipulating/administering/supervising/controlling one or more objects.

variants.name: PaintAction
variants.definition: The act of producing a painting, typically with paint and canvas as instruments.

variants.name: participant
variants.definition: Other co-agents that participated in the action indirectly. e.g. John wrote a book with *Steve*.

variants.name: PayAction
variants.definition: An agent pays a price to a participant.

variants.name: PerformAction
variants.definition: The act of participating in performance arts.

variants.name: PhotographAction
variants.definition: The act of capturing still images of objects using a camera.

variants.name: PlanAction
variants.definition: The act of planning the execution of an event/task/action/reservation/plan to a future date.

variants.name: PlayAction
variants.definition:
The act of playing/exercising/training/performing for enjoyment, leisure, recreation, competion or exercise.

Related actions:

  • ListenAction: Unlike ListenAction (which is under ConsumeAction), PlayAction refers to performing for an audience or at an event, rather than consuming music.
  • WatchAction: Unlike WatchAction (which is under ConsumeAction), PlayAction refers to showing/displaying for an audience or at an event, rather than consuming visual content.

variants.name: PrependAction
variants.definition: The act of inserting at the beginning if an ordered collection.

variants.name: purpose
variants.definition: A goal towards an action is taken. Can be concrete or abstract.

variants.name: query
variants.definition: A sub property of instrument. The query used on this action.

variants.name: question
variants.definition: A sub property of object. A question.

variants.name: QuoteAction
variants.definition: An agent quotes/estimates/appraises an object/product/service with a price at a location/store.

variants.name: ReactAction
variants.definition: The act of responding instinctively and emotionally to an object, expressing a sentiment.

variants.name: ReadAction
variants.definition: The act of consuming written content.

variants.name: realEstateAgent
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The real estate agent involved in the action.

variants.name: ReceiveAction
variants.definition:
The act of physically/electronically taking delivery of an object thathas been transferred from an origin to a destination. Reciprocal of SendAction.

Related actions:

  • SendAction: The reciprocal of ReceiveAction.
  • TakeAction: Unlike TakeAction, ReceiveAction does not imply that the ownership has been transfered (e.g. I can receive a package, but it does not mean the package is now mine).

variants.name: recipe
variants.definition: A sub property of instrument. The recipe/instructions used to perform the action.

variants.name: recipient
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The participant who is at the receiving end of the action.

variants.name: RegisterAction
variants.definition:
The act of registering to be a user of a service, product or web page.

Related actions:

  • JoinAction: Unlike JoinAction, RegisterAction implies you are registering to be a user of a service, *not* a group/team of people.
  • FollowAction: Unlike FollowAction, RegisterAction doesn't imply that the agent is expecting to poll for updates from the object.
  • SubscribeAction: Unlike SubscribeAction, RegisterAction doesn't imply that the agent is expecting updates from the object.

variants.name: RejectAction
variants.definition:
The act of rejecting to/adopting an object.

Related actions:

  • AcceptAction: The antagonym of RejectAction.

variants.name: RentAction
variants.definition: The act of giving money in return for temporary use, but not ownership, of an object such as a vehicle or property. For example, an agent rents a property from a landlord in exchange for a periodic payment.

variants.name: ReplaceAction
variants.definition: The act of editing a recipient by replacing an old object with a new object.

variants.name: replacee
variants.definition: A sub property of object. The object that is being replaced.

variants.name: replacer
variants.definition: A sub property of object. The object that replaces.

variants.name: ReplyAction
variants.definition:
The act of responding to a question/message asked/sent by the object. Related to AskAction.

Related actions:

  • AskAction: Appears generally as an origin of a ReplyAction.

variants.name: ReserveAction
variants.definition:
Reserving a concrete object.

Related actions:

  • ScheduleAction: Unlike ScheduleAction, ReserveAction reserves concrete objects (e.g. a table, a hotel) towards a time slot / spatial allocation.

variants.name: result
variants.definition: The result produced in the action. e.g. John wrote *a book*.

variants.name: resultReview
variants.definition: A sub property of result. The review that resulted in the performing of the action.

variants.name: ReturnAction
variants.definition: The act of returning to the origin that which was previously received (concrete objects) or taken (ownership).

variants.name: ReviewAction
variants.definition: The act of producing a balanced opinion about the object for an audience. An agent reviews an object with participants resulting in a review.

variants.name: RsvpAction
variants.definition: The act of notifying an event organiser as to whether you expect to attend the event.

variants.name: sameAs
variants.definition: URL of a reference Web page that unambiguously indicates the item's identity. E.g. the URL of the item's Wikipedia page, Freebase page, or official website.

variants.name: ScheduleAction
variants.definition:
Scheduling future actions, events, or tasks.

Related actions:

  • ReserveAction: Unlike ReserveAction, ScheduleAction allocates future actions (e.g. an event, a task, etc) towards a time slot / spatial allocation.

variants.name: scheduledTime
variants.definition: The time the object is scheduled to.

variants.name: SearchAction
variants.definition:
The act of searching for an object.

Related actions:

  • FindAction: SearchAction generally leads to a FindAction, but not necessarily.

variants.name: SellAction
variants.definition: The act of taking money from a buyer in exchange for goods or services rendered. An agent sells an object, product, or service to a buyer for a price. Reciprocal of BuyAction.

variants.name: SendAction
variants.definition:
The act of physically/electronically dispatching an object for transfer from an origin to a destination.

Related actions:

  • ReceiveAction: The reciprocal of SendAction.
  • GiveAction: Unlike GiveAction, SendAction does not imply the transfer of ownership (e.g. I can send you my laptop, but I'm not necessarily giving it to you).

variants.name: sender
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The participant who is at the sending end of the action.

variants.name: ShareAction
variants.definition: The act of distributing content to people for their amusement or edification.

variants.name: sportsActivityLocation
variants.definition: A sub property of location. The sports activity location where this action occurred.

variants.name: sportsEvent
variants.definition: A sub property of location. The sports event where this action occurred.

variants.name: sportsTeam
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The sports team that participated on this action.

variants.name: startTime
variants.definition: When the Action was performed: start time. This is for actions that span a period of time. e.g. John wrote a book from *January* to December.

variants.name: SubscribeAction
variants.definition:
The act of forming a personal connection with someone/something (object) unidirectionally/asymmetrically to get updates pushed to.

Related actions:

  • FollowAction: Unlike FollowAction, SubscribeAction implies that the subscriber acts as a passive agent being constantly/actively pushed for updates.
  • RegisterAction: Unlike RegisterAction, SubscribeAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object.
  • JoinAction: Unlike JoinAction, SubscribeAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object.

variants.name: TakeAction
variants.definition:
The act of gaining ownership of an object from an origin. Reciprocal of GiveAction.

Related actions:

  • GiveAction: The reciprocal of TakeAction.
  • ReceiveAction: Unlike ReceiveAction, TakeAction implies that ownership has been transfered.

variants.name: TieAction
variants.definition: The act of reaching a draw in a competitive activity.

variants.name: TipAction
variants.definition: The act of giving money voluntarily to a beneficiary in recognition of services rendered.

variants.name: toLocation
variants.definition: A sub property of location. The final location of the object or the agent after the action.

variants.name: TrackAction
variants.definition:
An agent tracks an object for updates.

Related actions:

  • FollowAction: Unlike FollowAction, TrackAction refers to the interest on the location of innanimates objects.
  • SubscribeAction: Unlike SubscribeAction, TrackAction refers to the interest on the location of innanimate objects.

variants.name: TradeAction
variants.definition: The act of participating in an exchange of goods and services for monetary compensation. An agent trades an object, product or service with a participant in exchange for a one time or periodic payment.

variants.name: TransferAction
variants.definition: The act of transferring/moving (abstract or concrete) animate or inanimate objects from one place to another.

variants.name: TravelAction
variants.definition: The act of traveling from an fromLocation to a destination by a specified mode of transport, optionally with participants.

variants.name: UnRegisterAction
variants.definition:
The act of un-registering from a service.

Related actions:

  • RegisterAction: Antagonym of UnRegisterAction.
  • Leave: Unlike LeaveAction, UnRegisterAction implies that you are unregistering from a service you werer previously registered, rather than leaving a team/group of people.

variants.name: UpdateAction
variants.definition: The act of managing by changing/editing the state of the object.

variants.name: UseAction
variants.definition: The act of applying an object to its intended purpose.

variants.name: vendor
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The seller.The participant/person/organization that sold the object.

variants.name: ViewAction
variants.definition: The act of consuming static visual content.

variants.name: VoteAction
variants.definition: The act of expressing a preference from a fixed/finite/structured set of choices/options.

variants.name: WantAction
variants.definition: The act of expressing a desire about the object. An agent wants an object.

variants.name: warrantyPromise
variants.definition: The warranty promise(s) included in the offer.

variants.name: WatchAction
variants.definition: The act of consuming dynamic/moving visual content.

variants.name: WearAction
variants.definition: The act of dressing oneself in clothing.

variants.name: WinAction
variants.definition: The act of achieving victory in a competitive activity.

variants.name: winner
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The winner of the action.

variants.name: WriteAction
variants.definition: The act of authoring written creative content.

variants.name: acceptedOffer
variants.definition: The offer(s) -- e.g., product, quantity and price combinations -- included in the order.

variants.name: accessCode
variants.definition: Password, PIN, or access code needed for delivery (e.g. from a locker).

variants.name: accessibilityAPI
variants.definition: Indicates that the resource is compatible with the referenced accessibility API (WebSchemas wiki lists possible values).

variants.name: accessibilityControl
variants.definition: Identifies input methods that are sufficient to fully control the described resource (WebSchemas wiki lists possible values).

variants.name: accessibilityFeature
variants.definition: Content features of the resource, such as accessible media, alternatives and supported enhancements for accessibility (WebSchemas wiki lists possible values).

variants.name: accessibilityHazard
variants.definition: A characteristic of the described resource that is physiologically dangerous to some users. Related to WCAG 2.0 guideline 2.3. (WebSchemas wiki lists possible values)

variants.name: accountablePerson
variants.definition: Specifies the Person that is legally accountable for the CreativeWork.

variants.name: additionalName
variants.definition: An additional name for a Person, can be used for a middle name.

variants.name: alternativeHeadline
variants.definition: A secondary title of the CreativeWork.

variants.name: area
variants.definition: The area within which users can expect to reach the broadcast service.

variants.name: areaServed
variants.definition: The location served by this contact point (e.g., a phone number intended for Europeans vs. North Americans or only within the United States.)

variants.name: aspect
variants.definition: An aspect of medical practice that is considered on the page, such as 'diagnosis', 'treatment', 'causes', 'prognosis', 'etiology', 'epidemiology', etc.

variants.name: associatedArticle
variants.definition: A NewsArticle associated with the Media Object.

variants.name: associatedMedia
variants.definition: The media objects that encode this creative work. This property is a synonym for encodings.

variants.name: availableChannel
variants.definition: A means of accessing the service (e.g. a phone bank, a web site, a location, etc.)

variants.name: availableFrom
variants.definition: When the item is available for pickup from the store, locker, etc.

variants.name: availableLanguage
variants.definition: A language someone may use with the item.

variants.name: availableService
variants.definition: A medical service available from this provider.

variants.name: availableTest
variants.definition: A diagnostic test or procedure offered by this lab.

variants.name: availableThrough
variants.definition: After this date, the item will no longer be available for pickup.

variants.name: billingAddress
variants.definition: The billing address for the order.

variants.name: box
variants.definition: A polygon is the area enclosed by a point-to-point path for which the starting and ending points are the same. A polygon is expressed as a series of four or more spacedelimited points where the first and final points are identical.

variants.name: Brand
variants.definition: A brand is a name used by an organization or business person for labeling a product, product group, or similar.

variants.name: broadcaster
variants.definition: The organization owning or operating the broadcast service.

variants.name: BroadcastEvent
variants.definition: An over the air or online broadcast event.

variants.name: BroadcastService
variants.definition: A delivery service through which content is provided via broadcast over the air or online.

variants.name: BusinessEntityType
variants.definition:
A business entity type is a conceptual entity representing the legal form, the size, the main line of business, the position in the value chain, or any combination thereof, of an organization or business person.

    Commonly used values:

    http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Business
    http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Enduser
    http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PublicInstitution
    http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Reseller

variants.name: BusinessFunction
variants.definition:
The business function specifies the type of activity or access (i.e., the bundle of rights) offered by the organization or business person through the offer. Typical are sell, rental or lease, maintenance or repair, manufacture / produce, recycle / dispose, engineering / construction, or installation. Proprietary specifications of access rights are also instances of this class.

    Commonly used values:

    http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ConstructionInstallation
    http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Dispose
    http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#LeaseOut
    http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Maintain
    http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ProvideService
    http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Repair
    http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Sell
    http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Buy

variants.name: carrier
variants.definition: The party responsible for the parcel delivery.

variants.name: circle

variants.name: openingHours
variants.definition:
The opening hours for a business. Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.
- Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: Mo, Tu, We, Th, Fr, Sa, Su.
- Times are specified using 24:00 time. For example, 3pm is specified as 15:00.
- Here is an example: <time itemprop="openingHours" datetime="Tu,Th 16:00-20:00">Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm</time>.
- If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <time itemprop="openingHours" datetime="Mo-Su">Monday through Sunday, all day</time>.

variants.name: CheckInAction
variants.definition:
The act of an agent communicating (service provider, social media, etc) their arrival by registering/confirming for a previously reserved service (e.g. flight check in) or at a place (e.g. hotel), possibly resulting in a result (boarding pass, etc).

Related actions:

  • CheckOutAction: The antagonym of CheckInAction.
  • ArriveAction: Unlike ArriveAction, CheckInAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the start of a previously reserved service.
  • ConfirmAction: Unlike ConfirmAction, CheckInAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the *start* of a previously reserved service rather than its validity/existence.

Delivery methods are characterized by the means of transportation used, and by the organization or group that is the contracting party for the sending organization or person.

    Commonly used values:

    http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeDirectDownload
    http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeFreight
    http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeMail
    http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeOwnFleet
