variants.definition: Enumerated categories of medical drug costs.

variants.name: DrugPregnancyCategory
variants.definition: Categories that represent an assessment of the risk of fetal injury due to a drug or pharmaceutical used as directed by the mother during pregnancy.

variants.name: DrugPrescriptionStatus
variants.definition: Indicates whether this drug is available by prescription or over-the-counter.

variants.name: encodingType
variants.definition: The supported encoding type(s) for an EntryPoint request.

variants.name: endDate
variants.definition: The end date and time of the role, event or item (in ISO 8601 date format).

variants.name: endTime
variants.definition:
The endTime of something. For a reserved event or service (e.g. FoodEstablishmentReservation), the time that it is expected to end. For actions that span a period of time, when the action was performed. e.g. John wrote a book from January to *December*.

Note that Event uses startDate/endDate instead of startTime/endTime, even when describing dates with times. This situation may be clarified in future revisions.

variants.name: Energy
variants.definition: Properties that take Energy as values are of the form '<Number> <Energy unit of measure>'

variants.name: EntryPoint
variants.definition: An entry point, within some Web-based protocol.

variants.name: False
variants.definition: The boolean value false

variants.name: flightNumber
variants.definition: The unique identifier for a flight, not including the airline IATA code. For example, if describing United flight 110, the flightNumber is '110'. The IATA code can be set on the Airline.

variants.name: foodEstablishment
variants.definition: A sub property of location. The specific food establishment where the action occurred.

variants.name: httpMethod
variants.definition: An HTTP method that specifies the appropriate HTTP method for a request to an HTTP EntryPoint. Values are capitalized strings as used in HTTP.

variants.name: icaoCode
variants.definition: IACO identifier for an airport.

variants.name: InfectiousAgentClass
variants.definition: Classes of agents or pathogens that transmit infectious diseases. Enumerated type.

variants.name: InStock
variants.definition: Indicates that the item is in stock.

variants.name: InStoreOnly
variants.definition: Indicates that the item is available only at physical locations.

variants.name: inverseOf
variants.definition: Relates a property to a property that is its inverse. Inverse properties relate the same pairs of items to each other, but in reversed direction. For example, the 'alumni' and 'alumniOf' properties are inverseOf each other. Some properties don't have explicit inverses; in these situations RDFa and JSON-LD syntax for reverse properties can be used.

variants.name: ItemAvailability
variants.definition: A list of possible product availability options.

variants.name: itemOffered
variants.definition: The item being offered.

variants.name: keywords
variants.definition: Keywords or tags used to describe this content. Multiple entries in a keywords list are typically delimited by commas.

variants.name: landlord
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The owner of the real estate property.

variants.name: language
variants.definition: A sub property of instrument. The language used on this action.

variants.name: license
variants.definition: A license document that applies to this content, typically indicated by URL.

variants.name: maxValue
variants.definition: The upper value of some characteristic or property.

variants.name: MedicalAudience
variants.definition: Target audiences for medical web pages. Enumerated type.

variants.name: MedicalDevicePurpose
variants.definition: Categories of medical devices, organized by the purpose or intended use of the device.

variants.name: MedicalEnumeration
variants.definition: Enumerations related to health and the practice of medicine.

variants.name: MedicalEvidenceLevel
variants.definition: Level of evidence for a medical guideline. Enumerated type.

variants.name: MedicalImagingTechnique
variants.definition: Any medical imaging modality typically used for diagnostic purposes. Enumerated type.

variants.name: MedicalObservationalStudyDesign
variants.definition: Design models for observational medical studies. Enumerated type.

variants.name: MedicalProcedureType
variants.definition: An enumeration that describes different types of medical procedures.

variants.name: MedicalSpecialty
variants.definition: Any specific branch of medical science or practice. Medical specialities include clinical specialties that pertain to particular organ systems and their respective disease states, as well as allied health specialties. Enumerated type.

variants.name: MedicalStudyStatus
variants.definition: The status of a medical study. Enumerated type.

variants.name: MedicalTrialDesign
variants.definition: Design models for medical trials. Enumerated type.

variants.name: MedicineSystem
variants.definition: Systems of medical practice.

variants.name: member
variants.definition: A member of an Organization or a ProgramMembership. Organizations can be members of organizations; ProgramMembership is typically for individuals.

variants.name: memberOf
variants.definition: An Organization (or ProgramMembership) to which this Person or Organization belongs.

variants.name: members
variants.definition: A member of this organization (legacy spelling; see singular form, member).

variants.name: minValue
variants.definition: The lower value of some characteristic or property.

variants.name: multipleValues
variants.definition: Whether multiple values are allowed for the property.  Default is false.

variants.name: muscleAction
variants.definition: The movement the muscle generates.

variants.name: musicGroupMember
variants.definition: A member of a music group—for example, John, Paul, George, or Ringo.

variants.name: namedPosition
variants.definition: A position played, performed or filled by a person or organization, as part of an organization. For example, an athlete in a SportsTeam might play in the position named 'Quarterback'.

variants.name: NewCondition
variants.definition: Indicates that the item is new.

variants.name: Offer
variants.definition: An offer to transfer some rights to an item or to provide a service—for example, an offer to sell tickets to an event, to rent the DVD of a movie, to stream a TV show over the internet, to repair a motorcycle, or to loan a book.

variants.name: OfferItemCondition
variants.definition: A list of possible conditions for the item.

variants.name: offers
variants.definition: An offer to provide this item—for example, an offer to sell a product, rent the DVD of a movie, or give away tickets to an event.

variants.name: OnlineOnly
variants.definition: Indicates that the item is available only online.

variants.name: opponent
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The opponent on this action.

variants.name: OrganizationRole
variants.definition: A subclass of Role used to describe roles within organizations.

variants.name: OutOfStock
variants.definition: Indicates that the item is out of stock.

variants.name: PalliativeProcedure
variants.definition: A medical procedure intended primarily for palliative purposes, aimed at relieving the symptoms of an underlying health condition.

variants.name: partySize
variants.definition: Number of people the reservation should accommodate.

variants.name: PawnShop
variants.definition: A pawn store.

variants.name: PerformanceRole
variants.definition: A PerformanceRole is a Role that some entity places with regard to a theatrical performance, e.g. in a Movie, TVSeries etc.

variants.name: PerformingArtsTheater
variants.definition: A theater or other performing art center.

variants.name: PhysicalActivityCategory
variants.definition: Categories of physical activity, organized by physiologic classification.

variants.name: PhysicalExam
variants.definition: A type of physical examination of a patient performed by a physician. Enumerated type.

variants.name: pickupTime
variants.definition: When a taxi will pickup a passenger or a rental car can be picked up.

variants.name: PlayAction
variants.definition:
The act of playing/exercising/training/performing for enjoyment, leisure, recreation, Competition or exercise.

Related actions:

  • ListenAction: Unlike ListenAction (which is under ConsumeAction), PlayAction refers to performing for an audience or at an event, rather than consuming music.
  • WatchAction: Unlike WatchAction (which is under ConsumeAction), PlayAction refers to showing/displaying for an audience or at an event, rather than consuming visual content.

variants.name: polygon
variants.definition: A polygon is the area enclosed by a point-to-point path for which the starting and ending points are the same. A polygon is expressed as a series of four or more space delimited points where the first and final points are identical.

variants.name: postOfficeBoxNumber
variants.definition: The post office box number for PO box addresses.

variants.name: potentialAction
variants.definition: Indicates a potential Action, which describes an idealized action in which this thing would play an 'object' role.

variants.name: PotentialActionStatus
variants.definition: A description of an action that is supported.

variants.name: PreOrder
variants.definition: Indicates that the item is available for pre-order.

variants.name: primaryImageOfPage
variants.definition: Indicates the main image on the page.

variants.name: Product
variants.definition: Any offered product or service. For example: a pair of shoes; a concert ticket; the rental of a car; a haircut; or an episode of a TV show streamed online.

variants.name: Property
variants.definition: A property, used to indicate attributes and relationships of some Thing; equivalent to rdf:Property.

variants.name: PropertyValueSpecification
variants.definition: A Property value specification.

variants.name: provider
variants.definition: The person or organization providing the service, reservation, or creative work. The provider may subcontract out the service.

variants.name: publishedOn
variants.definition: A broadcast service associated with the publication event.

variants.name: RadioClip
variants.definition: A short radio program or a segment/part of a radio program.

variants.name: readonlyValue
variants.definition: Whether or not a property is mutable.  Default is false. Specifying this for a property that also has a value makes it act similar to a "hidden" input in an HTML form.

variants.name: recipeCuisine
variants.definition: The cuisine of the recipe (for example, French or Ethiopian).

variants.name: RefurbishedCondition
variants.definition: Indicates that the item is refurbished.

variants.name: reviewBody
variants.definition: The actual body of the review.

variants.name: Rheumatologic
variants.definition: A specific branch of medical science that deals with the study and treatment of rheumatic, autoimmune or joint diseases.

variants.name: Role
variants.definition: Represents additional information about a relationship or property. For example a Role can be used to say that a 'member' role linking some SportsTeam to a player occurred during a particular time period. Or that a Person's 'actor' role in a Movie was for some particular characterName. Such properties can be attached to a Role entity, which is then associated with the main entities using ordinary properties like 'member' or 'actor'.

variants.name: RsvpAction
variants.definition: The act of notifying an event organizer as to whether you expect to attend the event.

variants.name: seller
variants.definition: The organization or person making the offer.

variants.name: servingSize
variants.definition: The serving size, in terms of the number of volume or mass.

variants.name: signOrSymptom
variants.definition: A sign or symptom of this condition. Signs are objective or physically observable manifestations of the medical condition while symptoms are the subjective experience of the medical condition.

variants.name: startDate
variants.definition: The start date and time of the event, role or item (in ISO 8601 date format).

variants.name: startTime
variants.definition:
The startTime of something. For a reserved event or service (e.g. FoodEstablishmentReservation), the time that it is expected to start. For actions that span a period of time, when the action was performed. e.g. John wrote a book from *January* to December.

Note that Event uses startDate/endDate instead of startTime/endTime, even when describing dates with times. This situation may be clarified in future revisions.

variants.name: stepValue
variants.definition: The stepValue attribute indicates the granularity that is expected (and required) of the value in a PropertyValueSpecification.

variants.name: subEvent
variants.definition: An Event that is part of this event. For example, a conference event includes many presentations, each of which is a subEvent of the conference.

variants.name: subEvents
variants.definition: Events that are a part of this event. For example, a conference event includes many presentations, each subEvents of the conference (legacy spelling; see singular form, subEvent).

variants.name: suggestedAnswer
variants.definition: An answer (possibly one of several, possibly incorrect) to a Question, e.g. on a Question/Answer site.

variants.name: suggestedMaxAge
variants.definition: Maximal age recommended for viewing content.

variants.name: suggestedMinAge
variants.definition: Minimal age recommended for viewing content.

variants.name: supercededBy
variants.definition: Relates a property to one that supercedes it.

variants.name: supplyTo
variants.definition: The area to which the artery supplies blood.

variants.name: target
variants.definition: Indicates a target EntryPoint for an Action.

variants.name: TherapeuticProcedure
variants.definition: A medical procedure intended primarily for therapeutic purposes, aimed at improving a health condition.

variants.name: ToyStore
variants.definition: A toy store.

variants.name: True
variants.definition: The boolean value true

variants.name: TVClip
variants.definition: A short TV program or a segment/part of a TV program.

variants.name: urlTemplate
variants.definition: An url template (RFC6570) that will be used to construct the target of the execution of the action.

variants.name: UsedCondition
variants.definition: Indicates that the item is used.

variants.name: valueMaxLength
variants.definition: Specifies the allowed range for number of characters in a literal value.

variants.name: valueMinLength
variants.definition: Specifies the minimum allowed range for number of characters in a literal value.

variants.name: valueName
variants.definition: Indicates the name of the PropertyValueSpecification to be used in URL templates and form encoding in a manner analogous to HTML's input@name.

variants.name: valuePattern
variants.definition: Specifies a regular expression for testing literal values according to the HTML spec.

variants.name: valueRequired
variants.definition: Whether the property must be filled in to complete the action.  Default is false.

variants.name: vatID
variants.definition: The Value-added Tax ID of the organization or person.

variants.name: vendor
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The seller. The participant/person/organization that sold the object.

variants.name: Volcano
variants.definition: A volcano, like Fuji san.

variants.name: workPerformed
variants.definition: A work performed in some event, for example a play performed in a TheaterEvent.

variants.name: associatedMedia
variants.definition: A media object that encodes this CreativeWork. This property is a synonym for encoding.

variants.name: bookingAgent
variants.definition: 'bookingAgent' is an out-dated term indicating a 'broker' that serves as a booking agent.

variants.name: broker
variants.definition: An entity that arranges for an exchange between a buyer and a seller.  In most cases a broker never acquires or releases ownership of a product or service involved in an exchange.  If it is not clear whether an entity is a broker, seller, or buyer, the latter two terms are preferred.

variants.name: carrier
variants.definition: 'carrier' is an out-dated term indicating the 'provider' for parcel delivery and flights.

variants.name: clipNumber
variants.definition: Position of the clip within an ordered group of clips.

variants.name: encodesCreativeWork
variants.definition: The CreativeWork encoded by this media object.

variants.name: encoding
variants.definition: A media object that encodes this CreativeWork. This property is a synonym for associatedMedia.

variants.name: encodings
variants.definition: A media object that encodes this CreativeWork (legacy spelling; see singular form, encoding).

variants.name: episodeNumber
variants.definition: Position of the episode within an ordered group of episodes.

variants.name: EventCancelled
variants.definition: The event has been cancelled. If the event has multiple startDate values, all are assumed to be cancelled. Either startDate or previousStartDate may be used to specify the event's cancelled date(s).

variants.name: EventPostponed
variants.definition: The event has been postponed and no new date has been set. The event's previousStartDate should be set.

variants.name: EventRescheduled
variants.definition: The event has been rescheduled. The event's previousStartDate should be set to the old date and the startDate should be set to the event's new date. (If the event has been rescheduled multiple times, the previousStartDate property may be repeated.)

variants.name: exampleOfWork
variants.definition: A creative work that this work is an example/instance/realization/derivation of.

variants.name: flightNumber
variants.definition: The unique identifier for a flight including the airline IATA code. For example, if describing United flight 110, where the IATA code for United is 'UA', the flightNumber is 'UA110'.

variants.name: gtin13
variants.definition: The GTIN-13 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. This is equivalent to 13-digit ISBN codes and EAN UCC-13. Former 12-digit UPC codes can be converted into a GTIN-13 code by simply adding a preceeding zero. See GS1 GTIN Summary for more details.

variants.name: gtin14
variants.definition: The GTIN-14 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. See GS1 GTIN Summary for more details.

variants.name: gtin8
variants.definition: The GTIN-8 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. This code is also known as EAN/UCC-8 or 8-digit EAN. See GS1 GTIN Summary for more details.

variants.name: hasMap
variants.definition: A URL to a map of the place.

variants.name: hasPart
variants.definition: Indicates a CreativeWork that is (in some sense) a part of this CreativeWork.

variants.name: height
variants.definition: The height of the item or person.

variants.name: HobbyShop
variants.definition: A store that sells materials useful or necessary for various hobbies.

variants.name: Hostel
variants.definition: A hostel - cheap accommodation, often in shared dormitories.

variants.name: HVACBusiness
variants.definition: A business that provide Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning services.

variants.name: image
variants.definition: An image of the item. This can be a URL or a fully described ImageObject.

variants.name: InsuranceAgency
variants.definition: An Insurance agency.

variants.name: isPartOf
variants.definition: Indicates a CreativeWork that this CreativeWork is (in some sense) part of.

variants.name: issn
variants.definition: The International Standard Serial Number (ISSN) that identifies this periodical. You can repeat this property to (for example) identify different formats of this periodical.

variants.name: issueNumber
variants.definition: Identifies the issue of publication; for example, "iii" or "2".

variants.name: item
variants.definition: An entity represented by an entry in a list (e.g. an 'artist' in a list of 'artists')’.

variants.name: ItemList
variants.definition: A list of items of any sort—for example, Top 10 Movies About Weathermen, or Top 100 Party Songs. Not to be confused with HTML lists, which are often used only for formatting.

variants.name: itemListElement
variants.definition:
For itemListElement values, you can use simple strings (e.g. "Peter", "Paul, "Mary"), existing entities, or use ListItem.

Text values are best if the elements in the list are plain strings. Existing entities are best for a simple, unordered list of existing things in your data. ListItem is used with ordered lists when you want to provide additional context about the element in that list or when the same item might be in different places in different lists.

Note: The order of elements in your mark-up is not sufficient for indicating the order or elements. Use ItemList with a 'position' property in such cases.

variants.name: itemListOrder
variants.definition: Type of ordering (e.g. Ascending, Descending, Unordered).

variants.name: ItemListOrderAscending
variants.definition: An ItemList ordered with lower values listed first.

variants.name: ItemListOrderDescending
variants.definition: An ItemList ordered with higher values listed first.

variants.name: ItemListOrderType
variants.definition: Enumerated for values for itemListOrder for indicating how an ordered ItemList is organized.

variants.name: ItemListUnordered
variants.definition: An ItemList ordered with no explicit order.

variants.name: LiquorStore
variants.definition: A shop that sells alcoholic drinks such as wine, beer, whisky and other spirits.

variants.name: ListItem
variants.definition: An list item, e.g. a step in a checklist or how-to description.

variants.name: MapCategoryType
variants.definition: An enumeration of several kinds of Map.

variants.name: mapType
variants.definition: Indicates the kind of Map, from the MapCategoryType Enumeration.

variants.name: merchant
variants.definition: 'merchant' is an out-dated term for 'seller'.

variants.name: MiddleSchool
variants.definition: A middle school (typically for children aged around 11-14, although this varies somewhat).

variants.name: MobileApplication
variants.definition: A software application designed specifically to work well on a mobile device such as a telephone.

variants.name: MobilePhoneStore
variants.definition: A store that sells mobile phones and related accessories.

variants.name: nextItem
variants.definition: A link to the ListItem that follows the current one.

variants.name: numberOfItems
variants.definition: The number of items in an ItemList. Note that some descriptions might not full describe all items in a list (e.g. multi-page pagination).

variants.name: Offer
variants.definition:
An offer to transfer some rights to an item or to provide a service—for example, an offer to sell tickets to an event, to rent the DVD of a movie, to stream a TV show over the internet, to repair a motorcycle, or to loan a book.

For GTIN-related fields, see Check Digit calculator and validation guide from GS1.

variants.name: Optician
variants.definition: A store that sells reading glasses and similar devices for improving vision.

variants.name: organizer
variants.definition: An organizer of an Event.

variants.name: pageEnd
variants.definition: The page on which the work ends; for example "138" or "xvi".

variants.name: pageStart
variants.definition: The page on which the work starts; for example "135" or "xiii".

variants.name: pagination
variants.definition: Any description of pages that is not separated into pageStart and pageEnd; for example, "1-6, 9, 55" or "10-12, 46-49".

variants.name: ParkingMap
variants.definition: A parking map.

variants.name: PawnShop
variants.definition: A shop that will buy, or lend money against the security of, personal possessions.

variants.name: Periodical
variants.definition: A publication in any medium issued in successive parts bearing numerical or chronological designations and intended, such as a magazine, scholarly journal, or newspaper to continue indefinitely.

variants.name: position
variants.definition: The position of an item in a series or sequence of items.

variants.name: previousItem
variants.definition: A link to the ListItem that preceeds the current one.

variants.name: price
variants.definition:
The offer price of a product, or of a price component when attached to PriceSpecification and its subtypes.

Usage guidelines:
  • Use the priceCurrency property (with ISO 4217 codes e.g. "USD") instead of including ambiguous symbols such as '$' in the value.
  • Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.
  • Note that both RDFa and Microdata syntax allow the use of a "content=" attribute for publishing simple machine-readable values alongside more human-friendly formatting.
  • Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similiar Unicode symbols.

variants.name: provider
variants.definition: The service provider, service operator, or service performer; the goods producer. Another party (a seller) may offer those services or goods on behalf of the provider. A provider may also serve as the seller.

variants.name: PublicationIssue
variants.definition: A part of a successively published publication such as a periodical or publication volume, often numbered, usually containing a grouping of works such as articles.

variants.name: PublicationVolume
variants.definition: A part of a successively published publication such as a periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered. It may represent a time span, such as a year.

variants.name: Reservoir
variants.definition: A reservoir of water, typically an artificially created lake, like the Lake Kariba reservoir.

variants.name: Review
variants.definition: A review of an item - for example, of a restaurant, movie, or store.

variants.name: RVPark
variants.definition: A place offering space for "Recreational Vehicles", Caravans, mobile homes and the like.

variants.name: seasonNumber
variants.definition: Position of the season within an ordered group of seasons.

variants.name: SeatingMap
variants.definition: A seating map.

variants.name: SelfStorage
variants.definition: A self-storage facility.

variants.name: seller
variants.definition: An entity which offers (sells / leases / lends / loans) the services / goods.  A seller may also be a provider.

variants.name: State
variants.definition: A state or province of a country.

variants.name: supersededBy
variants.definition: Relates a property to one that supersedes it.

variants.name: Table
variants.definition: A table on a Web page.

variants.name: TheaterGroup
variants.definition: A theater group or company, for example, the Royal Shakespeare Company or Druid Theatre.

variants.name: TransitMap
variants.definition: A transit map.

variants.name: vendor
variants.definition: 'vendor' is an earlier term for 'seller'.

variants.name: VenueMap
variants.definition: A venue map (e.g. for malls, auditoriums, museums, etc.).

variants.name: volumeNumber
variants.definition: Identifies the volume of publication or multi-part work; for example, "iii" or "2".

variants.name: WebSite
variants.definition: A WebSite is a set of related web pages and other items typically served from a single web domain and accessible via URLs.

variants.name: weight
variants.definition: The weight of the product or person.

variants.name: workExample
variants.definition: Example/instance/realization/derivation of the concept of this creative work. eg. The paperback edition, first edition, or eBook.

variants.name: Action
variants.definition:
An action performed by a direct agent and indirect participants upon a direct object. Optionally happens at a location with the help of an inanimate instrument. The execution of the action may produce a result. Specific action sub-type documentation specifies the exact expectation of each argument/role.

See also blog post and Actions overview document.

variants.name: ActivateAction
variants.definition: The act of starting or activating a device or application (e.g. starting a timer or turning on a flashlight).

variants.name: actor
variants.definition: An actor, e.g. in tv, radio, movie, video games etc. Actors can be associated with individual items or with a series, episode, clip.

variants.name: actors
variants.definition: An actor, e.g. in tv, radio, movie, video games etc. Actors can be associated with individual items or with a series, episode, clip.

variants.name: additionalNumberOfGuests
variants.definition: If responding yes, the number of guests who will attend in addition to the invitee.

variants.name: albumProductionType
variants.definition: Classification of the album by it's type of content: soundtrack, live album, studio album, etc.

variants.name: albumRelease
variants.definition: A release of this album.

variants.name: AlbumRelease
variants.definition: AlbumRelease.

variants.name: albumReleaseType
variants.definition: The kind of release which this album is: single, EP or album.

variants.name: albums
variants.definition: A collection of music albums.

variants.name: alternateName
variants.definition: An alias for the item.

variants.name: amount
variants.definition: The amount of money.

variants.name: Article
variants.definition:
An article, such as a news article or piece of investigative report. Newspapers and magazines have articles of many different types and this is intended to cover them all.

See also blog post

variants.name: athlete
variants.definition: A person that acts as performing member of a sports team; a player as opposed to a coach

variants.name: attendees
variants.definition: A person attending the event.

variants.name: awards
variants.definition: Awards won by this person or for this creative work.

variants.name: awayTeam
variants.definition: The away team in a sports event.

variants.name: baseSalary
variants.definition: The base salary of the job or of an employee in an EmployeeRole.

variants.name: birthPlace
variants.definition: The place where the person was born.

variants.name: blogPosts
variants.definition: The postings that are part of this blog.

variants.name: BookSeries
variants.definition: A series of books. Included books can be indicated with the hasPart property.

variants.name: branch
variants.definition: The branches that delineate from the nerve bundle.

variants.name: breadcrumb
variants.definition: A set of links that can help a user understand and navigate a website hierarchy.

variants.name: BreadcrumbList
variants.definition: A BreadcrumbList is an ItemList consisting of a chain of linked Web pages, typically described using at least their URL and their name, ending with the current page.

variants.name: BroadcastRelease
variants.definition: BroadcastRelease.

variants.name: CassetteFormat
variants.definition: CassetteFormat.

variants.name: catalogNumber
variants.definition: The catalog number for the release.

variants.name: CDFormat
variants.definition: CDFormat.

variants.name: character
variants.definition: Fictional person connected with a creative work.

variants.name: itemListElement
variants.definition:
For itemListElement values, you can use simple strings (e.g. "Peter", "Paul, "Mary"), existing entities, or use ListItem.

Text values are best if the elements in the list are plain strings. Existing entities are best for a simple, unordered list of existing things in your data. ListItem is used with ordered lists when you want to provide additional context about the element in that list or when the same item might be in different places in different lists.

Note: The order of elements in your mark-up is not sufficient for indicating the order or elements. Use ListItem with a 'position' property in such cases.

Such properties can be attached to a Role entity, which is then associated with the main entities using ordinary properties like 'member' or 'actor'.

variants.name: Series
variants.definition:
A Series in schema.org is a group of related items, typically but not necessarily of the same kind. Series are usually organized into some order, often chronological. Unlike ItemList which is a general purpose data structure for lists of things, the emphasis with Series is on published materials (written e.g. books and periodicals, or media such as tv, radio and games).

Specific subtypes are available for describing TVSeries, RadioSeries, MovieSeries, BookSeries, Periodical and VideoGameSeries. In each case, the hasPart / isPartOf properties can be used to relate the Series to its parts. The general Series type serves largely just to organize these more specific and practical subtypes.

It is common for properties applicable to an item from the series to be usefully applied to the containing group. Schema.org attempts to anticipate some of these cases, but publishers should be free to apply properties of the series parts to the series as a whole wherever they seem appropriate.

variants.name: CheckInAction
variants.definition:
The act of an agent communicating (service provider, social media, etc) their arrival by registering/confirming for a previously reserved service (e.g. flight check in) or at a place (e.g. hotel), possibly resulting in a result (boarding pass, etc).

Related actions:

  • CheckOutAction: The antagonym of CheckInAction.
  • ArriveAction: Unlike ArriveAction, CheckInAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the start of a previously reserved service.
  • ConfirmAction: Unlike ConfirmAction, CheckInAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the *start* of a previously reserved service rather than its validity/existence
.

variants.name: CheckOutAction
variants.definition:
The act of an agent communicating (service provider, social media, etc) their departure of a previously reserved service (e.g. flight check in) or place (e.g. hotel).

Related actions:

  • CheckInAction: The antagonym of CheckOutAction.
  • DepartAction: Unlike DepartAction, CheckOutAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the end of a previously reserved service.
  • CancelAction: Unlike CancelAction, CheckOutAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the end of a previously reserved service
.

variants.name: ConfirmAction

The act of notifying someone that a future event/action is going to happen as expected.

Related actions:

variants.name: Eye

variants.name: FollowAction
variants.definition:
The act of forming a personal connection with someone/something (object) unidirectionally/asymmetrically to get updates polled from.

Related actions:

  • BefriendAction: Unlike BefriendAction, FollowAction implies that the connection is *not* necessarily reciprocal.
  • SubscribeAction: Unlike SubscribeAction, FollowAction implies that the follower acts as an active agent constantly/actively polling for updates.
  • RegisterAction: Unlike RegisterAction, FollowAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object.
  • JoinAction: Unlike JoinAction, FollowAction implies that the agent is interested in getting updates from the object.
  • TrackAction: Unlike TrackAction, FollowAction refers to the polling of updates of all aspects of animate objects rather than the location of inanimate objects (e.g. you track a package, but you don't follow it)
.

Related actions:

  • TakeAction: Reciprocal of GiveAction.
  • SendAction: Unlike SendAction, GiveAction implies that ownership is being transferred (e.g. I may send my laptop to you, but that doesn't mean I'm giving it to you)
.

variants.definition:
For itemListElement values, you can use simple strings (e.g. "Peter", "Paul", "Mary"), existing entities, or use ListItem.

Text values are best if the elements in the list are plain strings. Existing entities are best for a simple, unordered list of existing things in your data. ListItem is used with ordered lists when you want to provide additional context about the element in that list or when the same item might be in different places in different lists.

Note: The order of elements in your mark-up is not sufficient for indicating the order or elements. Use ListItem with a 'position' property in such cases.

variants.name: JoinAction
variants.definition:
An agent joins an event/group with participants/friends at a location.

Related actions:

  • RegisterAction: Unlike RegisterAction, JoinAction refers to joining a group/team of people.
  • SubscribeAction: Unlike SubscribeAction, JoinAction does not imply that you'll be receiving updates.
  • FollowAction: Unlike FollowAction, JoinAction does not imply that you'll be polling for updates
.

variants.name: LeaveAction
variants.definition:
An agent leaves an event / group with participants/friends at a location.

Related actions:

  • JoinAction: The antagonym of LeaveAction.
  • UnRegisterAction: Unlike UnRegisterAction, LeaveAction implies leaving a group/team of people rather than a service
.

variants.name: LendAction
variants.definition:
The act of providing an object under an agreement that it will be returned at a later date. Reciprocal of BorrowAction.

Related actions:

  • BorrowAction: Reciprocal of LendAction
.

variants.name: Lung
variants.definition: Lung.

variants.name: Mass
variants.definition: Properties that take Mass as values are of the form '<Number> <Mass unit of measure>'. E.g., '7 kg'.

variants.name: material
variants.definition: e.g. Oil, Watercolour, Acrylic, Linoprint, Marble, Cyanotype, Digital, Lithograph, DryPoint, Intaglio, Pastel, Woodcut, Pencil, Mixed Media, etc.

variants.name: minimumPaymentDue
variants.definition: The minimum payment required at this time.

variants.name: Mountain
variants.definition: A mountain, like Mount Whitney or Mount Everest.

variants.name: MoveAction
variants.definition:
The act of an agent relocating to a place.

Related actions:

  • TransferAction: Unlike TransferAction, the subject of the move is a living Person or Organization rather than an inanimate object
.

variants.name: MusculoskeletalExam
variants.definition: Musculoskeletal.

variants.name: musicBy
variants.definition: The composer of the soundtrack.

variants.name: musicCompositionForm
variants.definition: The type of composition (e.g. overture, sonata, symphony, etc.).

variants.name: Neck
variants.definition: Neck.

variants.name: Neuro
variants.definition: Neuro.

variants.name: NewsArticle
variants.definition: A news article.

variants.name: Nose
variants.definition: Nose.

variants.name: numberOfEmployees
variants.definition: The size of business by number of employees.

variants.name: offers
variants.definition: An offer to provide this item—for example, an offer to sell a product, rent the DVD of a movie, or give away tickets to an event.

variants.name: ParentAudience
variants.definition: A set of characteristics describing parents, who can be interested in viewing some content.

variants.name: partOfInvoice
variants.definition: The order is being paid as part of the referenced Invoice.

variants.name: partOfTVSeries
variants.definition: The TV series to which this episode or season belongs.

variants.name: paymentDue
variants.definition: The date that payment is due.

variants.name: paymentMethod
variants.definition: The name of the credit card or other method of payment for the order.

variants.name: paymentMethodId
variants.definition: An identifier for the method of payment used (e.g. the last 4 digits of the credit card).

variants.name: paymentStatus
variants.definition: The status of payment; whether the invoice has been paid or not.

variants.name: Periodical
variants.definition:
A publication in any medium issued in successive parts bearing numerical or chronological designations and intended, such as a magazine, scholarly journal, or newspaper to continue indefinitely.

See also blog post.

variants.name: PlayAction
variants.definition:
The act of playing/exercising/training/performing for enjoyment, leisure, recreation, Competition or exercise.

Related actions:

  • ListenAction: Unlike ListenAction (which is under ConsumeAction), PlayAction refers to performing for an audience or at an event, rather than consuming music.
  • WatchAction: Unlike WatchAction (which is under ConsumeAction), PlayAction refers to showing/displaying for an audience or at an event, rather than consuming visual content
.

variants.name: Pond
variants.definition: A pond.

variants.name: priceSpecification
variants.definition: One or more detailed price specifications, indicating the unit price and delivery or payment charges.

variants.name: producer
variants.definition: The person or organization who produced the work (e.g. music album, movie, tv/radio series etc.).

variants.name: provider
variants.definition: The service provider, service operator, or service performer; the goods producer. Another party (a seller) may offer those services or goods on behalf of the provider. A provider may also serve as the seller.

variants.name: PublicationIssue
variants.definition:
A part of a successively published publication such as a periodical or publication volume, often numbered, usually containing a grouping of works such as articles.

See also blog post.

variants.name: PublicationVolume
variants.definition:
A part of a successively published publication such as a periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered. It may represent a time span, such as a year.

See also blog post.

variants.name: QualitativeValue
variants.definition: A predefined value for a product characteristic, e.g. the power cord plug type "US" or the garment sizes "S", "M", "L", and "XL".

variants.name: ReceiveAction
variants.definition:
The act of physically/electronically taking delivery of an object thathas been transferred from an origin to a destination. Reciprocal of SendAction.

Related actions:

  • SendAction: The reciprocal of ReceiveAction.
  • TakeAction: Unlike TakeAction, ReceiveAction does not imply that the ownership has been transfered (e.g. I can receive a package, but it does not mean the package is now mine)
.

variants.name: referencesOrder
variants.definition: The Order(s) related to this Invoice. One or more Orders may be combined into a single Invoice.

variants.name: RegisterAction
variants.definition:
The act of registering to be a user of a service, product or web page.

Related actions:

  • JoinAction: Unlike JoinAction, RegisterAction implies you are registering to be a user of a service, *not* a group/team of people.
  • FollowAction: Unlike FollowAction, RegisterAction doesn't imply that the agent is expecting to poll for updates from the object.
  • SubscribeAction: Unlike SubscribeAction, RegisterAction doesn't imply that the agent is expecting updates from the object
.

variants.name: RejectAction
variants.definition:
The act of rejecting to/adopting an object.

Related actions:

  • AcceptAction: The antagonym of RejectAction
.

variants.name: ReplyAction
variants.definition:
The act of responding to a question/message asked/sent by the object. Related to AskAction.

Related actions:

  • AskAction: Appears generally as an origin of a ReplyAction
.

variants.name: ReserveAction
variants.definition:
Reserving a concrete object.

Related actions:

  • ScheduleAction: Unlike ScheduleAction, ReserveAction reserves concrete objects (e.g. a table, a hotel) towards a time slot / spatial allocation
.

variants.name: Role
variants.definition:
Represents additional information about a relationship or property. For example a Role can be used to say that a 'member' role linking some SportsTeam to a player occurred during a particular time period. Or that a Person's 'actor' role in a Movie was for some particular characterName. Such properties can be attached to a Role entity, which is then associated with the main entities using ordinary properties like 'member' or 'actor'.

See also blog post.

variants.name: runtime
variants.definition: Runtime platform or script interpreter dependencies (Example - Java v1, Python2.3, .Net Framework 3.0).

variants.name: ScheduleAction
variants.definition:
Scheduling future actions, events, or tasks.

Related actions:

  • ReserveAction: Unlike ReserveAction, ScheduleAction allocates future actions (e.g. an event, a task, etc) towards a time slot / spatial allocation
.

variants.name: scheduledPaymentDate
variants.definition: The date the invoice is scheduled to be paid.

variants.name: SearchAction
variants.definition:
The act of searching for an object.

Related actions:

  • FindAction: SearchAction generally leads to a FindAction, but not necessarily
.

variants.name: SendAction
variants.definition:
The act of physically/electronically dispatching an object for transfer from an origin to a destination.

Related actions:

  • ReceiveAction: The reciprocal of SendAction.
  • GiveAction: Unlike GiveAction, SendAction does not imply the transfer of ownership (e.g. I can send you my laptop, but I'm not necessarily giving it to you)
.

variants.name: Skin
variants.definition: Skin.

variants.name: SubscribeAction
variants.definition:
The act of forming a personal connection with someone/something (object) unidirectionally/asymmetrically to get updates pushed to.

Related actions:

  • FollowAction: Unlike FollowAction, SubscribeAction implies that the subscriber acts as a passive agent being constantly/actively pushed for updates.
  • RegisterAction: Unlike RegisterAction, SubscribeAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object.
  • JoinAction: Unlike JoinAction, SubscribeAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object
.

variants.name: surface
variants.definition: e.g. Canvas, Paper, Wood, Board, etc.

variants.name: TakeAction
variants.definition:
The act of gaining ownership of an object from an origin. Reciprocal of GiveAction.

Related actions:

  • GiveAction: The reciprocal of TakeAction.
  • ReceiveAction: Unlike ReceiveAction, TakeAction implies that ownership has been transfered
.

variants.name: Throat
variants.definition: Throat.

variants.name: toLocation
variants.definition: A sub property of location. The final location of the object or the agent after the action.

variants.name: totalPaymentDue
variants.definition: The total amount due.

variants.name: track
variants.definition: A music recording (track)—usually a single song. If an ItemList is given, the list should contain items of type MusicRecording.

variants.name: TrackAction
variants.definition:
An agent tracks an object for updates.

Related actions:

  • FollowAction: Unlike FollowAction, TrackAction refers to the interest on the location of innanimates objects.
  • SubscribeAction: Unlike SubscribeAction, TrackAction refers to the interest on the location of innanimate objects
.

variants.name: trailer
variants.definition: The trailer of a movie or tv/radio series, season, episode, etc.

variants.name: True
variants.definition: The boolean value true.

variants.name: UnRegisterAction
variants.definition:
The act of un-registering from a service.

Related actions:

  • RegisterAction: Antagonym of UnRegisterAction.
  • Leave: Unlike LeaveAction, UnRegisterAction implies that you are unregistering from a service you werer previously registered, rather than leaving a team/group of people
.

variants.name: UserInteraction
variants.definition: A user interacting with a page.

variants.name: valuePattern
variants.definition: Specifies a regular expression for testing literal values according to the HTML spec.

variants.name: VisualArtwork
variants.definition: A work of art that is primarily visual in character.

variants.name: VitalSign
variants.definition: VitalSign.

variants.name: Waterfall
variants.definition: A waterfall, like Niagara.

variants.name: WebPage
variants.definition: A web page. Every web page is implicitly assumed to be declared to be of type WebPage, so the various properties about that webpage, such as breadcrumb may be used. We recommend explicit declaration if these properties are specified, but if they are found outside of an itemscope, they will be assumed to be about the page.

variants.name: WebPageElement
variants.definition: A web page element, like a table or an image.

variants.name: width
variants.definition: The width of the item.

variants.name: about
variants.definition: The subject matter of the content.

variants.name: AboutPage
variants.definition: Web page type: About page.

variants.name: AcceptAction
variants.definition:
The act of committing to/adopting an object.

Related actions:

  • RejectAction: The antonym of AcceptAction
.

variants.name: acceptedAnswer
variants.definition: The answer that has been accepted as best, typically on a Question/Answer site. Sites vary in their selection mechanisms, e.g. drawing on community opinion and/or the view of the Question author.

variants.name: acceptedOffer
variants.definition: The offer(s) -- e.g., product, quantity and price combinations -- included in the order.

variants.name: acceptedPaymentMethod
variants.definition: The payment method(s) accepted by seller for this offer.

variants.name: acceptsReservations
variants.definition: Indicates whether a FoodEstablishment accepts reservations. Values can be Boolean, an URL at which reservations can be made or (for backwards compatibility) the strings Yes or No.

variants.name: accessCode
variants.definition: Password, PIN, or access code needed for delivery (e.g. from a locker).

variants.name: accessibilityAPI
variants.definition: Indicates that the resource is compatible with the referenced accessibility API (WebSchemas wiki lists possible values).

variants.name: accessibilityControl
variants.definition: Identifies input methods that are sufficient to fully control the described resource (WebSchemas wiki lists possible values).

variants.name: accessibilityFeature
variants.definition: Content features of the resource, such as accessible media, alternatives and supported enhancements for accessibility (WebSchemas wiki lists possible values).

variants.name: accessibilityHazard
variants.definition: A characteristic of the described resource that is physiologically dangerous to some users. Related to WCAG 2.0 guideline 2.3 (WebSchemas wiki lists possible values).

variants.name: accountablePerson
variants.definition: Specifies the Person that is legally accountable for the CreativeWork.

variants.name: accountId
variants.definition: The identifier for the account the payment will be applied to.

variants.name: AccountingService
variants.definition: Accountancy business.

variants.name: AchieveAction
variants.definition: The act of accomplishing something via     previous efforts. It is an instantaneous action rather than an ongoing     process.

variants.name: acquiredFrom
variants.definition: The organization or person from which the product was acquired.

variants.name: action
variants.definition: The movement the muscle generates.

variants.name: Action
variants.definition:
An action performed by a direct agent and indirect participants upon a direct object. Optionally happens at a location with the help of an inanimate instrument. The execution of the action may produce a result. Specific action sub-type documentation specifies the exact expectation of each argument/role.

See also blog post and Actions overview document.

variants.name: actionApplication
variants.definition: An application that can complete the request.

variants.name: actionOption
variants.definition: A sub property of object. The options subject to this action.

variants.name: actionStatus
variants.definition: Indicates the current disposition of the Action.

variants.name: ActionStatusType
variants.definition: The status of an Action.

variants.name: ActivateAction
variants.definition: The act of starting or activating a device or application (e.g. starting a timer or turning on a flashlight).

variants.name: activeIngredient
variants.definition: An active ingredient, typically chemical compounds and/or biologic substances.

variants.name: activityDuration
variants.definition: Length of time to engage in the activity.

variants.name: activityFrequency
variants.definition: How often one should engage in the activity.

variants.name: actor
variants.definition: An actor, e.g. in tv, radio, movie, video games etc. Actors can be associated with individual items or with a series, episode, clip.

variants.name: actors
variants.definition: An actor, e.g. in tv, radio, movie, video games etc. Actors can be associated with individual items or with a series, episode, clip.

variants.name: AddAction
variants.definition: The act of editing by adding an object to a collection.

variants.name: additionalName
variants.definition: An additional name for a Person, can be used for a middle name.

variants.name: additionalNumberOfGuests
variants.definition: If responding yes, the number of guests who will attend in addition to the invitee.

variants.name: additionalProperty
variants.definition:
A property-value pair representing an additional characteristics of the entitity, e.g. a product feature or another characteristic for which there is no matching property in schema.org.

Note: Publishers should be aware that applications designed to use specific schema.org properties (e.g. http://schema.org/width, http://schema.org/color, http://schema.org/gtin13, ...) will typically expect such data to be provided using those properties, rather than using the generic property/value mechanism.

variants.name: additionalType
variants.definition: An additional type for the item, typically used for adding more specific types from external vocabularies in microdata syntax. This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. In RDFa syntax, it is better to use the native RDFa syntax - the 'typeof' attribute - for multiple types. Schema.org tools may have only weaker understanding of extra types, in particular those defined externally.

variants.name: additionalVariable
variants.definition: Any additional component of the exercise prescription that may need to be articulated to the patient. This may include the order of exercises, the number of repetitions of movement, quantitative distance, progressions over time, etc.

variants.name: addOn
variants.definition: An additional offer that can only be obtained in combination with the first base offer (e.g. supplements and extensions that are available for a surcharge).

variants.name: address
variants.definition: Physical address of the item.

variants.name: addressCountry
variants.definition: The country. For example, USA. You can also provide the two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

variants.name: addressLocality
variants.definition: The locality. For example, Mountain View.

variants.name: addressRegion
variants.definition: The region. For example, CA.

variants.name: administrationRoute
variants.definition: A route by which this drug may be administered, e.g. 'oral'.

variants.name: AdministrativeArea
variants.definition: A geographical region under the jurisdiction of a particular government.

variants.name: AdultEntertainment
variants.definition: An adult entertainment establishment.

variants.name: advanceBookingRequirement
variants.definition: The amount of time that is required between accepting the offer and the actual usage of the resource or service.

variants.name: adverseOutcome
variants.definition: A possible complication and/or side effect of this therapy. If it is known that an adverse outcome is serious (resulting in death, disability, or permanent damage; requiring hospitalization; or is otherwise life-threatening or requires immediate medical attention), tag it as a seriouseAdverseOutcome instead.

variants.name: affectedBy
variants.definition: Drugs that affect the test's results.

variants.name: affiliation
variants.definition: An organization that this person is affiliated with. For example, a school/university, a club, or a team.

variants.name: agent
variants.definition: The direct performer or driver of the action (animate or inanimate). e.g. *John* wrote a book.

variants.name: AggregateOffer
variants.definition: When a single product is associated with multiple offers (for example, the same pair of shoes is offered by different merchants), then AggregateOffer can be used.

variants.name: aggregateRating
variants.definition: The overall rating, based on a collection of reviews or ratings, of the item.

variants.name: AggregateRating
variants.definition: The average rating based on multiple ratings or reviews.

variants.name: AgreeAction
variants.definition: The act of expressing a consistency of opinion with the object. An agent agrees to/about an object (a proposition, topic or theme) with participants.

variants.name: aircraft
variants.definition: The kind of aircraft (e.g., "Boeing 747").

variants.name: Airline
variants.definition: An organization that provides flights for passengers.

variants.name: Airport
variants.definition: An airport.

variants.name: album
variants.definition: A music album.

variants.name: albumProductionType
variants.definition: Classification of the album by it's type of content: soundtrack, live album, studio album, etc.

variants.name: albumRelease
variants.definition: A release of this album.

variants.name: albumReleaseType
variants.definition: The kind of release which this album is: single, EP or album.

variants.name: albums
variants.definition: A collection of music albums.

variants.name: alcoholWarning
variants.definition: Any precaution, guidance, contraindication, etc. related to consumption of alcohol while taking this drug.

variants.name: algorithm
variants.definition: The algorithm or rules to follow to compute the score.

variants.name: AlignmentObject
variants.definition: An intangible item that describes an alignment between a learning resource and a node in an educational framework.

variants.name: alignmentType
variants.definition: A category of alignment between the learning resource and the framework node. Recommended values include: 'assesses', 'teaches', 'requires', 'textComplexity', 'readingLevel', 'educationalSubject', and 'educationLevel'.

variants.name: AllocateAction
variants.definition: The act of organizing tasks/objects/events by associating resources to it.

variants.name: AllWheelDriveConfiguration
variants.definition: All-wheel Drive is a transmission layout where the engine drives all four wheels.

variants.name: alternateName
variants.definition: An alias for the item.

variants.name: alternativeHeadline
variants.definition: A secondary title of the CreativeWork.

variants.name: alumni
variants.definition: Alumni of educational organization.

variants.name: alumniOf
variants.definition: An educational organizations that the person is an alumni of.

variants.name: amount
variants.definition: The amount of money.

variants.name: amountOfThisGood
variants.definition: The quantity of the goods included in the offer.

variants.name: AmusementPark
variants.definition: An amusement park.

variants.name: AnatomicalStructure
variants.definition: Any part of the human body, typically a component of an anatomical system. Organs, tissues, and cells are all anatomical structures.

variants.name: AnatomicalSystem
variants.definition: An anatomical system is a group of anatomical structures that work together to perform a certain task. Anatomical systems, such as organ systems, are one organizing principle of anatomy, and can includes circulatory, digestive, endocrine, integumentary, immune, lymphatic, muscular, nervous, reproductive, respiratory, skeletal, urinary, vestibular, and other systems.

variants.name: AnimalShelter
variants.definition: Animal shelter.

variants.name: Answer
variants.definition: An answer offered to a question; perhaps correct, perhaps opinionated or wrong.

variants.name: answerCount
variants.definition: The number of answers this question has received.

variants.name: antagonist
variants.definition: The muscle whose action counteracts the specified muscle.

variants.name: ApartmentComplex
variants.definition: Residence type: Apartment complex.

variants.name: APIReference
variants.definition: Reference documentation for application programming interfaces (APIs).

variants.name: AppendAction
variants.definition: The act of inserting at the end if an ordered collection.

variants.name: applicableLocation
variants.definition: The location in which the status applies.

variants.name: application
variants.definition: An application that can complete the request.

variants.name: applicationCategory
variants.definition: Type of software application, e.g. "Game, Multimedia".

variants.name: applicationSubCategory
variants.definition: Subcategory of the application, e.g. "Arcade Game".

variants.name: applicationSuite
variants.definition: The name of the application suite to which the application belongs (e.g. Excel belongs to Office).

variants.name: appliesToDeliveryMethod
variants.definition: The delivery method(s) to which the delivery charge or payment charge specification applies.

variants.name: appliesToPaymentMethod
variants.definition: The payment method(s) to which the payment charge specification applies.

variants.name: ApplyAction
variants.definition:
The act of registering to an organization/service without the guarantee to receive it.

Related actions:

  • RegisterAction: Unlike RegisterAction, ApplyAction has no guarantees that the application will be accepted
.

variants.name: ApprovedIndication
variants.definition: An indication for a medical therapy that has been formally specified or approved by a regulatory body that regulates use of the therapy; for example, the US FDA approves indications for most drugs in the US.

variants.name: Aquarium
variants.definition: Aquarium.

variants.name: area
variants.definition: The area within which users can expect to reach the broadcast service.

variants.name: areaServed
variants.definition: The location served by this contact point (e.g., a phone number intended for Europeans vs. North Americans or only within the United States).

variants.name: arrivalAirport
variants.definition: The airport where the flight terminates.

variants.name: arrivalBusStop
variants.definition: The stop or station from which the bus arrives.

variants.name: arrivalGate
variants.definition: Identifier of the flight's arrival gate.

variants.name: arrivalPlatform
variants.definition: The platform where the train arrives.

variants.name: arrivalStation
variants.definition: The station where the train trip ends.

variants.name: arrivalTerminal
variants.definition: Identifier of the flight's arrival terminal.

variants.name: arrivalTime
variants.definition: The expected arrival time.

variants.name: ArriveAction
variants.definition: The act of arriving at a place. An agent arrives at a destination from an fromLocation, optionally with participants.

variants.name: artEdition
variants.definition: The number of copies when multiple copies of a piece of artwork are produced - e.g. for a limited edition of 20 prints, 'artEdition' refers to the total number of copies (in this example "20").

variants.name: arterialBranch
variants.definition: The branches that comprise the arterial structure.

variants.name: Artery
variants.definition: A type of blood vessel that specifically carries blood away from the heart.

variants.name: artform
variants.definition: e.g. Painting, Drawing, Sculpture, Print, Photograph, Assemblage, Collage, etc.

variants.name: ArtGallery
variants.definition: An art gallery.

variants.name: Article
variants.definition:
An article, such as a news article or piece of investigative report. Newspapers and magazines have articles of many different types and this is intended to cover them all.

See also blog post.

variants.name: articleBody
variants.definition: The actual body of the article.

variants.name: articleSection
variants.definition: Articles may belong to one or more 'sections' in a magazine or newspaper, such as Sports, Lifestyle, etc.

variants.name: artMedium
variants.definition: The material used. (e.g. Oil, Watercolour, Acrylic, Linoprint, Marble, Cyanotype, Digital, Lithograph, DryPoint, Intaglio, Pastel, Woodcut, Pencil, Mixed Media, etc.)

variants.name: artworkSurface
variants.definition: The supporting materials for the artwork, e.g. Canvas, Paper, Wood, Board, etc.

variants.name: AskAction
variants.definition:
The act of posing a question / favor to someone.

Related actions:

  • ReplyAction: Appears generally as a response to AskAction
.

variants.name: aspect
variants.definition: An aspect of medical practice that is considered on the page, such as 'diagnosis', 'treatment', 'causes', 'prognosis', 'etiology', 'epidemiology', etc.

variants.name: assembly
variants.definition: Library file name e.g., mscorlib.dll, system.web.dll.

variants.name: assemblyVersion
variants.definition: Associated product/technology version. e.g., .NET Framework 4.5.

variants.name: AssessAction
variants.definition: The act of forming one's opinion, reaction or sentiment.

variants.name: AssignAction
variants.definition: The act of allocating an action/event/task to some destination (someone or something).

variants.name: associatedAnatomy
variants.definition: The anatomy of the underlying organ system or structures associated with this entity.

variants.name: associatedArticle
variants.definition: A NewsArticle associated with the Media Object.

variants.name: associatedMedia
variants.definition: A media object that encodes this CreativeWork. This property is a synonym for encoding.

variants.name: associatedPathophysiology
variants.definition: If applicable, a description of the pathophysiology associated with the anatomical system, including potential abnormal changes in the mechanical, physical, and biochemical functions of the system.

variants.name: athlete
variants.definition: A person that acts as performing member of a sports team; a player as opposed to a coach.

variants.name: attendee
variants.definition: A person or organization attending the event.

variants.name: attendees
variants.definition: A person attending the event.

variants.name: Attorney
variants.definition: Professional service: Attorney.

variants.name: audience
variants.definition: An intended audience, i.e. a group for whom something was created.

variants.name: Audience
variants.definition: Intended audience for an item, i.e. the group for whom the item was created.

variants.name: audienceType
variants.definition: The target group associated with a given audience (e.g. veterans, car owners, musicians, etc.).

variants.name: audio

variants.name: AudioObject

variants.name: AuthorizeAction
variants.definition: The act of granting permission to an object.

variants.name: AutoBodyShop
variants.definition: Auto body shop.

variants.name: AutoDealer

variants.name: CreativeWorkSeries
variants.definition:
A CreativeWorkSeries in schema.org is a group of related items, typically but not necessarily of the same kind. CreativeWorkSeries are usually organized into some order, often chronological. Unlike ItemList which is a general purpose data structure for lists of things, the emphasis with CreativeWorkSeries is on published materials (written e.g. books and periodicals, or media such as tv, radio and games).

Specific subtypes are available for describing TVSeries, RadioSeries, MovieSeries, BookSeries, Periodical and VideoGameSeries. In each case, the hasPart / isPartOf properties can be used to relate the CreativeWorkSeries to its parts. The general CreativeWorkSeries type serves largely just to organize these more specific and practical subtypes.

It is common for properties applicable to an item from the series to be usefully applied to the containing group. Schema.org attempts to anticipate some of these cases, but publishers should be free to apply properties of the series parts to the series as a whole wherever they seem appropriate.

A delivery method is a standardized procedure for transferring the product or service to the destination of fulfillment chosen by the customer. variants.name: FollowAction
variants.definition:
The act of forming a personal connection with someone/something (object) unidirectionally/asymmetrically to get updates polled from.

Related actions:

  • BefriendAction: Unlike BefriendAction, FollowAction implies that the connection is *not* necessarily reciprocal.
  • SubscribeAction: Unlike SubscribeAction, FollowAction implies that the follower acts as an active agent constantly/actively polling for updates.
  • RegisterAction: Unlike RegisterAction, FollowAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object.
  • JoinAction: Unlike JoinAction, FollowAction implies that the agent is interested in getting updates from the object.
  • TrackAction: Unlike TrackAction, FollowAction refers to the polling of updates of all aspects of animate objects rather than the location of inanimate objects (e.g. you track a package, but you don't follow it)
.

Use unitText to indicate the unit of measurement, e.g. L/100 km. Note 2: There are two ways of indicating the fuel consumption, fuelConsumption (e.g. 8 liters per 100 km) and fuelEfficiency (e.g. 30 miles per gallon). They are reciprocal.
Note 3: Often, the absolute value is useful only when related to driving speed ("at 80 km/h") or usage pattern ("city traffic"). You can use valueReference to link the value for the fuel consumption to another value.

Note 1: There are unfortunately no standard unit codes for miles per gallon or kilometers per liter.
Use unitText to indicate the unit of measurement, e.g. mpg or km/L. Note 2: There are two ways of indicating the fuel consumption, fuelConsumption (e.g. 8 liters per 100 km) and fuelEfficiency (e.g. 30 miles per gallon). They are reciprocal.
Note 3: Often, the absolute value is useful only when related to driving speed ("at 80 km/h") or usage pattern ("city traffic"). You can use valueReference to link the value for the fuel economy to another value.

variants.name: mainEntity
variants.definition: Indicates the primary entity described in some page or other CreativeWork.

variants.name: mainEntityOfPage
variants.definition:
Indicates a page (or other CreativeWork) for which this thing is the main entity being described.

Many (but not all) pages have a fairly clear primary topic, some entity or thing that the page describes. For example a restaurant's home page might be primarily about that Restaurant, or an event listing page might represent a single event. The mainEntity and mainEntityOfPage properties allow you to explicitly express the relationship between the page and the primary entity.

Related properties include sameAs, about, and url.

The sameAs and url properties are both similar to mainEntityOfPage. The url property should be reserved to refer to more official or authoritative web pages, such as the item’s official website. The sameAs property also relates a thing to a page that indirectly identifies it. Whereas sameAs emphasises well known pages, the mainEntityOfPage property serves more to clarify which of several entities is the main one for that page.

mainEntityOfPage can be used for any page, including those not recognized as authoritative for that entity. For example, for a product, sameAs might refer to a page on the manufacturer’s official site with specs for the product, while mainEntityOfPage might be used on pages within various retailers’ sites giving details for the same product.

about is similar to mainEntity, with two key differences. First, about can refer to multiple entities/topics, while mainEntity should be used for only the primary one. Second, some pages have a primary entity that itself describes some other entity. For example, one web page may display a news article about a particular person. Another page may display a product review for a particular product. In these cases, mainEntity for the pages should refer to the news article or review, respectively, while about would more properly refer to the person or product.

variants.name: MarryAction

variants.definition: e.g. Oil, Watercolour, Acrylic, Linoprint, Marble, Cyanotype, Digital, Lithograph, DryPoint, Intaglio, Pastel, Woodcut, Pencil, Mixed Media, etc.

variants.name: MaximumDoseSchedule

variants.name: maxValue

variants.name: mealService
