variants.name: mechanismOfAction
variants.definition: The specific biochemical interaction through which this drug or supplement produces its pharmacological effect.

variants.name: MediaObject
variants.definition: An image, video, or audio object embedded in a web page. Note that a creative work may have many media objects associated with it on the same web page. For example, a page about a single song (MusicRecording) may have a music video (VideoObject), and a high and low bandwidth audio stream (2 AudioObject's).

variants.name: MedicalAudience
variants.definition: Target audiences for medical web pages. Enumerated type.

variants.name: MedicalCause
variants.definition:
The causative agent(s) that are responsible for the pathophysiologic process that eventually results in a medical condition, symptom or sign. In this schema, unless otherwise specified this is meant to be the proximate cause of the medical condition, symptom or sign. The proximate cause is defined as the causative agent that most directly results in the medical condition, symptom or sign. For example, the HIV virus could be considered a cause of AIDS. Or in a diagnostic context, if a patient fell and sustained a hip fracture and two days later sustained a pulmonary embolism which eventuated in a cardiac arrest, the cause of the cardiac arrest (the proximate cause) would be the pulmonary embolism and not the fall.

Medical causes can include cardiovascular, chemical, dermatologic, endocrine, environmental, gastroenterologic, genetic, hematologic, gynecologic, iatrogenic, infectious, musculoskeletal, neurologic, nutritional, obstetric, oncologic, otolaryngologic, pharmacologic, psychiatric, pulmonary, renal, rheumatologic, toxic, traumatic, or urologic causes; medical conditions can be causes as well.

variants.name: MedicalClinic
variants.definition: A medical clinic.

variants.name: MedicalCode
variants.definition: A code for a medical entity.

variants.name: MedicalCondition
variants.definition: Any condition of the human body that affects the normal functioning of a person, whether physically or mentally. Includes diseases, injuries, disabilities, disorders, syndromes, etc.

variants.name: MedicalConditionStage
variants.definition: A stage of a medical condition, such as 'Stage IIIa'.

variants.name: MedicalContraindication
variants.definition: A condition or factor that serves as a reason to withhold a certain medical therapy. Contraindications can be absolute (there are no reasonable circumstances for undertaking a course of action) or relative (the patient is at higher risk of complications, but that these risks may be outweighed by other considerations or mitigated by other measures).

variants.name: MedicalDevice
variants.definition: Any object used in a medical capacity, such as to diagnose or treat a patient.

variants.name: MedicalDevicePurpose
variants.definition: Categories of medical devices, organized by the purpose or intended use of the device.

variants.name: MedicalEntity
variants.definition: The most generic type of entity related to health and the practice of medicine.

variants.name: MedicalEnumeration
variants.definition: Enumerations related to health and the practice of medicine.

variants.name: MedicalEvidenceLevel
variants.definition: Level of evidence for a medical guideline. Enumerated type.

variants.name: MedicalGuideline
variants.definition: Any recommendation made by a standard society (e.g. ACC/AHA) or consensus statement that denotes how to diagnose and treat a particular condition. Note: this type should be used to tag the actual guideline recommendation; if the guideline recommendation occurs in a larger scholarly article, use MedicalScholarlyArticle to tag the overall article, not this type. Note also: the organization making the recommendation should be captured in the recognizingAuthority base property of MedicalEntity.

variants.name: MedicalGuidelineContraindication
variants.definition: A guideline contraindication that designates a process as harmful and where quality of the data supporting the contraindication is sound.

variants.name: MedicalGuidelineRecommendation
variants.definition: A guideline recommendation that is regarded as efficacious and where quality of the data supporting the recommendation is sound.

variants.name: MedicalImagingTechnique
variants.definition: Any medical imaging modality typically used for diagnostic purposes. Enumerated type.

variants.name: MedicalIndication
variants.definition: A condition or factor that indicates use of a medical therapy, including signs, symptoms, risk factors, anatomical states, etc.

variants.name: MedicalIntangible
variants.definition: A utility class that serves as the umbrella for a number of 'intangible' things in the medical space.

variants.name: MedicalObservationalStudy
variants.definition: An observational study is a type of medical study that attempts to infer the possible effect of a treatment through observation of a cohort of subjects over a period of time. In an observational study, the assignment of subjects into treatment groups versus control groups is outside the control of the investigator. This is in contrast with controlled studies, such as the randomized controlled trials represented by MedicalTrial, where each subject is randomly assigned to a treatment group or a control group before the start of the treatment.

variants.name: MedicalObservationalStudyDesign
variants.definition: Design models for observational medical studies. Enumerated type.

variants.name: MedicalOrganization
variants.definition: A medical organization, such as a doctor's office or clinic.

variants.name: MedicalProcedure
variants.definition: A process of care used in either a diagnostic, therapeutic, or palliative capacity that relies on invasive (surgical), non-invasive, or percutaneous techniques.

variants.name: MedicalProcedureType
variants.definition: An enumeration that describes different types of medical procedures.

variants.name: MedicalRiskCalculator
variants.definition: A complex mathematical calculation requiring an online calculator, used to assess prognosis. Note: use the url property of Thing to record any URLs for online calculators.

variants.name: MedicalRiskEstimator
variants.definition: Any rule set or interactive tool for estimating the risk of developing a complication or condition.

variants.name: MedicalRiskFactor
variants.definition: A risk factor is anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing or contracting a disease, medical condition, or complication.

variants.name: MedicalRiskScore
variants.definition: A simple system that adds up the number of risk factors to yield a score that is associated with prognosis, e.g. CHAD score, TIMI risk score.

variants.name: MedicalScholarlyArticle
variants.definition: A scholarly article in the medical domain.

variants.name: MedicalSign
variants.definition: Any physical manifestation of a person's medical condition discoverable by objective diagnostic tests or physical examination.

variants.name: MedicalSignOrSymptom
variants.definition: Any indication of the existence of a medical condition or disease.

variants.name: medicalSpecialty
variants.definition: A medical specialty of the provider.

variants.name: MedicalSpecialty
variants.definition: Any specific branch of medical science or practice. Medical specialities include clinical specialties that pertain to particular organ systems and their respective disease states, as well as allied health specialties. Enumerated type.

variants.name: MedicalStudy
variants.definition: A medical study is an umbrella type covering all kinds of research studies relating to human medicine or health, including observational studies and interventional trials and registries, randomized, controlled or not. When the specific type of study is known, use one of the extensions of this type, such as MedicalTrial or MedicalObservationalStudy. Also, note that this type should be used to mark up data that describes the study itself; to tag an article that publishes the results of a study, use MedicalScholarlyArticle. Note: use the code property of MedicalEntity to store study IDs, e.g. clinicaltrials.gov ID.

variants.name: MedicalStudyStatus
variants.definition: The status of a medical study. Enumerated type.

variants.name: MedicalSymptom
variants.definition: Any indication of the existence of a medical condition or disease that is apparent to the patient.

variants.name: MedicalTest
variants.definition: Any medical test, typically performed for diagnostic purposes.

variants.name: MedicalTestPanel
variants.definition: Any collection of tests commonly ordered together.

variants.name: MedicalTherapy
variants.definition: Any medical intervention designed to prevent, treat, and cure human diseases and medical conditions, including both curative and palliative therapies. Medical therapies are typically processes of care relying upon pharmacotherapy, behavioral therapy, supportive therapy (with fluid or nutrition for example), or detoxification (e.g. hemodialysis) aimed at improving or preventing a health condition.

variants.name: MedicalTrial
variants.definition: A medical trial is a type of medical study that uses scientific process used to compare the safety and efficacy of medical therapies or medical procedures. In general, medical trials are controlled and subjects are allocated at random to the different treatment and/or control groups.

variants.name: MedicalTrialDesign
variants.definition: Design models for medical trials. Enumerated type.

variants.name: MedicalWebPage
variants.definition: A web page that provides medical information.

variants.name: medicineSystem

variants.name: MedicineSystem
variants.definition: Systems of medical practice.

variants.name: membershipNumber

variants.name: memoryRequirements

variants.name: numberOfPages

For GTIN-related fields, see Check Digit calculator and validation guide from GS1.

variants.name: OfficeEquipmentStore

variants.name: OnDemandEvent

variants.name: openingHours
variants.definition:
The opening hours for a business. Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.
- Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: Mo, Tu, We, Th, Fr, Sa, Su.
- Times are specified using 24:00 time. For example, 3pm is specified as 15:00.
- Here is an example: <time itemprop="openingHours" datetime="Tu,Th 16:00-20:00">Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm</time>.
- If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <time itemprop="openingHours" datetime="Mo-Su">Monday through Sunday, all day</time>.

variants.definition: The date that payment is due.

variants.name: paymentMethod
variants.definition: The name of the credit card or other method of payment for the order.

variants.name: PaymentMethod
variants.definition:
A payment method is a standardized procedure for transferring the monetary amount for a purchase. Payment methods are characterized by the legal and technical structures used, and by the organization or group carrying out the transaction.
Commonly used values:

http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ByBankTransferInAdvance
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ByInvoice
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Cash
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#CheckInAdvance
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#COD
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DirectDebit
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#GoogleCheckout
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PayPal
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PaySwarm

variants.name: paymentMethodId
variants.definition: An identifier for the method of payment used (e.g. the last 4 digits of the credit card).

variants.name: paymentStatus
variants.definition: The status of payment; whether the invoice has been paid or not.

variants.name: paymentUrl
variants.definition: The URL for sending a payment.

variants.name: PeopleAudience
variants.definition: A set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g. who compose an item's target audience.

variants.name: PerformAction
variants.definition: The act of participating in performance arts.

variants.name: PerformanceRole
variants.definition: A PerformanceRole is a Role that some entity places with regard to a theatrical performance, e.g. in a Movie, TVSeries etc.

variants.name: performer
variants.definition: A performer at the event—for example, a presenter, musician, musical group or actor.

variants.name: performerIn
variants.definition: Event that this person is a performer or participant in.

variants.name: performers
variants.definition: The main performer or performers of the event—for example, a presenter, musician, or actor.

variants.name: PerformingArtsTheater
variants.definition: A theater or other performing art center.

variants.name: PerformingGroup
variants.definition: A performance group, such as a band, an orchestra, or a circus.

variants.name: Periodical
variants.definition:
A publication in any medium issued in successive parts bearing numerical or chronological designations and intended, such as a magazine, scholarly journal, or newspaper to continue indefinitely.

See also blog post.

variants.name: permissions
variants.definition: Permission(s) required to run the app (for example, a mobile app may require full internet access or may run only on wifi).

variants.name: Permit
variants.definition: A permit issued by an organization, e.g. a parking pass.

variants.name: permitAudience
variants.definition: The target audience for this permit.

variants.name: Person
variants.definition: A person (alive, dead, undead, or fictional).

variants.name: PetStore
variants.definition: A pet store.

variants.name: Pharmacy
variants.definition: A pharmacy or drugstore.

variants.name: phase
variants.definition: The phase of the trial.

variants.name: photo
variants.definition: A photograph of this place.

variants.name: Photograph
variants.definition: A photograph.

variants.name: PhotographAction
variants.definition: The act of capturing still images of objects using a camera.

variants.name: photos
variants.definition: Photographs of this place.

variants.name: PhysicalActivity
variants.definition: Any bodily activity that enhances or maintains physical fitness and overall health and wellness. Includes activity that is part of daily living and routine, structured exercise, and exercise prescribed as part of a medical treatment or recovery plan.

variants.name: PhysicalActivityCategory
variants.definition: Categories of physical activity, organized by physiologic classification.

variants.name: PhysicalExam
variants.definition: A type of physical examination of a patient performed by a physician. Enumerated type.

variants.name: PhysicalTherapy
variants.definition: A process of progressive physical care and rehabilitation aimed at improving a health condition.

variants.name: Physician
variants.definition: A doctor's office.

variants.name: physiologicalBenefits
variants.definition: Specific physiologic benefits associated to the plan.

variants.name: pickupLocation
variants.definition: Where a taxi will pick up a passenger or a rental car can be picked up.

variants.name: pickupTime
variants.definition: When a taxi will pickup a passenger or a rental car can be picked up.

variants.name: Place
variants.definition: Entities that have a somewhat fixed, physical extension.

variants.name: PlaceOfWorship
variants.definition: Place of worship, such as a church, synagogue, or mosque.

variants.name: PlanAction
variants.definition: The act of planning the execution of an event/task/action/reservation/plan to a future date.

variants.name: PlayAction
variants.definition:
The act of playing/exercising/training/performing for enjoyment, leisure, recreation, Competition or exercise.

Related actions:

  • ListenAction: Unlike ListenAction (which is under ConsumeAction), PlayAction refers to performing for an audience or at an event, rather than consuming music.
  • WatchAction: Unlike WatchAction (which is under ConsumeAction), PlayAction refers to showing/displaying for an audience or at an event, rather than consuming visual content
.

variants.name: playersOnline
variants.definition: Number of players on the server.

variants.name: playerType
variants.definition: Player type required—for example, Flash or Silverlight.

variants.name: Playground
variants.definition: A playground.

variants.name: playMode
variants.definition: Indicates whether this game is multi-player, co-op or single-player.  The game can be marked as multi-player, co-op and single-player at the same time.

variants.name: Plumber
variants.definition: A plumbing service.

variants.name: PoliceStation
variants.definition: A police station.

variants.name: polygon
variants.definition: A polygon is the area enclosed by a point-to-point path for which the starting and ending points are the same. A polygon is expressed as a series of four or more space delimited points where the first and final points are identical.

variants.name: Pond
variants.definition: A pond.

variants.name: population
variants.definition: Any characteristics of the population used in the study, e.g. 'males under 65'.

variants.name: position
variants.definition: The position of an item in a series or sequence of items.

variants.name: possibleComplication
variants.definition: A possible unexpected and unfavorable evolution of a medical condition. Complications may include worsening of the signs or symptoms of the disease, extension of the condition to other organ systems, etc.

variants.name: possibleTreatment
variants.definition: A possible treatment to address this condition, sign or symptom.

variants.name: PostalAddress
variants.definition: The mailing address.

variants.name: postalCode
variants.definition: The postal code. For example, 94043.

variants.name: PostOffice
variants.definition: A post office.

variants.name: postOfficeBoxNumber
variants.definition: The post office box number for PO box addresses.

variants.name: postOp
variants.definition: A description of the postoperative procedures, care, and/or followups for this device.

variants.name: potentialAction
variants.definition: Indicates a potential Action, which describes an idealized action in which this thing would play an 'object' role.

variants.name: predecessorOf
variants.definition: A pointer from a previous, often discontinued variant of the product to its newer variant.

variants.name: pregnancyCategory
variants.definition: Pregnancy category of this drug.

variants.name: pregnancyWarning
variants.definition: Any precaution, guidance, contraindication, etc. related to this drug's use during pregnancy.

variants.name: preOp
variants.definition: A description of the workup, testing, and other preparations required before implanting this device.

variants.name: preparation
variants.definition: Typical preparation that a patient must undergo before having the procedure performed.

variants.name: PrependAction
variants.definition: The act of inserting at the beginning if an ordered collection.

variants.name: prepTime
variants.definition: The length of time it takes to prepare the recipe, in ISO 8601 duration format.

variants.name: Preschool
variants.definition: A preschool.

variants.name: prescribingInfo
variants.definition: Link to prescribing information for the drug.

variants.name: prescriptionStatus
variants.definition: Indicates whether this drug is available by prescription or over-the-counter.

variants.name: PreventionIndication
variants.definition: An indication for preventing an underlying condition, symptom, etc.

variants.name: previousItem
variants.definition: A link to the ListItem that preceeds the current one.

variants.name: previousStartDate
variants.definition: Used in conjunction with eventStatus for rescheduled or cancelled events. This property contains the previously scheduled start date. For rescheduled events, the startDate property should be used for the newly scheduled start date. In the (rare) case of an event that has been postponed and rescheduled multiple times, this field may be repeated.

variants.name: price
variants.definition:
The offer price of a product, or of a price component when attached to PriceSpecification and its subtypes.

Usage guidelines:
  • Use the priceCurrency property (with ISO 4217 codes e.g. "USD") instead of including ambiguous symbols such as '$' in the value.
  • Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.
  • Note that both RDFa and Microdata syntax allow the use of a "content=" attribute for publishing simple machine-readable values alongside more human-friendly formatting.
  • Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similiar Unicode symbols.

variants.name: priceCurrency
variants.definition: The currency (in 3-letter ISO 4217 format) of the price or a price component, when attached to PriceSpecification and its subtypes.

variants.name: priceRange
variants.definition: The price range of the business, for example $$$.

variants.name: priceSpecification
variants.definition: One or more detailed price specifications, indicating the unit price and delivery or payment charges.

variants.name: PriceSpecification
variants.definition: A structured value representing a monetary amount. Typically, only the subclasses of this type are used for markup.

variants.name: priceType
variants.definition: A short text or acronym indicating multiple price specifications for the same offer, e.g. SRP for the suggested retail price or INVOICE for the invoice price, mostly used in the car industry.

variants.name: priceValidUntil
variants.definition: The date after which the price is no longer available.

variants.name: primaryImageOfPage
variants.definition: Indicates the main image on the page.

variants.name: primaryPrevention
variants.definition: A preventative therapy used to prevent an initial occurrence of the medical condition, such as vaccination.

variants.name: printColumn
variants.definition: The number of the column in which the NewsArticle appears in the print edition.

variants.name: printEdition
variants.definition: The edition of the print product in which the NewsArticle appears.

variants.name: printPage
variants.definition: If this NewsArticle appears in print, this field indicates the name of the page on which the article is found. Please note that this field is intended for the exact page name (e.g. A5, B18).

variants.name: printSection
variants.definition: If this NewsArticle appears in print, this field indicates the print section in which the article appeared.

variants.name: procedure
variants.definition: A description of the procedure involved in setting up, using, and/or installing the device.

variants.name: procedureType
variants.definition: The type of procedure, for example Surgical, Noninvasive, or Percutaneous.

variants.name: processingTime
variants.definition: Estimated processing time for the service using this channel.

variants.name: processorRequirements
variants.definition: Processor architecture required to run the application (e.g. IA64).

variants.name: producer
variants.definition: The person or organization who produced the work (e.g. music album, movie, tv/radio series etc.).

variants.name: produces
variants.definition: The tangible thing generated by the service, e.g. a passport, permit, etc.

variants.name: Product
variants.definition: Any offered product or service. For example: a pair of shoes; a concert ticket; the rental of a car; a haircut; or an episode of a TV show streamed online.

variants.name: productID
variants.definition: The product identifier, such as ISBN. For example: <meta itemprop='productID' content='isbn:123-456-789'/>.

variants.name: productionCompany
variants.definition: The production company or studio responsible for the item e.g. series, video game, episode etc.

variants.name: productionDate
variants.definition: The date of production of the item, e.g. vehicle.

variants.name: ProductModel
variants.definition: A datasheet or vendor specification of a product (in the sense of a prototypical description).

variants.name: productSupported
variants.definition: The product or service this support contact point is related to (such as product support for a particular product line). This can be a specific product or product line (e.g. "iPhone") or a general category of products or services (e.g. "smartphones").

variants.name: ProfessionalService
variants.definition: Provider of professional services.

variants.name: proficiencyLevel
variants.definition: Proficiency needed for this content; expected values: 'Beginner', 'Expert'.

variants.name: ProfilePage
variants.definition: Web page type: Profile page.

variants.name: ProgramMembership
variants.definition: Used to describe membership in a loyalty programs (e.g. "StarAliance"), traveler clubs (e.g. "AAA"), purchase clubs ("Safeway Club"), etc.

variants.name: programMembershipUsed
variants.definition: Any membership in a frequent flyer, hotel loyalty program, etc. being applied to the reservation.

variants.name: programmingLanguage
variants.definition: The computer programming language.

variants.name: programmingModel
variants.definition: Indicates whether API is managed or unmanaged.

variants.name: programName
variants.definition: The program providing the membership.

variants.name: Property
variants.definition: A property, used to indicate attributes and relationships of some Thing; equivalent to rdf:Property.

variants.name: propertyID
variants.definition:
A commonly used identifier for the characteristic represented by the property, e.g. a manufacturer or a standard code for a property. propertyID can be
(1) a prefixed string, mainly meant to be used with standards for product properties; (2) a site-specific, non-prefixed string (e.g. the primary key of the property or the vendor-specific id of the property), or (3)
a URL indicating the type of the property, either pointing to an external vocabulary, or a Web resource that describes the property (e.g. a glossary entry).
Standards bodies should promote a standard prefix for the identifiers of properties from their standards.

variants.name: PropertyValue
variants.definition:
A property-value pair, e.g. representing a feature of a product or place. Use the 'name' property for the name of the property. If there is an additional human-readable version of the value, put that into the 'description' property.

Always use specific schema.org properties when a) they exist and b) you can populate them. Using PropertyValue as a substitute will typically not trigger the same effect as using the original, specific property.

variants.name: PropertyValueSpecification
variants.definition: A Property value specification.

variants.name: proprietaryName
variants.definition: Proprietary name given to the diet plan, typically by its originator or creator.

variants.name: proteinContent
variants.definition: The number of grams of protein.

variants.name: provider
variants.definition: The service provider, service operator, or service performer; the goods producer. Another party (a seller) may offer those services or goods on behalf of the provider. A provider may also serve as the seller.

variants.name: providesBroadcastService
variants.definition: The BroadcastService offered on this channel.

variants.name: providesService
variants.definition: The service provided by this channel.

variants.name: PsychologicalTreatment
variants.definition: A process of care relying upon counseling, dialogue, communication, verbalization aimed at improving a mental health condition.

variants.name: publication
variants.definition: A publication event associated with the item.

variants.name: PublicationEvent
variants.definition: A PublicationEvent corresponds indifferently to the event of publication for a CreativeWork of any type e.g. a broadcast event, an on-demand event, a book/journal publication via a variety of delivery media.

variants.name: PublicationIssue
variants.definition:
A part of a successively published publication such as a periodical or publication volume, often numbered, usually containing a grouping of works such as articles.

See also blog post.

variants.name: publicationType
variants.definition: The type of the medical article, taken from the US NLM MeSH <a href=http://www.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/pubtypes.html>publication type catalog.

variants.name: PublicationVolume
variants.definition:
A part of a successively published publication such as a periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered. It may represent a time span, such as a year.

See also blog post.

variants.name: PublicSwimmingPool
variants.definition: A public swimming pool.

variants.name: publishedOn
variants.definition: A broadcast service associated with the publication event.

variants.name: publisher
variants.definition: The publisher of the creative work.

variants.name: publishingPrinciples
variants.definition: Link to page describing the editorial principles of the organization primarily responsible for the creation of the CreativeWork.

variants.name: purchaseDate
variants.definition: The date the item e.g. vehicle was purchased by the current owner.

variants.name: purpose
variants.definition: A goal towards an action is taken. Can be concrete or abstract.

variants.name: QAPage
variants.definition: A QAPage is a WebPage focussed on a specific Question and its Answer(s), e.g. in a question answering site or documenting Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).

variants.name: qualifications
variants.definition: Specific qualifications required for this role.

variants.name: QualitativeValue
variants.definition: A predefined value for a product characteristic, e.g. the power cord plug type "US" or the garment sizes "S", "M", "L", and "XL".

variants.name: QuantitativeValue
variants.definition: A point value or interval for product characteristics and other purposes.

variants.name: Quantity
variants.definition: Quantities such as distance, time, mass, weight, etc. Particular instances of say Mass are entities like '3 Kg' or '4 milligrams'.

variants.name: query
variants.definition: A sub property of instrument. The query used on this action.

variants.name: quest
variants.definition: The task that a player-controlled character, or group of characters may complete in order to gain a reward.

variants.name: question
variants.definition: A sub property of object. A question.

variants.name: Question
variants.definition: A specific question - e.g. from a user seeking answers online, or collected in a Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) document.

variants.name: QuoteAction
variants.definition: An agent quotes/estimates/appraises an object/product/service with a price at a location/store.

variants.name: RadiationTherapy
variants.definition: A process of care using radiation aimed at improving a health condition.

variants.name: RadioChannel
variants.definition: A unique instance of a radio BroadcastService on a CableOrSatelliteService lineup.

variants.name: RadioClip
variants.definition: A short radio program or a segment/part of a radio program.

variants.name: RadioEpisode
variants.definition: A radio episode which can be part of a series or season.

variants.name: RadioSeason
variants.definition: Season dedicated to radio broadcast and associated online delivery.

variants.name: RadioSeries
variants.definition: CreativeWorkSeries dedicated to radio broadcast and associated online delivery.

variants.name: RadioStation
variants.definition: A radio station.

variants.name: rangeIncludes
variants.definition: Relates a property to a class that constitutes (one of) the expected type(s) for values of the property.

variants.name: Rating
variants.definition: A rating is an evaluation on a numeric scale, such as 1 to 5 stars.

variants.name: ratingCount
variants.definition: The count of total number of ratings.

variants.name: ratingValue
variants.definition: The rating for the content.

variants.name: ReactAction
variants.definition: The act of responding instinctively and emotionally to an object, expressing a sentiment.

variants.name: ReadAction
variants.definition: The act of consuming written content.

variants.name: readonlyValue
variants.definition: Whether or not a property is mutable.  Default is false. Specifying this for a property that also has a value makes it act similar to a "hidden" input in an HTML form.

variants.name: realEstateAgent
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The real estate agent involved in the action.

variants.name: RealEstateAgent
variants.definition: A real-estate agent.

variants.name: RearWheelDriveConfiguration
variants.definition: Real-wheel drive is a transmission layout where the engine drives the rear wheels.

variants.name: ReceiveAction
variants.definition:
The act of physically/electronically taking delivery of an object thathas been transferred from an origin to a destination. Reciprocal of SendAction.

Related actions:

  • SendAction: The reciprocal of ReceiveAction.
  • TakeAction: Unlike TakeAction, ReceiveAction does not imply that the ownership has been transfered (e.g. I can receive a package, but it does not mean the package is now mine)
.

variants.name: recipe
variants.definition: A sub property of instrument. The recipe/instructions used to perform the action.

variants.name: Recipe
variants.definition: A recipe.

variants.name: recipeCategory
variants.definition: The category of the recipe—for example, appetizer, entree, etc.

variants.name: recipeCuisine
variants.definition: The cuisine of the recipe (for example, French or Ethiopian).

variants.name: recipeIngredient
variants.definition: A single ingredient used in the recipe, e.g. sugar, flour or garlic.

variants.name: recipeInstructions
variants.definition: A step or instruction involved in making the recipe.

variants.name: recipeYield
variants.definition: The quantity produced by the recipe (for example, number of people served, number of servings, etc).

variants.name: recipient
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The participant who is at the receiving end of the action.

variants.name: recognizingAuthority
variants.definition: If applicable, the organization that officially recognizes this entity as part of its endorsed system of medicine.

variants.name: recommendationStrength
variants.definition: Strength of the guideline's recommendation (e.g. 'class I').

variants.name: RecommendedDoseSchedule
variants.definition: A recommended dosing schedule for a drug or supplement as prescribed or recommended by an authority or by the drug/supplement's manufacturer. Capture the recommending authority in the recognizingAuthority property of MedicalEntity.

variants.name: recommendedIntake
variants.definition: Recommended intake of this supplement for a given population as defined by a specific recommending authority.

variants.name: recordedAs
variants.definition: An audio recording of the work.

variants.name: recordedAt
variants.definition: The Event where the CreativeWork was recorded. The CreativeWork may capture all or part of the event.

variants.name: recordedIn
variants.definition: The CreativeWork that captured all or part of this Event.

variants.name: recordingOf
variants.definition: The composition this track is a recording of.

variants.name: recordLabel
variants.definition: The label that issued the release.

variants.name: RecyclingCenter
variants.definition: A recycling center.

variants.name: referencesOrder
variants.definition: The Order(s) related to this Invoice. One or more Orders may be combined into a single Invoice.

variants.name: regionDrained
variants.definition: The anatomical or organ system drained by this vessel; generally refers to a specific part of an organ.

variants.name: regionsAllowed
variants.definition: The regions where the media is allowed. If not specified, then it's assumed to be allowed everywhere. Specify the countries in ISO 3166 format.

variants.name: RegisterAction
variants.definition:
The act of registering to be a user of a service, product or web page.

Related actions:

  • JoinAction: Unlike JoinAction, RegisterAction implies you are registering to be a user of a service, *not* a group/team of people.
  • FollowAction: Unlike FollowAction, RegisterAction doesn't imply that the agent is expecting to poll for updates from the object.
  • SubscribeAction: Unlike SubscribeAction, RegisterAction doesn't imply that the agent is expecting updates from the object
.

variants.name: RejectAction
variants.definition:
The act of rejecting to/adopting an object.

Related actions:

  • AcceptAction: The antonym of RejectAction
.

variants.name: relatedAnatomy
variants.definition: Anatomical systems or structures that relate to the superficial anatomy.

variants.name: relatedCondition
variants.definition: A medical condition associated with this anatomy.

variants.name: relatedDrug
variants.definition: Any other drug related to this one, for example commonly-prescribed alternatives.

variants.name: relatedLink
variants.definition: A link related to this web page, for example to other related web pages.

variants.name: relatedStructure
variants.definition: Related anatomical structure(s) that are not part of the system but relate or connect to it, such as vascular bundles associated with an organ system.

variants.name: relatedTherapy
variants.definition: A medical therapy related to this anatomy.

variants.name: relatedTo
variants.definition: The most generic familial relation.

variants.name: releaseDate
variants.definition: The release date of a product or product model. This can be used to distinguish the exact variant of a product.

variants.name: releasedEvent
variants.definition: The place and time the release was issued, expressed as a PublicationEvent.

variants.name: releaseNotes
variants.definition: Description of what changed in this version.

variants.name: releaseOf
variants.definition: The album this is a release of.

variants.name: relevantSpecialty
variants.definition: If applicable, a medical specialty in which this entity is relevant.

variants.name: RentAction
variants.definition: The act of giving money in return for temporary use, but not ownership, of an object such as a vehicle or property. For example, an agent rents a property from a landlord in exchange for a periodic payment.

variants.name: RentalCarReservation
variants.definition: A reservation for a rental car.Note: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations.

variants.name: RentalVehicleUsage
variants.definition: Indicates the usage of the vehicle as a rental car.

variants.name: repetitions
variants.definition: Number of times one should repeat the activity.

variants.name: ReplaceAction
variants.definition: The act of editing a recipient by replacing an old object with a new object.

variants.name: replacee
variants.definition: A sub property of object. The object that is being replaced.

variants.name: replacer
variants.definition: A sub property of object. The object that replaces.

variants.name: ReplyAction
variants.definition:
The act of responding to a question/message asked/sent by the object. Related to AskAction.

Related actions:

  • AskAction: Appears generally as an origin of a ReplyAction
.

variants.name: replyToUrl
variants.definition: The URL at which a reply may be posted to the specified UserComment.

variants.name: ReportedDoseSchedule
variants.definition: A patient-reported or observed dosing schedule for a drug or supplement.

variants.name: representativeOfPage
variants.definition: Indicates whether this image is representative of the content of the page.

variants.name: requiredGender
variants.definition: Audiences defined by a person's gender.

variants.name: requiredMaxAge
variants.definition: Audiences defined by a person's maximum age.

variants.name: requiredMinAge
variants.definition: Audiences defined by a person's minimum age.

variants.name: requirements
variants.definition: Component dependency requirements for application. This includes runtime environments and shared libraries that are not included in the application distribution package, but required to run the application (Examples: DirectX, Java or .NET runtime).

variants.name: requiresSubscription
variants.definition: Indicates if use of the media require a subscription (either paid or free). Allowed values are true or false (note that an earlier version had 'yes', 'no').

variants.name: Reservation
variants.definition: Describes a reservation for travel, dining or an event. Some reservations require tickets.Note: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, restaurant reservations, flights, or rental cars, use http://schema.org/Offer.

variants.name: reservationFor
variants.definition: The thing -- flight, event, restaurant,etc. being reserved.

variants.name: reservationId
variants.definition: A unique identifier for the reservation.

variants.name: ReservationPackage
variants.definition: A group of multiple reservations with common values for all sub-reservations.

variants.name: reservationStatus
variants.definition: The current status of the reservation.

variants.name: ReservationStatusType
variants.definition: Enumerated status values for Reservation.

variants.name: ReserveAction
variants.definition:
Reserving a concrete object.

Related actions:

  • ScheduleAction: Unlike ScheduleAction, ReserveAction reserves concrete objects (e.g. a table, a hotel) towards a time slot / spatial allocation
.

variants.name: reservedTicket
variants.definition: A ticket associated with the reservation.

variants.name: Reservoir
variants.definition: A reservoir of water, typically an artificially created lake, like the Lake Kariba reservoir.

variants.name: Residence
variants.definition: The place where a person lives.

variants.name: responsibilities
variants.definition: Responsibilities associated with this role.

variants.name: Restaurant
variants.definition: A restaurant.

variants.name: restPeriods
variants.definition: How often one should break from the activity.

variants.name: result
variants.definition: The result produced in the action. e.g. John wrote *a book*.

variants.name: resultComment
variants.definition: A sub property of result. The Comment created or sent as a result of this action.

variants.name: SuperficialAnatomy
variants.definition: Anatomical features that can be observed by sight (without dissection), including the form and proportions of the human body as well as surface landmarks that correspond to deeper subcutaneous structures. Superficial anatomy plays an important role in sports medicine, phlebotomy, and other medical specialties as underlying anatomical structures can be identified through surface palpation. For example, during back surgery, superficial anatomy can be used to palpate and count vertebrae to find the site of incision. Or in phlebotomy, superficial anatomy can be used to locate an underlying vein; for example, the median cubital vein can be located by palpating the borders of the cubital fossa (such as the epicondyles of the humerus) and then looking for the superficial signs of the vein, such as size, prominence, ability to refill after depression, and feel of surrounding tissue support. As another example, in a subluxation (dislocation) of the glenohumeral joint, the bony structure becomes pronounced with the deltoid muscle failing to cover the glenohumeral joint allowing the edges of the scapula to be superficially visible. Here, the superficial anatomy is the visible edges of the scapula, implying the underlying dislocation of the joint (the related anatomical structure).

variants.name: transcript
variants.definition: If this MediaObject is an AudioObject or VideoObject, the transcript of that object.

variants.name: transFatContent
variants.definition: The number of grams of trans fat.

variants.name: TransferAction
variants.definition: The act of transferring/moving (abstract or concrete) animate or inanimate objects from one place to another.

variants.name: translator
variants.definition: Organization or person who adapts a creative work to different languages, regional differences and technical requirements of a target market.

variants.name: transmissionMethod
variants.definition: How the disease spreads, either as a route or vector, for example 'direct contact', 'Aedes aegypti', etc.

variants.name: TravelAction
variants.definition: The act of traveling from an fromLocation to a destination by a specified mode of transport, optionally with participants.

variants.name: TravelAgency
variants.definition: A travel agency.

variants.name: TreatmentIndication
variants.definition: An indication for treating an underlying condition, symptom, etc.

variants.name: trialDesign
variants.definition: Specifics about the trial design (enumerated).

variants.name: tributary
variants.definition: The anatomical or organ system that the vein flows into; a larger structure that the vein connects to.

variants.name: True
variants.definition: The boolean value true.

variants.name: TVClip
variants.definition: A short TV program or a segment/part of a TV program.

variants.name: TVEpisode
variants.definition: A TV episode which can be part of a series or season.

variants.name: TVSeason
variants.definition: Season dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery.

variants.name: TVSeries
variants.definition: CreativeWorkSeries dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery.

variants.name: TypeAndQuantityNode
variants.definition: A structured value indicating the quantity, unit of measurement, and business function of goods included in a bundle offer.

variants.name: typeOfGood
variants.definition: The product that this structured value is referring to.

variants.name: typicalAgeRange
variants.definition: The typical expected age range, e.g. '7-9', '11-'.

variants.name: typicalTest
variants.definition: A medical test typically performed given this condition.

variants.name: underName
variants.definition: The person or organization the reservation or ticket is for.

variants.name: unitCode
variants.definition: The unit of measurement given using the UN/CEFACT Common Code (3 characters) or a URL. Other codes than the UN/CEFACT Common Code may be used with a prefix followed by a colon.

variants.name: UnitPriceSpecification
variants.definition: The price asked for a given offer by the respective organization or person.

variants.name: unitText
variants.definition: A string or text indicating the unit of measurement. Useful if you cannot provide a standard unit code for unitCode.

variants.name: UnRegisterAction
variants.definition:
The act of un-registering from a service.

Related actions:

  • RegisterAction: antonym of UnRegisterAction.
  • Leave: Unlike LeaveAction, UnRegisterAction implies that you are unregistering from a service you werer previously registered, rather than leaving a team/group of people
.

variants.name: unsaturatedFatContent
variants.definition: The number of grams of unsaturated fat.

variants.name: UpdateAction
variants.definition: The act of managing by changing/editing the state of the object.

variants.name: uploadDate
variants.definition: Date when this media object was uploaded to this site.

variants.name: upvoteCount
variants.definition: The number of upvotes this question, answer or comment has received from the community.

variants.name: url
variants.definition: URL of the item.

variants.name: URL
variants.definition: Data type: URL.

variants.name: urlTemplate
variants.definition: An url template (RFC6570) that will be used to construct the target of the execution of the action.

variants.name: UseAction
variants.definition: The act of applying an object to its intended purpose.

variants.name: usedToDiagnose
variants.definition: A condition the test is used to diagnose.

variants.name: UserBlocks
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use Action-based vocabulary, alongside types such as Comment.

variants.name: UserCheckins
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use Action-based vocabulary, alongside types such as Comment.

variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use Action-based vocabulary, alongside types such as Comment.

variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use Action-based vocabulary, alongside types such as Comment.

variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use Action-based vocabulary, alongside types such as Comment.

variants.name: UserTweets
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use Action-based vocabulary, alongside types such as Comment.

variants.name: usesDevice
variants.definition: Device used to perform the test.

variants.name: validFor
variants.definition: The time validity of the permit.

variants.name: validFrom
variants.definition: The date when the item becomes valid.

variants.name: validIn
variants.definition: The geographic area where the permit is valid.

variants.name: validThrough
variants.definition: The end of the validity of offer, price specification, or opening hours data.

variants.name: validUntil
variants.definition: The date when the item is no longer valid.

variants.name: value
variants.definition: The value of the quantitative value or property value node. For QuantitativeValue, the recommended type for values is 'Number'. For PropertyValue, it can be 'Text;', 'Number', 'Boolean', or 'StructuredValue'.

variants.name: valueAddedTaxIncluded
variants.definition: Specifies whether the applicable value-added tax (VAT) is included in the price specification or not.

variants.name: valueMaxLength
variants.definition: Specifies the allowed range for number of characters in a literal value.

variants.name: valueMinLength
variants.definition: Specifies the minimum allowed range for number of characters in a literal value.

variants.name: valueName
variants.definition: Indicates the name of the PropertyValueSpecification to be used in URL templates and form encoding in a manner analogous to HTML's input@name.

variants.name: valuePattern
variants.definition: Specifies a regular expression for testing literal values according to the HTML spec.

variants.name: valueReference
variants.definition: A pointer to a secondary value that provides additional information on the original value, e.g. a reference temperature.

variants.name: valueRequired
variants.definition: Whether the property must be filled in to complete the action.  Default is false.

variants.name: vatID
variants.definition: The Value-added Tax ID of the organization or person.

variants.name: Vehicle
variants.definition: A vehicle is a device that is designed or used to transport people or cargo over land, water, air, or through space.

variants.name: vehicleConfiguration
variants.definition: A short text indicating the configuration of the vehicle, e.g. '5dr hatchback ST 2.5 MT 225 hp' or 'limited edition'.

variants.name: vehicleEngine
variants.definition: Information about the engine or engines of the vehicle.

variants.name: vehicleIdentificationNumber
variants.definition: The Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) is a unique serial number used by the automotive industry to identify individual motor vehicles.

variants.name: vehicleInteriorColor
variants.definition: The color or color combination of the interior of the vehicle.

variants.name: vehicleInteriorType
variants.definition: The type or material of the interior of the vehicle (e.g. synthetic fabric, leather, wood, etc.). While most interior types are characterized by the material used, an interior type can also be based on vehicle usage or target audience.

variants.name: vehicleModelDate
variants.definition: The release date of a vehicle model (often used to differentiate versions of the same make and model).

variants.name: vehicleSeatingCapacity
variants.definition:
The number of passengers that can be seated in the vehicle, both in terms of the physical space available, and in terms of limitations set by law.
Typical unit code(s): C62 for persons

variants.name: vehicleSpecialUsage
variants.definition: Indicates whether the vehicle has been used for special purposes, like commercial rental, driving school, or as a taxi. The legislation in many countries requires this information to be revealed when offering a car for sale.

variants.name: vehicleTransmission
variants.definition: The type of component used for transmitting the power from a rotating power source to the wheels or other relevant component(s) ("gearbox" for cars).

variants.name: Vein
variants.definition: A type of blood vessel that specifically carries blood to the heart.

variants.name: vendor
variants.definition: 'vendor' is an earlier term for 'seller'.

variants.name: version
variants.definition: The version of the CreativeWork embodied by a specified resource.

variants.name: Vessel
variants.definition: A component of the human body circulatory system comprised of an intricate network of hollow tubes that transport blood throughout the entire body.

variants.name: VeterinaryCare
variants.definition: A vet's office.

variants.name: video
variants.definition: An embedded video object.

variants.name: videoFormat
variants.definition: The type of screening or video broadcast used (e.g. IMAX, 3D, SD, HD, etc.).

variants.name: videoFrameSize
variants.definition: The frame size of the video.

variants.name: VideoGallery
variants.definition: Web page type: Video gallery page.

variants.name: VideoGame
variants.definition: A video game is an electronic game that involves human interaction with a user interface to generate visual feedback on a video device.

variants.name: VideoGameClip
variants.definition: A short segment/part of a video game.

variants.name: VideoGameSeries
variants.definition: A video game series.

variants.name: VideoObject
variants.definition: A video file.

variants.name: videoQuality
variants.definition: The quality of the video.

variants.name: ViewAction
variants.definition: The act of consuming static visual content.

variants.name: VisualArtsEvent
variants.definition: Event type: Visual arts event.

variants.name: VisualArtwork
variants.definition: A work of art that is primarily visual in character.

variants.name: Volcano
variants.definition: A volcano, like Fuji san.

variants.name: volumeNumber
variants.definition: Identifies the volume of publication or multi-part work; for example, "iii" or "2".

variants.name: VoteAction
variants.definition: The act of expressing a preference from a fixed/finite/structured set of choices/options.

variants.name: WantAction
variants.definition: The act of expressing a desire about the object. An agent wants an object.

variants.name: warning
variants.definition: Any FDA or other warnings about the drug (text or URL).

variants.name: warranty
variants.definition: The warranty promise(s) included in the offer.

variants.name: warrantyPromise
variants.definition: The warranty promise(s) included in the offer.

variants.name: WarrantyPromise
variants.definition: A structured value representing the duration and scope of services that will be provided to a customer free of charge in case of a defect or malfunction of a product.

variants.name: warrantyScope
variants.definition: The scope of the warranty promise.

variants.name: WarrantyScope
variants.definition:
A range of of services that will be provided to a customer free of charge in case of a defect or malfunction of a product.
Commonly used values:

http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Labor-BringIn
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PartsAndLabor-BringIn
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PartsAndLabor-PickUp

variants.name: WatchAction
variants.definition: The act of consuming dynamic/moving visual content.

variants.name: Waterfall
variants.definition: A waterfall, like Niagara.

variants.name: WearAction
variants.definition: The act of dressing oneself in clothing.

variants.name: WebApplication
variants.definition: Web applications.

variants.name: webCheckinTime
variants.definition: The time when a passenger can check into the flight online.

variants.name: WebPage
variants.definition: A web page. Every web page is implicitly assumed to be declared to be of type WebPage, so the various properties about that webpage, such as breadcrumb may be used. We recommend explicit declaration if these properties are specified, but if they are found outside of an itemscope, they will be assumed to be about the page.

variants.name: WebPageElement
variants.definition: A web page element, like a table or an image.

variants.name: WebSite
variants.definition: A WebSite is a set of related web pages and other items typically served from a single web domain and accessible via URLs.

variants.name: weight
variants.definition: The weight of the product or person.

variants.name: WholesaleStore
variants.definition: A wholesale store.

variants.name: width
variants.definition: The width of the item.

variants.name: WinAction
variants.definition: The act of achieving victory in a competitive activity.

variants.name: Winery
variants.definition: A winery.

variants.name: winner
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The winner of the action.

variants.name: wordCount
variants.definition: The number of words in the text of the Article.

variants.name: workExample
variants.definition: Example/instance/realization/derivation of the concept of this creative work. eg. The paperback edition, first edition, or eBook.

variants.name: workHours
variants.definition: The typical working hours for this job (e.g. 1st shift, night shift, 8am-5pm).

variants.name: workload
variants.definition: Quantitative measure of the physiologic output of the exercise; also referred to as energy expenditure.

variants.name: workLocation
variants.definition: A contact location for a person's place of work.

variants.name: workPerformed
variants.definition: A work performed in some event, for example a play performed in a TheaterEvent.

variants.name: workPresented
variants.definition: The movie presented during this event.

variants.name: worksFor
variants.definition: Organizations that the person works for.

variants.name: worstRating
variants.definition: The lowest value allowed in this rating system. If worstRating is omitted, 1 is assumed.

variants.name: WPAdBlock
variants.definition: An advertising section of the page.

variants.name: WPFooter
variants.definition: The footer section of the page.

variants.name: WPHeader
variants.definition: The header section of the page.

variants.name: WPSideBar
variants.definition: A sidebar section of the page.

variants.name: WriteAction
variants.definition: The act of authoring written creative content.

variants.name: yearlyRevenue
variants.definition: The size of the business in annual revenue.

variants.name: yearsInOperation
variants.definition: The age of the business.

variants.name: ZoneBoardingPolicy
variants.definition: The airline boards by zones of the plane.

variants.name: Zoo
variants.definition: A zoo.

variants.name: abridged
variants.definition: Indicates whether the book is an abridged edition.

variants.name: accelerationTime
variants.definition:
The time needed to accelerate the vehicle from a given start velocity to a given target velocity.
Typical unit code(s): SEC for seconds
Note: There are unfortunately no standard unit codes for seconds/0..100 km/h or seconds/0..60 mph. Simply use "SEC" for seconds and indicate the velocities in the name of the QuantitativeValue, or use valueReference with a QuantitativeValue of 0..60 mph or 0..100 km/h to specify the reference speeds.

variants.name: acceptsReservations
variants.definition: Indicates whether a FoodEstablishment accepts reservations. Values can be Boolean, a URL at which reservations can be made or (for backwards compatibility) the strings Yes or No.

variants.name: acrissCode
variants.definition: The ACRISS Car Classification Code is a code used by many car rental companies, for classifying vehicles. ACRISS stands for Association of Car Rental Industry Systems and Standards.

variants.name: artist
variants.definition:
The primary artist for a work 
	in a medium other than pencils or digital line art--for example, if the
	primary artwork is done in watercolors or digital paints.

variants.name: Atlas
variants.definition: A collection or bound volume of maps, charts, plates or tables, physical or in media form illustrating any subject.

variants.name: Audiobook
variants.definition: An audiobook.

variants.name: BlogPosting
variants.definition: A blog post.

variants.name: bodyType
variants.definition: Indicates the design and body style of the vehicle (e.g. station wagon, hatchback, etc.).

variants.name: Bridge
variants.definition: A bridge.

variants.name: BroadcastService
variants.definition: A delivery service through which content is provided via broadcast over the air or online.

variants.name: BusOrCoach
variants.definition: A bus (also omnibus or autobus) is a road vehicle designed to carry passengers. Coaches are luxury busses, usually in service for long distance travel.

variants.name: Chapter
variants.definition: One of the sections into which a book is divided. A chapter usually has a section number or a name.

variants.name: codeSampleType
variants.definition: What type of code sample: full (compile ready) solution, code snippet, inline code, scripts, template.

variants.name: Collection
variants.definition: A created collection of Creative Works or other artefacts.

variants.name: colorist
variants.definition: The individual who adds color to inked drawings.

variants.name: ComicCoverArt
variants.definition: The artwork on the cover of a comic.

variants.name: ComicIssue
variants.definition:
Individual comic issues are serially published as
	part of a larger series. For the sake of consistency, even one-shot issues
	belong to a series comprised of a single issue. All comic issues can be
	uniquely identified by: the combination of the name and volume number of the
	series to which the issue belongs; the issue number; and the variant
	description of the issue (if any).

variants.name: ComicSeries
variants.definition:
A sequential publication of comic stories under a
	unifying title, for example "The Amazing Spider-Man" or "Groo the
	Wanderer".

variants.name: ComicStory
variants.definition:
The term "story" is any indivisible, re-printable
	unit of a comic, including the interior stories, covers, and backmatter. Most
	comics have at least two stories: a cover (ComicCoverArt) and an interior story.

variants.name: coverageEndTime
variants.definition: The time when the live blog will stop covering the Event. Note that coverage may continue after the Event concludes.

variants.name: coverageStartTime
variants.definition: The time when the live blog will begin covering the Event. Note that coverage may begin before the Event's start time. The LiveBlogPosting may also be created before coverage begins.

variants.name: CoverArt
variants.definition: The artwork on the outer surface of a CreativeWork.

variants.name: DateTime
variants.definition: A combination of date and time of day in the form [-]CCYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[Z|(+|-)hh:mm] (see Chapter 5.4 of ISO 8601).

variants.name: DiscussionForumPosting
variants.definition: A posting to a discussion forum.

variants.name: duration
variants.definition: The duration of the item (movie, audio recording, event, etc.) in ISO 8601 date format.

variants.name: emissionsCO2
variants.definition: The CO2 emissions in g/km. The property uses a number instead of a QuantitativeValue, since g/km is the dominant unit of measurement, and there is no UNCEFACT Common Code for g/km.

variants.name: engineDisplacement
variants.definition:
The volume swept by all of the pistons inside the cylinders of an internal combustion engine in a single movement.
Typical unit code(s): CMQ for cubic centimeter, LTR for liters, INQ for cubic inches
Note 1: You can link to information about how the given value has been determined using the valueReference property.
Note 2: You can use minValue and maxValue to indicate ranges.

variants.name: enginePower
variants.definition:
The power of the vehicle's engine. Typical unit code(s): KWT for kilowatt, BHP for brake horsepower, N12 for metric horsepower (PS, with 1 PS = 735,49875 W)
Note 1: There are many different ways of measuring an engine's power. For an overview, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horsepower#Engine_power_test_codes.
Note 2: You can link to information about how the given value has been determined using the valueReference property.
Note 3: You can use minValue and maxValue to indicate ranges.

variants.name: engineType
variants.definition: The type of engine or engines powering the vehicle.

variants.name: fileSize
variants.definition: Size of the application / package (e.g. 18MB). In the absence of a unit (MB, KB etc.), KB will be assumed.

variants.name: fuelCapacity
variants.definition:
The capacity of the fuel tank or in the case of electric cars, the battery. If there are multiple components for storage, this should indicate the total of all storage of the same type.
Typical unit code(s): LTR for liters, GLL of US gallons, GLI for UK / imperial gallons, AMH for ampere-hours (for electrical vehicles)

variants.name: genre
variants.definition: Genre of the creative work or group.

variants.name: GraphicNovel
variants.definition: Book format: GraphicNovel. May represent a bound collection of ComicIssue instances.

variants.name: inker
variants.definition: The individual who traces over the pencil drawings in ink after pencils are complete.

variants.name: inSupportOf
variants.definition: Qualification, candidature, degree, application that Thesis supports.

variants.name: InteractionCounter
variants.definition: A summary of how users have interacted with this CreativeWork. In most cases, authors will use a subtype to specify the specific type of interaction.

variants.name: interactionService
variants.definition: The WebSite or SoftwareApplication where the interactions took place.

variants.name: interactionStatistic
variants.definition: The number of interactions for the CreativeWork using the WebSite or SoftwareApplication. The most specific child type of InteractionCounter should be used.

variants.name: interactionType
variants.definition: The Action representing the type of interaction. For up votes, +1s, etc. use LikeAction. For down votes use DislikeAction. Otherwise, use the most specific Action.

variants.name: letterer
variants.definition: The individual who adds lettering, including speech balloons and sound effects, to artwork.

variants.name: LiveBlogPosting
variants.definition: A blog post intended to provide a rolling textual coverage of an ongoing event through continuous updates.

variants.name: liveBlogUpdate
variants.definition: An update to the LiveBlog.

variants.name: lyrics
variants.definition: The words in the song.

variants.name: mainEntityOfPage
variants.definition:
Indicates a page (or other CreativeWork) for which this thing is the main entity being described.

See background notes for details.

variants.name: meetsEmissionStandard
variants.definition: Indicates that the vehicle meets the respective emission standard.

variants.name: modelDate
variants.definition: The release date of a vehicle model (often used to differentiate versions of the same make and model).

variants.name: Motorcycle
variants.definition: A motorcycle or motorbike is a single-track, two-wheeled motor vehicle.

variants.name: MotorizedBicycle
variants.definition: A motorized bicycle is a bicycle with an attached motor used to power the vehicle, or to assist with pedaling.

variants.name: netWorth
variants.definition: The total financial value of the person as calculated by subtracting assets from liabilities.

variants.name: Newspaper
variants.definition: A publication containing information about varied topics that are pertinent to general information, a geographic area, or a specific subject matter (i.e. business, culture, education). Often published daily.

variants.name: pageEnd
variants.definition: The page on which the work ends; for example "138" or "xvi".

variants.name: pageStart
variants.definition: The page on which the work starts; for example "135" or "xiii".

variants.name: pagination
variants.definition: Any description of pages that is not separated into pageStart and pageEnd; for example, "1-6, 9, 55" or "10-12, 46-49".

variants.name: parentOrganization
variants.definition: The larger organization that this organization is a branch of, if any.

variants.name: payload
variants.definition:
The permitted weight of passengers and cargo, EXCLUDING the weight of the empty vehicle.
Typical unit code(s): KGM for kilogram, LBR for pound
Note 1: Many databases specify the permitted TOTAL weight instead, which is the sum of weight and payload.
Note 2: You can indicate additional information in the name of the QuantitativeValue node.
Note 3: You may also link to a QualitativeValue node that provides additional information using valueReference.
Note 4: Note that you can use minValue and maxValue to indicate ranges.

variants.name: PaymentAutomaticallyApplied
variants.definition: An automatic payment system is in place and will be used.

variants.name: PaymentComplete
variants.definition: The payment has been received and processed.

variants.name: PaymentDeclined
variants.definition: The payee received the payment, but it was declined for some reason.

variants.name: PaymentDue
variants.definition: The payment is due, but still within an acceptable time to be received.

variants.name: paymentDueDate
variants.definition: The date that payment is due.

variants.name: PaymentPastDue
variants.definition: The payment is due and considered late.

variants.name: paymentStatus
variants.definition: The status of payment; whether the invoice has been paid or not.

variants.name: PaymentStatusType
variants.definition: A specific payment status. For example, PaymentDue, PaymentComplete, etc.

variants.name: penciler
variants.definition: The individual who draws the primary narrative artwork.

variants.name: publishedBy
variants.definition: An agent associated with the publication event.

variants.name: publisher
variants.definition: The publisher of the creative work.

variants.name: publisherImprint
variants.definition: The publishing division which published the comic.

variants.name: readBy
variants.definition: A person who reads (performs) the audiobook.

variants.name: Report
variants.definition: A Report generated by governmental or non-governmental organization.

variants.name: reportNumber
variants.definition: The number or other unique designator assigned to a Report by the publishing organization.

variants.name: roofLoad
variants.definition:
The permitted total weight of cargo and installations (e.g. a roof rack) on top of the vehicle.
Typical unit code(s): KGM for kilogram, LBR for pound
Note 1: You can indicate additional information in the name of the QuantitativeValue node.
Note 2: You may also link to a QualitativeValue node that provides additional information using valueReference.
Note 3: Note that you can use minValue and maxValue to indicate ranges.

variants.name: sampleType
variants.definition: What type of sample: full (compile ready) solution, code snippet, inline code, scripts, template.

variants.name: schemaVersion
variants.definition: Indicates (by URL or string) a particular version of a schema used in some CreativeWork. For example, a document could declare a schemaVersion using a URL such as http://schema.org/version/2.0/ if precise indication of schema version was required by some application.

variants.name: seatingCapacity
variants.definition:
The number of passengers that can be seated in the vehicle, both in terms of the physical space available, and in terms of limitations set by law.
Typical unit code(s): C62 for persons

variants.name: sharedContent
variants.definition: A CreativeWork such as an image, video, or audio clip shared as part of this posting.

variants.name: SocialMediaPosting
variants.definition: A post to a social media platform, including blog posts, tweets, Facebook posts, etc.

variants.name: specialUsage
variants.definition: Indicates whether the vehicle has been used for special purposes, like commercial rental, driving school, or as a taxi. The legislation in many countries requires this information to be revealed when offering a car for sale.

variants.name: speed
variants.definition:
The speed range of the vehicle. If the vehicle is powered by an engine, the upper limit of the speed range (indicated by maxValue) should be the maximum speed achievable under regular conditions.
Typical unit code(s): KMH for km/h, HM for mile per hour (0.447 04 m/s), KNT for knot
Note 1: Use minValue and maxValue to indicate the range. Typically, the minimal value is zero.
Note 2: There are many different ways of measuring the speed range. You can link to information about how the given value has been determined using the valueReference property.

variants.name: Thesis
variants.definition: A thesis or dissertation document submitted in support of candidature for an academic degree or professional qualification.

variants.name: tongueWeight
variants.definition:
The permitted vertical load (TWR) of a trailer attached to the vehicle. Also referred to as Tongue Load Rating (TLR) or Vertical Load Rating (VLR).
Typical unit code(s): KGM for kilogram, LBR for pound
Note 1: You can indicate additional information in the name of the QuantitativeValue node.
Note 2: You may also link to a QualitativeValue node that provides additional information using valueReference.
Note 3: Note that you can use minValue and maxValue to indicate ranges.

variants.name: torque
variants.definition:
The torque (turning force) of the vehicle's engine.
Typical unit code(s): NU for newton metre (N m), F17 for pound-force per foot, or F48 for pound-force per inch
Note 1: You can link to information about how the given value has been determined (e.g. reference RPM) using the valueReference property.
Note 2: You can use minValue and maxValue to indicate ranges.

variants.name: trailerWeight
variants.definition:
The permitted weight of a trailer attached to the vehicle.
Typical unit code(s): KGM for kilogram, LBR for pound
Note 1: You can indicate additional information in the name of the QuantitativeValue node.
Note 2: You may also link to a QualitativeValue node that provides additional information using valueReference.
Note 3: Note that you can use minValue and maxValue to indicate ranges.

variants.name: translationOfWork
variants.definition: The work that this work has been translated from. e.g. 物种起源 is a translationOf “On the Origin of Species”

variants.name: translator
variants.definition:
An agent responsible for rendering a translated work from a source work

Organization or person who adapts a creative work to different languages, regional differences and technical requirements of a target market.

variants.name: urlTemplate
variants.definition: A url template (RFC6570) that will be used to construct the target of the execution of the action.

variants.name: userInteractionCount
variants.definition: The number of interactions for the CreativeWork using the WebSite or SoftwareApplication.

variants.name: variantCover
variants.definition:
A description of the variant cover
	for the issue, if the issue is a variant printing. For example, "Bryan Hitch
	Variant Cover" or "2nd Printing Variant".

variants.name: videoFormat
variants.definition: The type of screening or video broadcast used (e.g. IMAX, 3D, SD, HD, etc.).

variants.name: weightTotal
variants.definition:
The permitted total weight of the loaded vehicle, including passengers and cargo and the weight of the empty vehicle.
Typical unit code(s): KGM for kilogram, LBR for pound
Note 1: You can indicate additional information in the name of the QuantitativeValue node.
Note 2: You may also link to a QualitativeValue node that provides additional information using valueReference.
Note 3: Note that you can use minValue and maxValue to indicate ranges.

variants.name: wheelbase
variants.definition:
The distance between the centers of the front and rear wheels.
Typical unit code(s): CMT for centimeters, MTR for meters, INH for inches, FOT for foot/feet

variants.name: workTranslation
variants.definition: A work that is a translation of the content of this work. e.g. 西遊記 has an English workTranslation “Journey to the West”,a German workTranslation “Monkeys Pilgerfahrt” and a Vietnamese  translation Tây du ký bình khảo.

variants.name: AccountingService
variants.definition:
Accountancy business.

As a LocalBusiness it can be described as a provider of one or more Service(s).

variants.name: AchieveAction
variants.definition: The act of accomplishing something via previous efforts. It is an instantaneous action rather than an ongoing process.

variants.name: Action
variants.definition:
An action performed by a direct agent and indirect participants upon a direct object. Optionally happens at a location with the help of an inanimate instrument. The execution of the action may produce a result. Specific action sub-type documentation specifies the exact expectation of each argument/role.

See also blog post and Actions overview document.

variants.name: actionPlatform
variants.definition: The high level platform(s) where the Action can be performed for the given URL. To specify a specific application or operating system instance, use actionApplication.

variants.name: address
variants.definition: Physical address of the item.

variants.name: addressCountry
variants.definition: The country. For example, USA. You can also provide the two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

variants.name: AdministrativeArea
variants.definition: A geographical region, typically under the jurisdiction of a particular government.

variants.name: alumni
variants.definition: Alumni of an organization.

variants.name: alumniOf
variants.definition: An organization that the person is an alumni of.

variants.name: areaServed
variants.definition: The geographic area where a service or offered item is provided.

variants.name: Attorney
variants.definition:
Professional service: Attorney.

This type is deprecated - LegalService is more inclusive and less ambiguous.

variants.name: award
variants.definition: An award won by or for this item.

variants.name: Barcode
variants.definition: An image of a visual machine-readable code such as a barcode or QR code.

variants.name: branchCode
variants.definition:
A short textual code (also called "store code") that uniquely identifies a place of business. The code is typically assigned by the parentOrganization and used in structured URLs.
