For example, in the URL http://www.starbucks.co.uk/store-locator/etc/detail/3047 the code "3047" is a branchCode for a particular branch.

variants.name: broadcastOfEvent
variants.definition: The event being broadcast such as a sporting event or awards ceremony.

variants.name: category
variants.definition: A category for the item. Greater signs or slashes can be used to informally indicate a category hierarchy.

variants.name: containedIn
variants.definition: The basic containment relation between a place and one that contains it.

variants.name: containedInPlace
variants.definition: The basic containment relation between a place and one that contains it.

variants.name: containsPlace
variants.definition: The basic containment relation between a place and another that it contains.

variants.name: countryOfOrigin
variants.definition: The country of the principal offices of the production company or individual responsible for the movie or program.

variants.name: DataFeed
variants.definition: A single feed providing structured information about one or more entities or topics.

variants.name: dataFeedElement
variants.definition: An item within in a data feed. Data feeds may have many elements.

variants.name: DataFeedItem
variants.definition: A single item within a larger data feed.

variants.name: dateCreated
variants.definition: The date on which the CreativeWork was created or the item was added to a DataFeed.

variants.name: dateDeleted
variants.definition: The datetime the item was removed from the DataFeed.

variants.name: dateModified
variants.definition: The date on which the CreativeWork was most recently modified or when the item's entry was modified within a DataFeed.

variants.name: Dentist
variants.definition: A dentist.

variants.name: Electrician
variants.definition: An electrician.

variants.name: elevation
variants.definition: The elevation of a location (WGS 84).

variants.name: eligibleRegion
variants.definition:
The ISO 3166-1 (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) or ISO 3166-2 code, the place, or the GeoShape for the geo-political region(s) for which the offer or delivery charge specification is valid.

See also ineligibleRegion.

variants.name: ExhibitionEvent
variants.definition: Event type: Exhibition event, e.g. at a museum, library, archive, tradeshow, ...

variants.name: fileFormat
variants.definition: Media type (aka MIME format, see IANA site) of the content e.g. application/zip of a SoftwareApplication binary. In cases where a CreativeWork has several media type representations, 'encoding' can be used to indicate each MediaObject alongside particular fileFormat information.

variants.name: GeneralContractor
variants.definition: A general contractor.

variants.name: GeoCircle
variants.definition:
A GeoCircle is a GeoShape representing a circular geographic area. As it is a GeoShape
          it provides the simple textual property 'circle', but also allows the combination of postalCode alongside geoRadius.
          The center of the circle can be indicated via the 'geoMidpoint' property, or more approximately using 'address', 'postalCode'.

variants.name: geoMidpoint
variants.definition: Indicates the GeoCoordinates at the centre of a GeoShape e.g. GeoCircle.

variants.name: geoRadius
variants.definition: Indicates the approximate radius of a GeoCircle (metres unless indicated otherwise via Distance notation).

variants.name: hasOfferCatalog
variants.definition: Indicates an OfferCatalog listing for this Organization, Person, or Service.

variants.name: HomeAndConstructionBusiness
variants.definition:
A construction business.

A HomeAndConstructionBusiness is a LocalBusiness that provides services around homes and buildings.

As a LocalBusiness it can be described as a provider of one or more Service(s).

variants.name: hoursAvailable
variants.definition: The hours during which this service or contact is available.

variants.name: HousePainter
variants.definition: A house painting service.

variants.name: ineligibleRegion
variants.definition:
The ISO 3166-1 (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) or ISO 3166-2 code, the place, or the GeoShape for the geo-political region(s) for which the offer or delivery charge specification is not valid, e.g. a region where the transaction is not allowed.

See also eligibleRegion.

variants.name: item
variants.definition: An entity represented by an entry in a list or data feed (e.g. an 'artist' in a list of 'artists')’.

variants.name: itemOffered
variants.definition: The item being offered.

variants.name: latitude
variants.definition: The latitude of a location. For example 37.42242 (WGS 84).

variants.name: LegalService
variants.definition:
A LegalService is a business that provides legally-oriented services, advice and representation, e.g. law firms.

As a LocalBusiness it can be described as a provider of one or more Service(s).

variants.name: location
variants.definition: The location of for example where the event is happening, an organization is located, or where an action takes place.

variants.name: locationCreated
variants.definition: The location where the CreativeWork was created, which may not be the same as the location depicted in the CreativeWork.

variants.name: Locksmith
variants.definition: A locksmith.

variants.name: longitude
variants.definition: The longitude of a location. For example -122.08585 (WGS 84).

variants.name: Notary
variants.definition: A notary.

variants.name: OfferCatalog
variants.definition: An OfferCatalog is an ItemList that contains related Offers and/or further OfferCatalogs that are offeredBy the same provider.

variants.name: offeredBy
variants.definition: A pointer to the organization or person making the offer.

variants.name: offers
variants.definition: An offer to provide this item—for example, an offer to sell a product, rent the DVD of a movie, perform a service, or give away tickets to an event.

variants.name: Plumber
variants.definition: A plumbing service.

variants.name: postalCode
variants.definition: The postal code. For example, 94043.

variants.name: ProfessionalService
variants.definition:
Original definition: "provider of professional services."

The general ProfessionalService type for local businesses was deprecated due to confusion with Service. For reference, the types that it included were: Dentist, AccountingService, Attorney, Notary, as well as types for several kinds of HomeAndConstructionBusiness: Electrician, GeneralContractor, HousePainter, Locksmith, Plumber, RoofingContractor. LegalService was introduced as a more inclusive supertype of Attorney.

variants.name: providerMobility
variants.definition: Indicates the mobility of a provided service (e.g. 'static', 'dynamic').

variants.name: RoofingContractor
variants.definition: A roofing contractor.

variants.name: seatingCapacity
variants.definition:
The number of persons that can be seated (e.g. in a vehicle), both in terms of the physical space available, and in terms of limitations set by law.
Typical unit code(s): C62 for persons

variants.name: serviceArea
variants.definition: The geographic area where the service is provided.

variants.name: specialUsage
variants.definition: Indicates whether the object has been used for special purposes, like vehicles that have been used for commercial rental, driving school, or as a taxi. The legislation in some countries may require this information to be revealed when offering the item for sale.

variants.name: supportingData
variants.definition: Supporting data for a SoftwareApplication.

variants.name: workFeatured
variants.definition:
A work featured in some event, e.g. exhibited in an ExhibitionEvent.
       Specific subproperties are available for workPerformed (e.g. a play), or a workPresented (a Movie at a ScreeningEvent).

variants.name: accelerationTime
variants.definition:
The time needed to accelerate the vehicle from a given start velocity to a given target velocity.
Typical unit code(s): SEC for seconds

Note: There are unfortunately no standard unit codes for seconds/0..100 km/h or seconds/0..60 mph. Simply use "SEC" for seconds and indicate the velocities in the <a href="name">name</a> of the <a href="QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a>, or use <a href="valueReference">valueReference</a> with a <a href="QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a> of 0..60 mph or 0..100 km/h to specify the reference speeds.

variants.name: acceptedPaymentMethod
variants.definition: The payment method(s) accepted by seller for this offer.

variants.name: accessibilitySummary
variants.definition: A human-readable summary of specific accessibility features or deficiencies, consistent with the other accessibility metadata but expressing subtleties such as "short descriptions are present but long descriptions will be needed for non-visual users" or "short descriptions are present and no long descriptions are needed."

variants.name: accessMode
variants.definition: The human sensory perceptual system or cognitive faculty through which a person may process or perceive information. Expected values include: auditory, tactile, textual, visual, colorDependent, chartOnVisual, chemOnVisual, diagramOnVisual, mathOnVisual, musicOnVisual, textOnVisual.

variants.name: accessModeSufficient
variants.definition: A list of single or combined accessModes that are sufficient to understand all the intellectual content of a resource. Expected values include:  auditory, tactile, textual, visual.

variants.name: AccountingService
variants.definition:
Accountancy business.

As a LocalBusiness it can be described as a provider of one or more Service(s).

variants.name: actor
variants.definition: An actor, e.g. in tv, radio, movie, video games etc., or in an event. Actors can be associated with individual items or with a series, episode, clip.

variants.name: additionalProperty
variants.definition:
A property-value pair representing an additional characteristics of the entitity, e.g. a product feature or another characteristic for which there is no matching property in schema.org.

Note: Publishers should be aware that applications designed to use specific schema.org properties (e.g. http://schema.org/width, http://schema.org/color, http://schema.org/gtin13, ...) will typically expect such data to be provided using those properties, rather than using the generic property/value mechanism.

variants.name: agent
variants.definition: The direct performer or driver of the action (animate or inanimate). e.g. John wrote a book.

variants.name: amount
variants.definition: The amount of money.

variants.name: annualPercentageRate
variants.definition: The annual rate that is charged for borrowing (or made by investing), expressed as a single percentage number that represents the actual yearly cost of funds over the term of a loan. This includes any fees or additional costs associated with the transaction.

variants.name: Article
variants.definition:
An article, such as a news article or piece of investigative report. Newspapers and magazines have articles of many different types and this is intended to cover them all.

  <br/><br/>See also <a href="https://blog.schema.org/2014/09/02/schema-org-support-for-bibliographic-relationships-and-periodicals/">blog post</a>.

variants.name: artist
variants.definition:
The primary artist for a work 
    in a medium other than pencils or digital line art--for example, if the
    primary artwork is done in watercolors or digital paints.

variants.name: Attorney
variants.definition:
Professional service: Attorney.

This type is deprecated - LegalService is more inclusive and less ambiguous.

variants.name: audience
variants.definition: An intended audience, i.e. a group for whom something was created.

variants.name: AudiobookFormat
variants.definition: Book format: Audiobook. This is an enumerated value for use with the bookFormat property. There is also a type 'Audiobook' in the bib extension which includes Audiobook specific properties.

variants.name: availableLanguage
variants.definition: A language someone may use with the item. Please use one of the language codes from the IETF BCP 47 standard. See also inLanguage.

variants.name: BankAccount
variants.definition: A product or service offered by a bank whereby one may deposit, withdraw or transfer money and in some cases be paid interest.

variants.name: baseSalary
variants.definition: The base salary of the job or of an employee in an EmployeeRole.

variants.name: benefitsSummaryUrl
variants.definition: The URL that goes directly to the summary of benefits and coverage for the specific standard plan or plan variation.

variants.name: branchCode
variants.definition:
A short textual code (also called "store code") that uniquely identifies a place of business. The code is typically assigned by the parentOrganization and used in structured URLs.

For example, in the URL http://www.starbucks.co.uk/store-locator/etc/detail/3047 the code "3047" is a branchCode for a particular branch.

variants.name: branchOf
variants.definition: The larger organization that this local business is a branch of, if any. Not to be confused with (anatomical)branch.

variants.name: brand
variants.definition: The brand(s) associated with a product or service, or the brand(s) maintained by an organization or business person.

variants.name: BreadcrumbList
variants.definition:
A BreadcrumbList is an ItemList consisting of a chain of linked Web pages, typically described using at least their URL and their name, and typically ending with the current page.

The 'position' property is used to reconstruct the order of the items in a BreadcrumbList. The convention is that a breadcrumb list has an itemListOrder of ItemListOrderAscending (lower values listed first), and that the first items in this list correspond to the "top" or beginning of the breadcrumb trail, e.g. with a site or section homepage. The specific values of 'position' are not assigned meaning for a BreadcrumbList, but they should be integers, e.g. beginning with '1' for the first item in the list.

variants.name: broadcastFrequency
variants.definition: The frequency used for over-the-air broadcasts.

variants.name: BroadcastFrequencySpecification
variants.definition: The frequency in MHz and the modulation used for a particular BroadcastService.

variants.name: broadcastFrequencyValue
variants.definition: The frequency in MHz for a particular broadcast.

variants.name: broadcastSignalModulation
variants.definition: The modulation (e.g. FM, AM, etc) used by a particular broadcast service

variants.name: BusinessEntityType
variants.definition:
A business entity type is a conceptual entity representing the legal form, the size, the main line of business, the position in the value chain, or any combination thereof, of an organization or business person.
Commonly used values:

http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Business
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Enduser
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PublicInstitution
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Reseller

variants.name: BusinessFunction
variants.definition:
The business function specifies the type of activity or access (i.e., the bundle of rights) offered by the organization or business person through the offer. Typical are sell, rental or lease, maintenance or repair, manufacture / produce, recycle / dispose, engineering / construction, or installation. Proprietary specifications of access rights are also instances of this class.
Commonly used values:

http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ConstructionInstallation
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Dispose
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#LeaseOut
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Maintain
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ProvideService
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Repair
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Sell
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Buy

variants.name: cargoVolume
variants.definition:
The available volume for cargo or luggage. For automobiles, this is usually the trunk volume.
Typical unit code(s): LTR for liters, FTQ for cubic foot/feet

Note: You can use minValue and maxValue to indicate ranges.

variants.name: catalog
variants.definition: A data catalog which contains this dataset.

variants.name: category
variants.definition: A category for the item. Greater signs or slashes can be used to informally indicate a category hierarchy.

variants.name: CheckInAction
variants.definition:
The act of an agent communicating (service provider, social media, etc) their arrival by registering/confirming for a previously reserved service (e.g. flight check in) or at a place (e.g. hotel), possibly resulting in a result (boarding pass, etc).

Related actions:

  • CheckOutAction: The antonym of CheckInAction.
  • ArriveAction: Unlike ArriveAction, CheckInAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the start of a previously reserved service.
  • ConfirmAction: Unlike ConfirmAction, CheckInAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the start of a previously reserved service rather than its validity/existence.

variants.name: ClaimReview
variants.definition: A fact-checking review of claims made (or reported) in some creative work (referenced via itemReviewed).

variants.name: claimReviewed
variants.definition: A short summary of the specific claims reviewed in a ClaimReview.

variants.name: colleague
variants.definition: A colleague of the person.

variants.name: Collection
variants.definition: A created collection of Creative Works or other artefacts.

variants.name: ComicIssue
variants.definition:
Individual comic issues are serially published as
    part of a larger series. For the sake of consistency, even one-shot issues
    belong to a series comprised of a single issue. All comic issues can be
    uniquely identified by: the combination of the name and volume number of the
    series to which the issue belongs; the issue number; and the variant
    description of the issue (if any).

variants.name: ComicSeries
variants.definition:
A sequential publication of comic stories under a
    unifying title, for example "The Amazing Spider-Man" or "Groo the
    Wanderer".

variants.name: ComicStory
variants.definition:
The term "story" is any indivisible, re-printable
    unit of a comic, including the interior stories, covers, and backmatter. Most
    comics have at least two stories: a cover (ComicCoverArt) and an interior story.

variants.name: CommentPermission
variants.definition: Permission to add comments to the document.

variants.name: composer
variants.definition: The person or organization who wrote a composition, or who is the composer of a work performed at some event.

variants.name: CompoundPriceSpecification
variants.definition: A compound price specification is one that bundles multiple prices that all apply in combination for different dimensions of consumption. Use the name property of the attached unit price specification for indicating the dimension of a price component (e.g. "electricity" or "final cleaning").

variants.name: ComputerLanguage
variants.definition: This type covers computer programming languages such as Scheme and Lisp, as well as other language-like computer representations. Natural languages are best represented with the Language type.

variants.name: contactPoint
variants.definition:
A contact point for a person or organization.

TODO: Unify description

variants.name: contentReferenceTime
variants.definition: The specific time described by a creative work, for works (e.g. articles, video objects etc.) that emphasise a particular moment within an Event.

variants.name: contributor
variants.definition: A secondary contributor to the CreativeWork or Event.

variants.name: Conversation
variants.definition: One or more messages between organizations or people on a particular topic. Individual messages can be linked to the conversation with isPartOf or hasPart properties.

variants.name: cookTime
variants.definition: The time it takes to actually cook the dish, in ISO 8601 duration format.

variants.name: Course
variants.definition: A description of an educational course which may be offered as distinct instances at different times and places, or through different media or modes of study. An educational course is a sequence of one or more educational events and/or creative works which aims to build knowledge, competence or ability of learners.

variants.name: courseCode
variants.definition: The identifier used for the Course (e.g. CS101 or 6.001)

variants.name: courseCredits
variants.definition: The number of credits offered for the Course toward an academic goal.

variants.name: courseCreditsUnit
variants.definition: The type of credit associated with the credits earned for the Course. (e.g. TODO NoCredit, Quarter, Semester, CarnegieUnits, ContinuingEducationUnits, ClockHours, Other)

variants.name: CourseInstance
variants.definition: An instance of a Course offered at a specific time and place or through specific media or mode of study or to a specific section of students.

variants.name: courseMode
variants.definition: The medium or means of delivery of the course, or the mode of study.

variants.name: coursePrerequisites
variants.definition: Requirements for taking the Course. May be completion of another Course or a textual description like "permission of instructor". Requirements may be a pre-requisite competency, referenced using AlignmentObject.

variants.name: CreativeWorkSeries
variants.definition:
A CreativeWorkSeries in schema.org is a group of related items, typically but not necessarily of the same kind. CreativeWorkSeries are usually organized into some order, often chronological. Unlike ItemList which is a general purpose data structure for lists of things, the emphasis with CreativeWorkSeries is on published materials (written e.g. books and periodicals, or media such as tv, radio and games).

      <br/><br/>

      Specific subtypes are available for describing <a href="/TVSeries">TVSeries</a>, <a href="/RadioSeries">RadioSeries</a>,
      <a href="/MovieSeries">MovieSeries</a>,
      <a href="/BookSeries">BookSeries</a>,
      <a href="/Periodical">Periodical</a>
      and <a href="/VideoGameSeries">VideoGameSeries</a>. In each case,
      the <a href="/hasPart">hasPart</a> / <a href="/isPartOf">isPartOf</a> properties
      can be used to relate the CreativeWorkSeries to its parts. The general CreativeWorkSeries type serves largely
      just to organize these more specific and practical subtypes.

      <br/><br/>

      It is common for properties applicable to an item from the series to be usefully applied to the containing group.
      Schema.org attempts to anticipate some of these cases, but publishers should be free to apply
      properties of the series parts to the series as a whole wherever they seem appropriate.

variants.name: CreditCard
variants.definition:
A card payment method of a particular brand or name. Used to mark up a particular payment method and/or the financial product/service that supplies the card account.
Commonly used values:

http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#AmericanExpress
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DinersClub
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Discover
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#JCB
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#MasterCard
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#VISA

variants.name: currency
variants.definition: The currency in which the monetary amount is expressed (in 3-letter ISO 4217 format).

variants.name: CurrencyConversionService
variants.definition: A service to convert funds from one currency to another currency.

variants.name: dataset
variants.definition: A dataset contained in this catalog.

variants.name: DatedMoneySpecification
variants.definition: A DatedMoneySpecification represents monetary values with optional start and end dates. For example, this could represent an employee's salary over a specific period of time. Note: This type has been superseded by MonetaryAmount use of that type is recommended

variants.name: dateRead
variants.definition: The date/time at which the message has been read by the recipient if a single recipient exists.

variants.name: dateReceived
variants.definition: The date/time the message was received if a single recipient exists.

variants.name: dateSent
variants.definition: The date/time at which the message was sent.

variants.name: DayOfWeek
variants.definition:
The day of the week, e.g. used to specify to which day the opening hours of an OpeningHoursSpecification refer.

Originally, URLs from GoodRelations were used (for Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday plus a special entry for PublicHolidays); these have now been integrated directly into schema.org.

variants.name: DeliveryMethod
variants.definition:
A delivery method is a standardized procedure for transferring the product or service to the destination of fulfillment chosen by the customer. Delivery methods are characterized by the means of transportation used, and by the organization or group that is the contracting party for the sending organization or person.
Commonly used values:

http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeDirectDownload
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeFreight
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeMail
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeOwnFleet
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModePickUp
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DHL
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#FederalExpress
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#UPS

variants.name: DepositAccount
variants.definition: A type of Bank Account with a main purpose of depositing funds to gain interest or other benefits.

variants.name: description
variants.definition: A description of the item.

variants.name: DiabeticDiet
variants.definition: A diet appropriate for people with diabetes.

variants.name: DigitalDocument
variants.definition: An electronic file or document.

variants.name: DigitalDocumentPermission
variants.definition: A permission for a particular person or group to access a particular file.

variants.name: DigitalDocumentPermissionType
variants.definition: A type of permission which can be granted for accessing a digital document.

variants.name: director
variants.definition: A director of e.g. tv, radio, movie, video gaming etc. content, or of an event. Directors can be associated with individual items or with a series, episode, clip.

variants.name: disambiguatingDescription
variants.definition: A sub property of description. A short description of the item used to disambiguate from other, similar items. Information from other properties (in particular, name) may be necessary for the description to be useful for disambiguation.

variants.name: Distillery
variants.definition: A distillery.

variants.name: duns
variants.definition: The Dun & Bradstreet DUNS number for identifying an organization or business person.

variants.name: eligibleRegion
variants.definition:
The ISO 3166-1 (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) or ISO 3166-2 code, the place, or the GeoShape for the geo-political region(s) for which the offer or delivery charge specification is valid.

See also ineligibleRegion.

variants.name: EmailMessage
variants.definition: An email message.

variants.name: emissionsCO2
variants.definition: The CO2 emissions in g/km. When used in combination with a QuantitativeValue, put "g/km" into the unitText property of that value, since there is no UN/CEFACT Common Code for "g/km".

variants.name: endTime
variants.definition:
The endTime of something. For a reserved event or service (e.g. FoodEstablishmentReservation), the time that it is expected to end. For actions that span a period of time, when the action was performed. e.g. John wrote a book from January to December.

Note that Event uses startDate/endDate instead of startTime/endTime, even when describing dates with times. This situation may be clarified in future revisions.

variants.name: engineDisplacement
variants.definition:
The volume swept by all of the pistons inside the cylinders of an internal combustion engine in a single movement.
Typical unit code(s): CMQ for cubic centimeter, LTR for liters, INQ for cubic inches

Note 1: You can link to information about how the given value has been determined using the <a href="valueReference">valueReference</a> property.<br />
Note 2: You can use <a href="minValue">minValue</a> and <a href="maxValue">maxValue</a> to indicate ranges.

variants.name: enginePower
variants.definition:
The power of the vehicle's engine. Typical unit code(s): KWT for kilowatt, BHP for brake horsepower, N12 for metric horsepower (PS, with 1 PS = 735,49875 W) 

Note 1: There are many different ways of measuring an engine's power. For an overview, see  http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horsepower#Engine_power_test_codes. <br />
Note 2: You can link to information about how the given value has been determined using the <a href="valueReference">valueReference</a> property.<br />
Note 3: You can use <a href="minValue">minValue</a> and <a href="maxValue">maxValue</a> to indicate ranges.

variants.name: Enumeration
variants.definition: Lists or enumerations—for example, a list of cuisines or music genres, etc.

variants.name: EventSeries
variants.definition:
A series of Events. Included events can relate with the series using the superEvent property.

An EventSeries is a collection of events that share some unifying characteristic. For example, "The Olympic Games" is a series, which is repeated regularly. The "2012 London Olympics" can be presented both as an Event in the series "Olympic Games", and as an EventSeries that included a number of sporting competitions as Events.

The nature of the association between the events in an EventSeries can vary, but typical examples could include a thematic event series (e.g. topical meetups or classes), or a series of regular events that share a location, attendee group and/or organizers.

EventSeries has been defined as a kind of Event to make it easy for publishers to use it in an Event context without worrying about which kinds of series are really event-like enough to call an Event. In general an EventSeries may seem more Event-like when the period of time is compact and when aspects such as location are fixed, but it may also sometimes prove useful to describe a longer-term series as an Event.

variants.name: feesAndCommissionsSpecification
variants.definition: Description of fees, commissions, and other terms applied either to a class of financial product, or by a financial service organization.

variants.name: Female
variants.definition: The female gender.

variants.name: FinancialProduct
variants.definition: A product provided to consumers and businesses by financial institutions such as banks, insurance companies, brokerage firms, consumer finance companies, and investment companies which comprise the financial services industry.

variants.name: FollowAction
variants.definition:
The act of forming a personal connection with someone/something (object) unidirectionally/asymmetrically to get updates polled from.

Related actions:

  • BefriendAction: Unlike BefriendAction, FollowAction implies that the connection is not necessarily reciprocal.
  • SubscribeAction: Unlike SubscribeAction, FollowAction implies that the follower acts as an active agent constantly/actively polling for updates.
  • RegisterAction: Unlike RegisterAction, FollowAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object.
  • JoinAction: Unlike JoinAction, FollowAction implies that the agent is interested in getting updates from the object.
  • TrackAction: Unlike TrackAction, FollowAction refers to the polling of updates of all aspects of animate objects rather than the location of inanimate objects (e.g. you track a package, but you don't follow it)
.

variants.name: Friday
variants.definition: The day of the week between Thursday and Saturday.

variants.name: fuelCapacity
variants.definition:
The capacity of the fuel tank or in the case of electric cars, the battery. If there are multiple components for storage, this should indicate the total of all storage of the same type.
Typical unit code(s): LTR for liters, GLL of US gallons, GLI for UK / imperial gallons, AMH for ampere-hours (for electrical vehicles)

variants.name: Game
variants.definition: The Game type represents things which are games. These are typically rule-governed recreational activities, e.g. role-playing games in which players assume the role of characters in a fictional setting.

variants.name: gender
variants.definition: Gender of the person. While http://schema.org/Male and http://schema.org/Female may be used, text strings are also acceptable for people who do not identify as a binary gender.

variants.name: GenderType
variants.definition: An enumeration of genders.

variants.name: GeoCircle
variants.definition:
A GeoCircle is a GeoShape representing a circular geographic area. As it is a GeoShape
          it provides the simple textual property 'circle', but also allows the combination of postalCode alongside geoRadius.
          The center of the circle can be indicated via the 'geoMidpoint' property, or more approximately using 'address', 'postalCode'.

variants.name: GlutenFreeDiet
variants.definition: A diet exclusive of gluten.

variants.name: grantee
variants.definition: The person, organization, contact point, or audience that has been granted this permission.

variants.name: grantsCredential
variants.definition: A Credential granted upon successfully completing the Course.

variants.name: gtin12
variants.definition: The GTIN-12 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. The GTIN-12 is the 12-digit GS1 Identification Key composed of a U.P.C. Company Prefix, Item Reference, and Check Digit used to identify trade items. See GS1 GTIN Summary for more details.

variants.name: gtin13
variants.definition: The GTIN-13 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. This is equivalent to 13-digit ISBN codes and EAN UCC-13. Former 12-digit UPC codes can be converted into a GTIN-13 code by simply adding a preceeding zero. See GS1 GTIN Summary for more details.

variants.name: gtin14
variants.definition: The GTIN-14 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. See GS1 GTIN Summary for more details.

variants.name: gtin8
variants.definition: The GTIN-8 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. This code is also known as EAN/UCC-8 or 8-digit EAN. See GS1 GTIN Summary for more details.

variants.name: HalalDiet
variants.definition: A diet conforming to Islamic dietary practices.

variants.name: hasCourseInstance
variants.definition: An offering of the course at a specific time and place or through specific media or mode of study or to a specific section of students.

variants.name: hasDigitalDocumentPermission
variants.definition: A permission related to the access to this document (e.g. permission to read or write an electronic document). For a public document, specify a grantee with an Audience with audienceType equal to "public".

variants.name: HealthInsurancePlan
variants.definition: A US-style health insurance plan, including PPOs, EPOs, and HMOs.

variants.name: healthPlanCoinsuranceOption
variants.definition: Whether the coinsurance applies before or after deductible, etc. TODO: Is this a closed set?

variants.name: healthPlanCoinsuranceRate
variants.definition: Whether The rate of coinsurance expressed as a number between 0.0 and 1.0.

variants.name: healthPlanCopay
variants.definition: Whether The copay amount.

variants.name: healthPlanCopayOption
variants.definition: Whether the copay is before or after deductible, etc. TODO: Is this a closed set?

variants.name: healthPlanCostSharing
variants.definition: Whether The costs to the patient for services under this network or formulary.

variants.name: HealthPlanCostSharingSpecification
variants.definition: A description of costs to the patient under a given network or formulary.

variants.name: healthPlanDrugOption
variants.definition: TODO.

variants.name: healthPlanDrugTier
variants.definition: The tier(s) of drugs offered by this formulary or insurance plan.

variants.name: HealthPlanFormulary
variants.definition: For a given health insurance plan, the specification for costs and coverage of prescription drugs.

variants.name: healthPlanId
variants.definition: The 14-character, HIOS-generated Plan ID number. (Plan IDs must be unique, even across different markets.)

variants.name: healthPlanMarketingUrl
variants.definition: The URL that goes directly to the plan brochure for the specific standard plan or plan variation.

variants.name: HealthPlanNetwork
variants.definition: A US-style health insurance plan network.

variants.name: healthPlanNetworkId
variants.definition: Name or unique ID of network. (Networks are often reused across different insurance plans).

variants.name: healthPlanNetworkTier
variants.definition: The tier(s) for this network.

variants.name: healthPlanPharmacyCategory
variants.definition: The category or type of pharmacy associated with this cost sharing.

variants.name: HinduDiet
variants.definition: A diet conforming to Hindu dietary practices, in particular, beef-free.

variants.name: HomeAndConstructionBusiness
variants.definition:
A construction business.

A HomeAndConstructionBusiness is a LocalBusiness that provides services around homes and buildings.

As a LocalBusiness it can be described as a provider of one or more Service(s).

variants.name: icaoCode
variants.definition: ICAO identifier for an airport.

variants.name: includedDataCatalog
variants.definition: A data catalog which contains this dataset (this property was previously 'catalog', preferred name is now 'includedInDataCatalog').

variants.name: includedInDataCatalog
variants.definition: A data catalog which contains this dataset.

variants.name: includedInHealthInsurancePlan
variants.definition: The insurance plans that cover this drug.

variants.name: includesHealthPlanFormulary
variants.definition: Formularies covered by this plan.

variants.name: includesHealthPlanNetwork
variants.definition: Networks covered by this plan.

variants.name: ineligibleRegion
variants.definition:
The ISO 3166-1 (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) or ISO 3166-2 code, the place, or the GeoShape for the geo-political region(s) for which the offer or delivery charge specification is not valid, e.g. a region where the transaction is not allowed.

See also eligibleRegion.

variants.name: inLanguage
variants.definition: The language of the content or performance or used in an action. Please use one of the language codes from the IETF BCP 47 standard. See also availableLanguage.

variants.name: instructor
variants.definition: A person assigned to instruct or provide instructional assistance for the CourseInstance.

variants.name: instrument
variants.definition: The object that helped the agent perform the action. e.g. John wrote a book with a pen.

variants.name: interestRate
variants.definition: The interest rate, charged or paid, applicable to the financial product. Note: This is different from the calculated annualPercentageRate.

variants.name: InvestmentOrDeposit
variants.definition: A type of financial product that typically requires the client to transfer funds to a financial service in return for potential beneficial financial return.

variants.name: isAcceptingNewPatients
variants.definition: Whether the provider is accepting new patients.

variants.name: isBasedOn
variants.definition: A resource that was used in the creation of this resource. This term can be repeated for multiple sources. For example, http://example.com/great-multiplication-intro.html.

variants.name: isBasedOnUrl
variants.definition: A resource that was used in the creation of this resource. This term can be repeated for multiple sources. For example, http://example.com/great-multiplication-intro.html.

variants.name: isRelatedTo
variants.definition: A pointer to another, somehow related product (or multiple products).

variants.name: isSimilarTo
variants.definition: A pointer to another, functionally similar product (or multiple products).

variants.name: KosherDiet
variants.definition: A diet conforming to Jewish dietary practices.

variants.name: Language
variants.definition: Natural languages such as Spanish, Tamil, Hindi, English, etc. Formal language code tags expressed in BCP 47 can be used via the alternateName property. The Language type previously also covered programming languages such as Scheme and Lisp, which are now best represented using ComputerLanguage.

variants.name: LegalService
variants.definition:
A LegalService is a business that provides legally-oriented services, advice and representation, e.g. law firms.

As a LocalBusiness it can be described as a provider of one or more Service(s).

variants.name: leiCode
variants.definition: An organization identifier that uniquely identifies a legal entity as defined in ISO 17442.

variants.name: linkRelationship
variants.definition: Indicates the relationship type of a Web link.

variants.name: LinkRole
variants.definition: A Role that represents a Web link e.g. as expressed via the 'url' property. Its linkRelationship property can indicate URL-based and plain textual link types e.g. those in IANA link registry or others such as 'amphtml'. This structure provides a placeholder where details from HTML's link element can be represented outside of HTML, e.g. in JSON-LD feeds.

variants.name: LoanOrCredit
variants.definition: A financial product for the loaning of an amount of money under agreed terms and charges.

variants.name: loanTerm
variants.definition: The duration of the loan or credit agreement.

variants.name: logo
variants.definition: An associated logo.

variants.name: LowCalorieDiet
variants.definition: A diet focused on reduced calorie intake.

variants.name: LowFatDiet
variants.definition: A diet focused on reduced fat and cholesterol intake.

variants.name: LowLactoseDiet
variants.definition: A diet appropriate for people with lactose intolerance.

variants.name: LowSaltDiet
variants.definition: A diet focused on reduced sodium intake.

variants.name: mainEntityOfPage
variants.definition: Indicates a page (or other CreativeWork) for which this thing is the main entity being described. See background notes for details.

variants.name: Male
variants.definition: The male gender.

variants.name: maxValue
variants.definition: The upper value of some characteristic or property.

variants.name: MedicalOrganization
variants.definition: A medical organization (physical or not), such as hospital, institution or clinic.

variants.name: Message
variants.definition: A single message from a sender to one or more organizations or people.

variants.name: messageAttachment
variants.definition: A CreativeWork attached to the message.

variants.name: minimumPaymentDue
variants.definition: The minimum payment required at this time.

variants.name: minValue
variants.definition: The lower value of some characteristic or property.

variants.name: Monday
variants.definition: The day of the week between Sunday and Tuesday.

variants.name: MonetaryAmount
variants.definition: A monetary value or range. This type can be used to describe an amount of money such as $50 USD, or a range as in describing a bank account being suitable for a balance between £1,000 and £1,000,000 GBP, or the value of a salary, etc. It is recommended to use PriceSpecification Types to describe the price of an Offer, Invoice, etc.

variants.name: netWorth
variants.definition: The total financial value of the organization or person as calculated by subtracting assets from liabilities.

variants.name: NoteDigitalDocument
variants.definition: A file containing a note, primarily for the author.

variants.name: object
variants.definition: The object upon the action is carried out, whose state is kept intact or changed. Also known as the semantic roles patient, affected or undergoer (which change their state) or theme (which doesn't). e.g. John read a book.

variants.name: offersPrescriptionByMail
variants.definition: Whether prescriptions can be delivered by mail.

variants.name: openingHours
variants.definition:
The general opening hours for a business. Opening hours can be specified as a weekly time range, starting with days, then times per day. Multiple days can be listed with commas ',' separating each day. Day or time ranges are specified using a hyphen '-'.
- Days are specified using the following two-letter combinations: Mo, Tu, We, Th, Fr, Sa, Su.
- Times are specified using 24:00 time. For example, 3pm is specified as 15:00.
- Here is an example: <span itemprop="openingHours" content="Tu,Th 16:00-20:00">Tuesdays and Thursdays 4-8pm</span>.
- If a business is open 7 days a week, then it can be specified as <span itemprop="openingHours" content="Mo-Su">Monday through Sunday, all day</span>.

variants.name: OpeningHoursSpecification
variants.definition:
A structured value providing information about the opening hours of a place or a certain service inside a place.
The place is open if the opens property is specified, and closed otherwise.
If the value for the closes property is less than the value for the opens property then the hour range is assumed to span over the next day.

variants.name: ParcelService
variants.definition:
A private parcel service as the delivery mode available for a certain offer.
Commonly used values:

http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DHL
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#FederalExpress
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#UPS

variants.name: parentOrganization
variants.definition: The larger organization that this local business is a branch of, if any.

variants.name: participant
variants.definition: Other co-agents that participated in the action indirectly. e.g. John wrote a book with Steve.

variants.name: payload
variants.definition:
The permitted weight of passengers and cargo, EXCLUDING the weight of the empty vehicle.
Typical unit code(s): KGM for kilogram, LBR for pound

Note 1: Many databases specify the permitted TOTAL weight instead, which is the sum of <a href="weight">weight</a> and <a href="payload">payload</a>.<br />
Note 2: You can indicate additional information in the <a href="name">name</a> of the <a href="QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a> node.<br />
Note 3: You may also link to a <a href="QualitativeValue">QualitativeValue</a> node that provides additional information using <a href="valueReference">valueReference</a>.<br />
Note 4: Note that you can use <a href="minValue">minValue</a> and <a href="maxValue">maxValue</a> to indicate ranges.

variants.name: PaymentCard
variants.definition: A payment method using a credit, debit, store or other card to associate the payment with an account.

variants.name: PaymentMethod
variants.definition:
A payment method is a standardized procedure for transferring the monetary amount for a purchase. Payment methods are characterized by the legal and technical structures used, and by the organization or group carrying out the transaction.
Commonly used values:

http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ByBankTransferInAdvance
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ByInvoice
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Cash
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#CheckInAdvance
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#COD
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DirectDebit
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#GoogleCheckout
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PayPal
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PaySwarm

variants.name: PaymentService
variants.definition: A Service to transfer funds from a person or organization to a beneficiary person or organization.

variants.name: Periodical
variants.definition:
A publication in any medium issued in successive parts bearing numerical or chronological designations and intended, such as a magazine, scholarly journal, or newspaper to continue indefinitely.

See also blog post.

variants.name: permissionType
variants.definition: The type of permission granted the person, organization, or audience.

variants.name: PreOrder
variants.definition: Indicates that the item is available for pre-order, but will be delivered when generally available.

variants.name: PreOrderAction
variants.definition: An agent orders a (not yet released) object/product/service to be delivered/sent.

variants.name: prepTime
variants.definition: The length of time it takes to prepare the recipe, in ISO 8601 duration format.

variants.name: PreSale
variants.definition: Indicates that the item is available for ordering and delivery before general availability.

variants.name: PresentationDigitalDocument
variants.definition: A file containing slides or used for a presentation.

variants.name: previewUrl
variants.definition: A link to a site where a preview of the course is offered.

variants.name: price
variants.definition:
The offer price of a product, or of a price component when attached to PriceSpecification and its subtypes.

Usage guidelines:
  • Use the priceCurrency property (with ISO 4217 codes e.g. "USD") instead of including ambiguous symbols such as '$' in the value.
  • Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.
  • Note that both RDFa and Microdata syntax allow the use of a "content=" attribute for publishing simple machine-readable values alongside more human-friendly formatting.
  • Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similiar Unicode symbols.

variants.name: priceComponent
variants.definition: This property links to all UnitPriceSpecification nodes that apply in parallel for the CompoundPriceSpecification node.

variants.name: PriceSpecification
variants.definition: A structured value representing a price or price range. Typically, only the subclasses of this type are used for markup. It is recommended to use MonetaryAmount to describe independent amounts of money such as a salary, credit card limits, etc.

variants.name: ProfessionalService
variants.definition:
Original definition: "provider of professional services."

The general ProfessionalService type for local businesses was deprecated due to confusion with Service. For reference, the types that it included were: Dentist, AccountingService, Attorney, Notary, as well as types for several kinds of HomeAndConstructionBusiness: Electrician, GeneralContractor, HousePainter, Locksmith, Plumber, RoofingContractor. LegalService was introduced as a more inclusive supertype of Attorney.

variants.name: programmingLanguage
variants.definition: The computer programming language.

variants.name: PropertyValue
variants.definition:
A property-value pair, e.g. representing a feature of a product or place. Use the 'name' property for the name of the property. If there is an additional human-readable version of the value, put that into the 'description' property.

Always use specific schema.org properties when a) they exist and b) you can populate them. Using PropertyValue as a substitute will typically not trigger the same effect as using the original, specific property.

variants.name: PublicationIssue
variants.definition:
A part of a successively published publication such as a periodical or publication volume, often numbered, usually containing a grouping of works such as articles.

  <br/><br/>See also <a href="https://blog.schema.org/2014/09/02/schema-org-support-for-bibliographic-relationships-and-periodicals/">blog post</a>.

variants.name: PublicationVolume
variants.definition:
A part of a successively published publication such as a periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered. It may represent a time span, such as a year.

  <br/><br/>See also <a href="https://blog.schema.org/2014/09/02/schema-org-support-for-bibliographic-relationships-and-periodicals/">blog post</a>.

variants.name: PublicHolidays
variants.definition: This stands for any day that is a public holiday; it is a placeholder for all official public holidays in some particular location. While not technically a "day of the week", it can be used with OpeningHoursSpecification. In the context of an opening hours specification it can be used to indicate opening hours on public holidays, overriding general opening hours for the day of the week on which a public holiday occurs.

variants.name: QuantitativeValue
variants.definition: A point value or interval for product characteristics and other purposes.

variants.name: Quotation
variants.definition: A quotation from some work, attributable to real world author and - if associated with a fictional character - to any fictional Person. Use isBasedOnUrl to link to source/origin.

variants.name: ReadPermission
variants.definition: Permission to read or view the document.

variants.name: Recipe
variants.definition: A recipe. For dietary restrictions covered by the recipe, a few common restrictions are enumerated via suitableForDiet. The keywords property can also be used to add more detail.

variants.name: recipeCategory
variants.definition: The category of the recipe—for example, appetizer, entree, etc.

variants.name: recipient
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The participant who is at the receiving end of the action.

variants.name: referenceQuantity
variants.definition: The reference quantity for which a certain price applies, e.g. 1 EUR per 4 kWh of electricity. This property is a replacement for unitOfMeasurement for the advanced cases where the price does not relate to a standard unit.

variants.name: RegisterAction
variants.definition:
The act of registering to be a user of a service, product or web page.

Related actions:

  • JoinAction: Unlike JoinAction, RegisterAction implies you are registering to be a user of a service, not a group/team of people.
  • FollowAction: Unlike FollowAction, RegisterAction doesn't imply that the agent is expecting to poll for updates from the object.
  • SubscribeAction: Unlike SubscribeAction, RegisterAction doesn't imply that the agent is expecting updates from the object
.

variants.name: requiredCollateral
variants.definition: Assets required to secure loan or credit repayments. It may take form of third party pledge, goods, financial instruments (cash, securities, etc.)

variants.name: RestrictedDiet
variants.definition: A diet restricted to certain foods or preparations for cultural, religious, health or lifestyle reasons.

variants.name: result
variants.definition: The result produced in the action. e.g. John wrote a book.

variants.name: Role
variants.definition:
Represents additional information about a relationship or property. For example a Role can be used to say that a 'member' role linking some SportsTeam to a player occurred during a particular time period. Or that a Person's 'actor' role in a Movie was for some particular characterName. Such properties can be attached to a Role entity, which is then associated with the main entities using ordinary properties like 'member' or 'actor'.

  <br/><br/>See also <a href="https://blog.schema.org/2014/06/16/introducing-role/">blog post</a>.

variants.name: roofLoad
variants.definition:
The permitted total weight of cargo and installations (e.g. a roof rack) on top of the vehicle.
Typical unit code(s): KGM for kilogram, LBR for pound

Note 1: You can indicate additional information in the <a href="name">name</a> of the <a href="QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a> node.<br />
Note 2: You may also link to a <a href="QualitativeValue">QualitativeValue</a> node that provides additional information using <a href="valueReference">valueReference</a>.<br />
Note 3: Note that you can use <a href="minValue">minValue</a> and <a href="maxValue">maxValue</a> to indicate ranges.

variants.name: rxcui
variants.definition: The RxCUI drug identifier from RXNORM.

variants.name: Saturday
variants.definition: The day of the week between Friday and Sunday.

variants.name: schemaVersion
variants.definition: Indicates (by URL or string) a particular version of a schema used in some CreativeWork. For example, a document could declare a schemaVersion using an URL such as http://schema.org/version/2.0/ if precise indication of schema version was required by some application.

variants.name: seatingCapacity
variants.definition:
The number of persons that can be seated (e.g. in a vehicle), both in terms of the physical space available, and in terms of limitations set by law.
Typical unit code(s): C62 for persons

variants.name: sender
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The participant who is at the sending end of the action.

variants.name: Series
variants.definition: A Series in schema.org is a group of related items, typically but not necessarily of the same kind.

variants.name: specialOpeningHoursSpecification
variants.definition:
The special opening hours of a certain place.
Use this to explicitly override general opening hours brought in scope by openingHoursSpecification or openingHours.

variants.name: speed
variants.definition:
The speed range of the vehicle. If the vehicle is powered by an engine, the upper limit of the speed range (indicated by maxValue) should be the maximum speed achievable under regular conditions.
Typical unit code(s): KMH for km/h, HM for mile per hour (0.447 04 m/s), KNT for knot

Note 1: Use <a href="minValue">minValue</a> and <a href="maxValue">maxValue</a> to indicate the range. Typically, the minimal value is zero.<br />
Note 2: There are many different ways of measuring the speed range. You can link to information about how the given value has been determined using the <a href="valueReference">valueReference</a> property.

variants.name: spokenByCharacter
variants.definition: The (e.g. fictional) character, Person or Organization to whom the quotation is attributed within the containing CreativeWork.

variants.name: sponsor
variants.definition: A person or organization that supports a thing through a pledge, promise, or financial contribution. e.g. a sponsor of a Medical Study or a corporate sponsor of an event.

variants.name: SpreadsheetDigitalDocument
variants.definition: A spreadsheet file.

variants.name: startTime
variants.definition:
The startTime of something. For a reserved event or service (e.g. FoodEstablishmentReservation), the time that it is expected to start. For actions that span a period of time, when the action was performed. e.g. John wrote a book from January to December.

Note that Event uses startDate/endDate instead of startTime/endTime, even when describing dates with times. This situation may be clarified in future revisions.

variants.name: suitableForDiet
variants.definition: Indicates a dietary restriction or guideline for which this recipe is suitable, e.g. diabetic, halal etc.

variants.name: Sunday
variants.definition: The day of the week between Saturday and Monday.

variants.name: TextDigitalDocument
variants.definition: A file composed primarily of text.

variants.name: Thursday
variants.definition: The day of the week between Wednesday and Friday.

variants.name: tongueWeight
variants.definition:
The permitted vertical load (TWR) of a trailer attached to the vehicle. Also referred to as Tongue Load Rating (TLR) or Vertical Load Rating (VLR).
Typical unit code(s): KGM for kilogram, LBR for pound

Note 1: You can indicate additional information in the <a href="name">name</a> of the <a href="QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a> node.<br />
Note 2: You may also link to a <a href="QualitativeValue">QualitativeValue</a> node that provides additional information using <a href="valueReference">valueReference</a>.<br />
Note 3: Note that you can use <a href="minValue">minValue</a> and <a href="maxValue">maxValue</a> to indicate ranges.

variants.name: torque
variants.definition:
The torque (turning force) of the vehicle's engine.
Typical unit code(s): NU for newton metre (N m), F17 for pound-force per foot, or F48 for pound-force per inch

Note 1: You can link to information about how the given value has been determined (e.g. reference RPM) using the <a href="valueReference">valueReference</a> property.<br />
Note 2: You can use <a href="minValue">minValue</a> and <a href="maxValue">maxValue</a> to indicate ranges.

variants.name: totalPaymentDue
variants.definition: The total amount due.

variants.name: totalTime
variants.definition: The total time it takes to prepare and cook the recipe, in ISO 8601 duration format.

variants.name: trailerWeight
variants.definition:
The permitted weight of a trailer attached to the vehicle.
Typical unit code(s): KGM for kilogram, LBR for pound

Note 1: You can indicate additional information in the <a href="name">name</a> of the <a href="QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a> node.<br />
Note 2: You may also link to a <a href="QualitativeValue">QualitativeValue</a> node that provides additional information using <a href="valueReference">valueReference</a>.<br />
Note 3: Note that you can use <a href="minValue">minValue</a> and <a href="maxValue">maxValue</a> to indicate ranges.

variants.name: translator
variants.definition:
An agent responsible for rendering a translated work from a source work

Organization or person who adapts a creative work to different languages, regional differences and technical requirements of a target market, or that translates during some event.

variants.name: Tuesday
variants.definition: The day of the week between Monday and Wednesday.

variants.name: UserBlocks
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use Action-based vocabulary, alongside types such as Comment.

variants.name: UserCheckins
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use Action-based vocabulary, alongside types such as Comment.

variants.name: UserComments
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use Action-based vocabulary, alongside types such as Comment.

variants.name: UserDownloads
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use Action-based vocabulary, alongside types such as Comment.

variants.name: UserInteraction
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use Action-based vocabulary, alongside types such as Comment.

variants.name: UserLikes
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use Action-based vocabulary, alongside types such as Comment.

variants.name: UserPageVisits
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use Action-based vocabulary, alongside types such as Comment.

variants.name: UserPlays
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use Action-based vocabulary, alongside types such as Comment.

variants.name: UserPlusOnes
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use Action-based vocabulary, alongside types such as Comment.

variants.name: UserTweets
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use Action-based vocabulary, alongside types such as Comment.

variants.name: usesHealthPlanIdStandard
variants.definition: The standard for interpreting thePlan ID. The preferred is "HIOS". See the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services for more details.

variants.name: validFrom
variants.definition: The date when the item becomes valid.

variants.name: validThrough
variants.definition: The date after when the item is not valid. For example the end of an offer, salary period, or a period of opening hours.

variants.name: value
variants.definition:
The value of the quantitative value or property value node.
For QuantitativeValue and MonetaryValue, the recommended type for values is 'Number'.
For PropertyValue, it can be 'Text;', 'Number', 'Boolean', or 'StructuredValue'.

variants.name: variantCover
variants.definition:
A description of the variant cover
    for the issue, if the issue is a variant printing. For example, "Bryan Hitch
    Variant Cover" or "2nd Printing Variant".

variants.name: VeganDiet
variants.definition: A diet exclusive of all animal products.

variants.name: VegetarianDiet
variants.definition: A diet exclusive of animal meat.

variants.name: vehicleSeatingCapacity
variants.definition:
The number of passengers that can be seated in the vehicle, both in terms of the physical space available, and in terms of limitations set by law.
Typical unit code(s): C62 for persons.

variants.name: vehicleSpecialUsage
variants.definition: Indicates whether the vehicle has been used for special purposes, like commercial rental, driving school, or as a taxi. The legislation in many countries requires this information to be revealed when offering a car for sale.

variants.name: WarrantyScope
variants.definition:
A range of of services that will be provided to a customer free of charge in case of a defect or malfunction of a product.
Commonly used values:

http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Labor-BringIn
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PartsAndLabor-BringIn
http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PartsAndLabor-PickUp

variants.name: Wednesday
variants.definition: The day of the week between Tuesday and Thursday.

variants.name: weightTotal
variants.definition:
The permitted total weight of the loaded vehicle, including passengers and cargo and the weight of the empty vehicle.
Typical unit code(s): KGM for kilogram, LBR for pound

Note 1: You can indicate additional information in the <a href="name">name</a> of the <a href="QuantitativeValue">QuantitativeValue</a> node.<br />
Note 2: You may also link to a <a href="QualitativeValue">QualitativeValue</a> node that provides additional information using <a href="valueReference">valueReference</a>.<br />
Note 3: Note that you can use <a href="minValue">minValue</a> and <a href="maxValue">maxValue</a> to indicate ranges.

variants.name: WorkersUnion
variants.definition: A Workers Union (also known as a Labor Union, Labour Union, or Trade Union) is an organization that promotes the interests of its worker members by collectively bargaining with management, organizing, and political lobbying.

variants.name: WritePermission
variants.definition: Permission to write or edit the document.

variants.name: Abdomen
variants.definition: Abdomen clinical examination.

variants.name: accelerationTime
variants.definition:
The time needed to accelerate the vehicle from a given start velocity to a given target velocity.

Typical unit code(s): SEC for seconds

  • Note: There are unfortunately no standard unit codes for seconds/0..100 km/h or seconds/0..60 mph. Simply use "SEC" for seconds and indicate the velocities in the name of the QuantitativeValue, or use valueReference with a QuantitativeValue of 0..60 mph or 0..100 km/h to specify the reference speeds.

variants.name: AcceptAction
variants.definition:
The act of committing to/adopting an object.

Related actions:

  • RejectAction: The antonym of AcceptAction.

variants.name: Accommodation
variants.definition:
An accommodation is a place that can accommodate human beings, e.g. a hotel room, a camping pitch, or a meeting room. Many accommodations are for overnight stays, but this is not a mandatory requirement. For more specific types of accommodations not defined in schema.org, one can use additionalType with external vocabularies.

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

variants.name: AccountingService
variants.definition:
Accountancy business.

As a LocalBusiness it can be described as a provider of one or more Service(s).

variants.name: action
variants.definition: Obsolete term for muscleAction. Not to be confused with potentialAction.

variants.name: Action
variants.definition:
An action performed by a direct agent and indirect participants upon a direct object. Optionally happens at a location with the help of an inanimate instrument. The execution of the action may produce a result. Specific action sub-type documentation specifies the exact expectation of each argument/role.

See also blog post and Actions overview document.

variants.name: activeIngredient
variants.definition: An active ingredient, typically chemical compounds and/or biologic substances.

variants.name: activityDuration
variants.definition: Length of time to engage in the activity.

variants.name: activityFrequency
variants.definition: How often one should engage in the activity.

variants.name: additionalProperty
variants.definition:
A property-value pair representing an additional characteristics of the entitity, e.g. a product feature or another characteristic for which there is no matching property in schema.org.

Note: Publishers should be aware that applications designed to use specific schema.org properties (e.g. http://schema.org/width, http://schema.org/color, http://schema.org/gtin13, ...) will typically expect such data to be provided using those properties, rather than using the generic property/value mechanism.

variants.name: addressCountry
variants.definition: The country. For example, USA. You can also provide the two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

variants.name: adverseOutcome
variants.definition: A possible complication and/or side effect of this therapy. If it is known that an adverse outcome is serious (resulting in death, disability, or permanent damage; requiring hospitalization; or is otherwise life-threatening or requires immediate medical attention), tag it as a seriouseAdverseOutcome instead.

variants.name: amenityFeature
variants.definition: An amenity feature (e.g. a characteristic or service) of the Accommodation. This generic property does not make a statement about whether the feature is included in an offer for the main accommodation or available at extra costs.

variants.name: Apartment
variants.definition: An apartment (in American English) or flat (in British English) is a self-contained housing unit (a type of residential real estate) that occupies only part of a building (Source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartment).

variants.name: Appearance
variants.definition: Appearance assessment with clinical examination.

variants.name: applicationCategory
variants.definition: Type of software application, e.g. 'Game, Multimedia'.

variants.name: applicationSubCategory
variants.definition: Subcategory of the application, e.g. 'Arcade Game'.

variants.name: ApplyAction
variants.definition:
The act of registering to an organization/service without the guarantee to receive it.

Related actions:

  • RegisterAction: Unlike RegisterAction, ApplyAction has no guarantees that the application will be accepted.

variants.name: ArriveAction
variants.definition: The act of arriving at a place. An agent arrives at a destination from a fromLocation, optionally with participants.

variants.name: Article
variants.definition:
An article, such as a news article or piece of investigative report. Newspapers and magazines have articles of many different types and this is intended to cover them all.

See also blog post.

variants.name: artist
variants.definition:
The primary artist for a work
    in a medium other than pencils or digital line art--for example, if the
    primary artwork is done in watercolors or digital paints.

variants.name: AskAction
variants.definition:
The act of posing a question / favor to someone.

Related actions:

  • ReplyAction: Appears generally as a response to AskAction.

variants.name: Attorney
variants.definition:
Professional service: Attorney.

This type is deprecated - LegalService is more inclusive and less ambiguous.

variants.name: audience
variants.definition: An intended audience, i.e. a group for whom something was created.

variants.name: author
variants.definition: The author of this content or rating. Please note that author is special in that HTML 5 provides a special mechanism for indicating authorship via the rel tag. That is equivalent to this and may be used interchangeably.

variants.name: availableLanguage
variants.definition: A language someone may use with the item. Please use one of the language codes from the IETF BCP 47 standard. See also inLanguage

variants.name: bed
variants.definition:
The type of bed or beds included in the accommodation. For the single case of just one bed of a certain type, you use bed directly with a text.
      If you want to indicate the quantity of a certain kind of bed, use an instance of BedDetails. For more detailed information, use the amenityFeature property.

variants.name: BedAndBreakfast
variants.definition:
Bed and breakfast.

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

variants.name: BedDetails
variants.definition: An entity holding detailed information about the available bed types, e.g. the quantity of twin beds for a hotel room. For the single case of just one bed of a certain type, you can use bed directly with a text. See also BedType (under development).

variants.name: BedType
variants.definition: A type of bed. This is used for indicating the bed or beds available in an accommodation.

variants.name: BefriendAction
variants.definition:
The act of forming a personal connection with someone (object) mutually/bidirectionally/symmetrically.

Related actions:

  • FollowAction: Unlike FollowAction, BefriendAction implies that the connection is reciprocal.

variants.name: benefitsSummaryUrl
variants.definition: The URL that goes directly to the summary of benefits and coverage for the specific standard plan or plan variation.

variants.name: bodyLocation
variants.definition: Location in the body of the anatomical structure.

variants.name: BorrowAction
variants.definition:
The act of obtaining an object under an agreement to return it at a later date. Reciprocal of LendAction.

Related actions:

  • LendAction: Reciprocal of BorrowAction.

variants.name: branch
variants.definition: The branches that delineate from the nerve bundle. Not to be confused with branchOf.

variants.name: branchCode
variants.definition:
A short textual code (also called "store code") that uniquely identifies a place of business. The code is typically assigned by the parentOrganization and used in structured URLs.

For example, in the URL http://www.starbucks.co.uk/store-locator/etc/detail/3047 the code "3047" is a branchCode for a particular branch.

variants.name: BreadcrumbList
variants.definition:
A BreadcrumbList is an ItemList consisting of a chain of linked Web pages, typically described using at least their URL and their name, and typically ending with the current page.

The position property is used to reconstruct the order of the items in a BreadcrumbList The convention is that a breadcrumb list has an itemListOrder of ItemListOrderAscending (lower values listed first), and that the first items in this list correspond to the "top" or beginning of the breadcrumb trail, e.g. with a site or section homepage. The specific values of 'position' are not assigned meaning for a BreadcrumbList, but they should be integers, e.g. beginning with '1' for the first item in the list.

variants.name: broadcastTimezone
variants.definition: The timezone in ISO 8601 format for which the service bases its broadcasts

variants.name: browserRequirements
variants.definition: Specifies browser requirements in human-readable text. For example, 'requires HTML5 support'.

variants.name: BusinessEntityType
variants.definition:
A business entity type is a conceptual entity representing the legal form, the size, the main line of business, the position in the value chain, or any combination thereof, of an organization or business person.

Commonly used values:

  • http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Business
  • http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Enduser
  • http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PublicInstitution
  • http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Reseller

variants.name: BusinessFunction
variants.definition:
The business function specifies the type of activity or access (i.e., the bundle of rights) offered by the organization or business person through the offer. Typical are sell, rental or lease, maintenance or repair, manufacture / produce, recycle / dispose, engineering / construction, or installation. Proprietary specifications of access rights are also instances of this class.

Commonly used values:

  • http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ConstructionInstallation
  • http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Dispose
  • http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#LeaseOut
  • http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Maintain
  • http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ProvideService
  • http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Repair
  • http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Sell
  • http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Buy

variants.name: BusReservation
variants.definition:
A reservation for bus travel.

Note: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, use Offer.

variants.name: Campground
variants.definition:
A camping site, campsite, or campground is a place used for overnight stay in the outdoors. In British English a campsite is an area, usually divided into a number of pitches, where people can camp overnight using tents or camper vans or caravans; this British English use of the word is synonymous with the American English expression campground. In American English the term campsite generally means an area where an individual, family, group, or military unit can pitch a tent or parks a camper; a campground may contain many campsites (Source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campsite).

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

variants.name: CampingPitch
variants.definition:
A camping pitch is an individual place for overnight stay in the outdoors, typically being part of a larger camping site.

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

variants.name: CancelAction
variants.definition:
The act of asserting that a future event/action is no longer going to happen.

Related actions:

  • ConfirmAction: The antonym of CancelAction.

variants.name: CardiovascularExam
variants.definition: Cardiovascular system assessment withclinical examination.

variants.name: cargoVolume
variants.definition:
The available volume for cargo or luggage. For automobiles, this is usually the trunk volume.

Typical unit code(s): LTR for liters, FTQ for cubic foot/feet

Note: You can use minValue and maxValue to indicate ranges.

variants.name: category
variants.definition: A category for the item. Greater signs or slashes can be used to informally indicate a category hierarchy.

variants.name: cause
variants.definition: Specifying a cause of something in general. e.g in medicine , one of the causative agent(s) that are most directly responsible for the pathophysiologic process that eventually results in the occurrence.

variants.name: checkinTime
variants.definition: The earliest someone may check into a lodging establishment.

variants.name: CheckOutAction
