  • Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.

variants.name: recognizedBy
variants.definition: An organization that acknowledges the validity, value or utility of a credential. Note: recognition may include a process of quality assurance or accreditation.

variants.name: ResearchProject
variants.definition: A Research project.

variants.name: responsibilities
variants.definition: Responsibilities associated with this role or Occupation.

variants.name: SheetMusic
variants.definition: Printed music, as opposed to performed or recorded music.

variants.name: ShortStory
variants.definition: Short story or tale. A brief work of literature, usually written in narrative prose.

variants.name: skills
variants.definition: Skills required to fulfill this role or in this Occupation.

variants.name: slogan
variants.definition: A slogan or motto associated with the item.

variants.name: spatial
variants.definition: The "spatial" property can be used in cases when more specific properties (e.g. locationCreated, spatialCoverage, contentLocation) are not known to be appropriate.

variants.name: sponsor
variants.definition: A person or organization that supports a thing through a pledge, promise, or financial contribution. e.g. a sponsor of a Medical Study or a corporate sponsor of an event.

variants.name: startOffset
variants.definition: The start time of the clip expressed as the number of seconds from the beginning of the work.

variants.name: startTime
variants.definition:
The startTime of something. For a reserved event or service (e.g. FoodEstablishmentReservation), the time that it is expected to start. For actions that span a period of time, when the action was performed. e.g. John wrote a book from January to December. For media, including audio and video, it's the time offset of the start of a clip within a larger file.

Note that Event uses startDate/endDate instead of startTime/endTime, even when describing dates with times. This situation may be clarified in future revisions.

variants.name: subTrip
variants.definition: Identifies a Trip that is a subTrip of this Trip. For example Day 1, Day 2, etc. of a multi-day trip.

variants.name: SurgicalProcedure
variants.definition: A medical procedure involving an incision with instruments; performed for diagnose, or therapeutic purposes.

variants.name: temporal
variants.definition: The "temporal" property can be used in cases where more specific properties (e.g. temporalCoverage, dateCreated, dateModified, datePublished) are not known to be appropriate.

variants.name: temporalCoverage
variants.definition:
The temporalCoverage of a CreativeWork indicates the period that the content applies to, i.e. that it describes, either as a DateTime or as a textual string indicating a time period in ISO 8601 time interval format. In the case of a Dataset it will typically indicate the relevant time period in a precise notation (e.g. for a 2011 census dataset, the year 2011 would be written "2011/2012"). Other forms of content e.g. ScholarlyArticle, Book, TVSeries or TVEpisode may indicate their temporalCoverage in broader terms - textually or via well-known URL. Written works such as books may sometimes have precise temporal coverage too, e.g. a work set in 1939 - 1945 can be indicated in ISO 8601 interval format format via "1939/1945".

Open-ended date ranges can be written with ".." in place of the end date. For example, "2015-11/.." indicates a range beginning in November 2015 and with no specified final date. This is tentative and might be updated in future when ISO 8601 is officially updated.

variants.name: timeRequired
variants.definition: Approximate or typical time it takes to work with or through this learning resource for the typical intended target audience, e.g. 'PT30M', 'PT1H25M'.

variants.name: totalPrice
variants.definition:
The total price for the reservation or ticket, including applicable taxes, shipping, etc.

Usage guidelines:

  • Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similiar Unicode symbols.
  • Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.

variants.name: TouristDestination
variants.definition: A tourist destination. In principle any Place can be a TouristDestination from a City, Region or Country to an AmusementPark or Hotel. This Type can be used on its own to describe a general TouristDestination, or be used as an additionalType to add tourist relevant properties to any other Place. A TouristDestination is defined as a Place that contains, or is colocated with, one or more TouristAttractions, often linked by a similar theme or interest to a particular touristType. The UNWTO defines Destination (main destination of a tourism trip) as the place visited that is central to the decision to take the trip. (See examples below).

variants.name: validFor
variants.definition: The duration of validity of a permit or similar thing.

variants.name: validIn
variants.definition: The geographic area where a permit or similar thing is valid.

variants.name: value
variants.definition:
The value of the quantitative value or property value node.

  • For QuantitativeValue and MonetaryAmount, the recommended type for values is 'Number'.
  • For PropertyValue, it can be 'Text;', 'Number', 'Boolean', or 'StructuredValue'.
  • Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similiar Unicode symbols.
  • Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.

variants.name: video
variants.definition: An embedded video object.

variants.name: accessModeSufficient
variants.definition: A list of single or combined accessModes that are sufficient to understand all the intellectual content of a resource. Expected values include:  auditory, tactile, textual, visual.

variants.name: arrivalTime
variants.definition: The expected arrival time.

variants.name: availabilityEnds
variants.definition: The end of the availability of the product or service included in the offer.

variants.name: availabilityStarts
variants.definition: The beginning of the availability of the product or service included in the offer.

variants.name: checkinTime
variants.definition: The earliest someone may check into a lodging establishment.

variants.name: checkoutTime
variants.definition: The latest someone may check out of a lodging establishment.

variants.name: conditionsOfAccess
variants.definition:
Conditions that affect the availability of, or method(s) of access to, an item. Typically used for real world items such as an ArchiveComponent held by an ArchiveOrganization. This property is not suitable for use as a general Web access control mechanism. It is expressed only in natural language.

For example "Available by appointment from the Reading Room" or "Accessible only from logged-in accounts ".

variants.name: constrainingProperty
variants.definition: Indicates a property used as a constraint to define a StatisticalPopulation with respect to the set of entities corresponding to an indicated type (via populationType).

variants.name: creativeWorkStatus
variants.definition: The status of a creative work in terms of its stage in a lifecycle. Example terms include Incomplete, Draft, Published, Obsolete. Some organizations define a set of terms for the stages of their publication lifecycle.

variants.name: dateDeleted
variants.definition: The datetime the item was removed from the DataFeed.

variants.name: dateIssued
variants.definition: The date the ticket was issued.

variants.name: dateRead
variants.definition: The date/time at which the message has been read by the recipient if a single recipient exists.

variants.name: departureTime
variants.definition: The expected departure time.

variants.name: doorTime
variants.definition: The time admission will commence.

variants.name: educationalCredentialAwarded
variants.definition: A description of the qualification, award, certificate, diploma or other educational credential awarded as a consequence of successful completion of this course or program.

variants.name: EducationalOccupationalProgram
variants.definition: A program offered by an institution which determines the learning progress to achieve an outcome, usually a credential like a degree or certificate. This would define a discrete set of opportunities (e.g., job, courses) that together constitute a program with a clear start, end, set of requirements, and transition to a new occupational opportunity (e.g., a job), or sometimes a higher educational opportunity (e.g., an advanced degree).

variants.name: endTime
variants.definition:
The endTime of something. For a reserved event or service (e.g. FoodEstablishmentReservation), the time that it is expected to end. For actions that span a period of time, when the action was performed. e.g. John wrote a book from January to December. For media, including audio and video, it's the time offset of the end of a clip within a larger file.

Note that Event uses startDate/endDate instead of startTime/endTime, even when describing dates with times. This situation may be clarified in future revisions.

variants.name: ExchangeRefund
variants.definition: A ExchangeRefund ...

variants.name: expectedArrivalFrom
variants.definition: The earliest date the package may arrive.

variants.name: expectedArrivalUntil
variants.definition: The latest date the package may arrive.

variants.name: FullRefund
variants.definition: A FullRefund ...

variants.name: gtin
variants.definition: A Global Trade Item Number (GTIN). GTINs identify trade items, including products and services, using numeric identification codes. The gtin property generalizes the earlier gtin8, gtin12, gtin13, and gtin14 properties. The GS1 digital link specifications express GTINs as URLs. A correct gtin value should be a valid GTIN, which means that it should be an all-numeric string of either 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits, or a "GS1 Digital Link" URL based on such a string. The numeric component should also have a valid GS1 check digit and meet the other rules for valid GTINs. See also GS1's GTIN Summary and Wikipedia for more details. Left-padding of the gtin values is not required or encouraged.

variants.name: hasCredential
variants.definition: A credential awarded to the Person or Organization.

variants.name: hasProductReturnPolicy
variants.definition: Indicates a ProductReturnPolicy that may be applicable.

variants.name: inStoreReturnsOffered
variants.definition: Are in-store returns offered?

variants.name: jobImmediateStart
variants.definition: An indicator as to whether a position is available for an immediate start.

variants.name: jobStartDate
variants.definition: The date on which a successful applicant for this job would be expected to start work. Choose a specific date in the future or use the jobImmediateStart property to indicate the position is to be filled as soon as possible.

variants.name: knowsAbout
variants.definition: Of a Person, and less typically of an Organization, to indicate a topic that is known about - suggesting possible expertise but not implying it. We do not distinguish skill levels here, or relate this to educational content, events, objectives or JobPosting descriptions.

variants.name: marginOfError
variants.definition: A marginOfError for an Observation.

variants.name: measuredProperty
variants.definition: The measuredProperty of an Observation, either a schema.org property, a property from other RDF-compatible systems e.g. W3C RDF Data Cube, or schema.org extensions such as GS1's.

variants.name: measuredValue
variants.definition: The measuredValue of an Observation.

variants.name: numConstraints
variants.definition: Indicates the number of constraints (not counting populationType) defined for a particular StatisticalPopulation. This helps applications understand if they have access to a sufficiently complete description of a StatisticalPopulation.

variants.name: Observation
variants.definition: Instances of the class Observation are used to specify observations about an entity (which may or may not be an instance of a StatisticalPopulation), at a particular time. The principal properties of an Observation are observedNode, measuredProperty, measuredValue (or median, etc.) and observationDate (measuredProperty properties can, but need not always, be W3C RDF Data Cube "measure properties", as in the lifeExpectancy example). See also StatisticalPopulation, and the data and datasets overview for more details.

variants.name: observationDate
variants.definition: The observationDate of an Observation.

variants.name: observedNode
variants.definition: The observedNode of an Observation, often a StatisticalPopulation.

variants.name: occupationalCategory
variants.definition:
A category describing the job, preferably using a term from a taxonomy such as BLS O*NET-SOC, ISCO-08 or similar, with the property repeated for each applicable value. Ideally the taxonomy should be identified, and both the textual label and formal code for the category should be provided.

Note: for historical reasons, any textual label and formal code provided as a literal may be assumed to be from O*NET-SOC.

variants.name: occupationalCredentialAwarded
variants.definition: A description of the qualification, award, certificate, diploma or other occupational credential awarded as a consequence of successful completion of this course or program.

variants.name: offers
variants.definition: An offer to provide this item—for example, an offer to sell a product, rent the DVD of a movie, perform a service, or give away tickets to an event.

variants.name: orderDate
variants.definition: Date order was placed.

variants.name: OriginalShippingFees
variants.definition: OriginalShippingFees ...

variants.name: paymentDueDate
variants.definition: The date that payment is due.

variants.name: populationType
variants.definition: Indicates the populationType common to all members of a StatisticalPopulation.

variants.name: productReturnDays
variants.definition: The productReturnDays property indicates the number of days (from purchase) within which relevant product return policy is applicable.

variants.name: ProductReturnEnumeration
variants.definition: ProductReturnEnumeration enumerates several kinds of product return policy. Note that this structure may not capture all aspects of the policy.

variants.name: ProductReturnFiniteReturnWindow
variants.definition: ProductReturnFiniteReturnWindow: there is a finite window for product returns.

variants.name: productReturnLink
variants.definition: Indicates a Web page or service by URL, for product return.

variants.name: ProductReturnNotPermitted
variants.definition: ProductReturnNotPermitted: product returns are not permitted.

variants.name: ProductReturnPolicy
variants.definition: A ProductReturnPolicy provides information about product return policies associated with an Organization or Product.

variants.name: ProductReturnUnlimitedWindow
variants.definition: ProductReturnUnlimitedWindow: there is an unlimited window for product returns.

variants.name: ProductReturnUnspecified
variants.definition: ProductReturnUnspecified: a product return policy is not specified here.

variants.name: programPrerequisites
variants.definition: Prerequisites for enrolling in the program.

variants.name: provider
variants.definition: The service provider, service operator, or service performer; the goods producer. Another party (a seller) may offer those services or goods on behalf of the provider. A provider may also serve as the seller.

variants.name: ratingExplanation
variants.definition: A short explanation (e.g. one to two sentences) providing background context and other information that led to the conclusion expressed in the rating. This is particularly applicable to ratings associated with "fact check" markup using ClaimReview.

variants.name: refundType
variants.definition: A refundType, from an enumerated list.

variants.name: RefundTypeEnumeration
variants.definition: RefundTypeEnumeration enumerates several kinds of product return refund types.

variants.name: RestockingFees
variants.definition: RestockingFees ...

variants.name: returnFees
variants.definition: Indicates (via enumerated options) the return fees policy for a ProductReturnPolicy

variants.name: ReturnFeesEnumeration
variants.definition: ReturnFeesEnumeration expresses policies for return fees.

variants.name: returnPolicyCategory
variants.definition: A returnPolicyCategory expresses at most one of several enumerated kinds of return.

variants.name: ReturnShippingFees
variants.definition: ReturnShippingFees ...

variants.name: salaryUponCompletion
variants.definition: The expected salary upon completing the training.

variants.name: startTime
variants.definition:
The startTime of something. For a reserved event or service (e.g. FoodEstablishmentReservation), the time that it is expected to start. For actions that span a period of time, when the action was performed. e.g. John wrote a book from January to December. For media, including audio and video, it's the time offset of the start of a clip within a larger file.

Note that Event uses startDate/endDate instead of startTime/endTime, even when describing dates with times. This situation may be clarified in future revisions.

variants.name: StatisticalPopulation
variants.definition: A StatisticalPopulation is a set of instances of a certain given type that satisfy some set of constraints. The property populationType is used to specify the type. Any property that can be used on instances of that type can appear on the statistical population. For example, a StatisticalPopulation representing all Persons with a homeLocation of East Podunk California, would be described by applying the appropriate homeLocation and populationType properties to a StatisticalPopulation item that stands for that set of people. The properties numConstraints and constrainingProperties are used to specify which of the populations properties are used to specify the population. Note that the sense of "population" used here is the general sense of a statistical population, and does not imply that the population consists of people. For example, a populationType of Event or NewsArticle could be used. See also Observation, and the data and datasets overview for more details.

variants.name: StoreCreditRefund
variants.definition: A StoreCreditRefund ...

variants.name: subjectOf
variants.definition: A CreativeWork or Event about this Thing.

variants.name: timeToComplete
variants.definition: The expected length of time to complete the program if attending full-time.

variants.name: trainingSalary
variants.definition: The estimated salary earned while in the program.

variants.name: validFrom
variants.definition: The date when the item becomes valid.

variants.name: validThrough
variants.definition: The date after when the item is not valid. For example the end of an offer, salary period, or a period of opening hours.

variants.name: WorkBasedProgram
variants.definition: A program with both an educational and employment component. Typically based at a workplace and structured around work-based learning, with the aim of instilling competencies related to an occupation. WorkBasedProgram is used to distinguish programs such as apprenticeships from school, college or other classroom based educational programs.

variants.name: abstract
variants.definition: An abstract is a short description that summarizes a CreativeWork.

variants.name: accommodationCategory
variants.definition: Category of an Accommodation, following real estate conventions e.g. RESO (see PropertySubType, and PropertyType fields for suggested values).

variants.name: BenefitsHealthAspect
variants.definition: Content about the benefits and advantages of usage or utilization of topic.

variants.name: callSign
variants.definition: A callsign, as used in broadcasting and radio communications to identify people, radio and TV stations, or vehicles.

variants.name: CausesHealthAspect
variants.definition: Information about the causes and main actions that gave rise to the topic.

variants.name: ContagiousnessHealthAspect
variants.definition: Content about contagion mechanisms and contagiousness information over the topic.

variants.name: employmentUnit
variants.definition: Indicates the department, unit and/or facility where the employee reports and/or in which the job is to be performed.

variants.name: floorLevel
variants.definition: The floor level for an Accommodation in a multi-storey building. Since counting systems vary internationally, the local system should be used where possible.

variants.name: gender
variants.definition: Gender of something, typically a Person, but possibly also fictional characters, animals, etc. While http://schema.org/Male and http://schema.org/Female may be used, text strings are also acceptable for people who do not identify as a binary gender. The gender property can also be used in an extended sense to cover e.g. the gender of sports teams. As with the gender of individuals, we do not try to enumerate all possibilities. A mixed-gender SportsTeam can be indicated with a text value of "Mixed".

variants.name: hasHealthAspect
variants.definition: Indicates the aspect or aspects specifically addressed in some HealthTopicContent. For example, that the content is an overview, or that it talks about treatment, self-care, treatments or their side-effects.

variants.name: HealthAspectEnumeration
variants.definition: HealthAspectEnumeration enumerates several aspects of health content online, each of which might be described using hasHealthAspect and HealthTopicContent.

variants.name: HealthTopicContent
variants.definition: HealthTopicContent is WebContent that is about some aspect of a health topic, e.g. a condition, its symptoms or treatments. Such content may be comprised of several parts or sections and use different types of media. Multiple instances of WebContent (and hence HealthTopicContent) can be related using hasPart / isPartOf where there is some kind of content hierarchy, and their content described with about and mentions e.g. building upon the existing MedicalCondition vocabulary.

variants.name: HowOrWhereHealthAspect
variants.definition: Information about how or where to find a topic. Also may contain location data that can be used for where to look for help if the topic is observed.

variants.name: ineligibleRegion
variants.definition:
The ISO 3166-1 (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) or ISO 3166-2 code, the place, or the GeoShape for the geo-political region(s) for which the offer or delivery charge specification is not valid, e.g. a region where the transaction is not allowed.

See also eligibleRegion.

variants.name: latitude
variants.definition: The latitude of a location. For example 37.42242 (WGS 84).

variants.name: leaseLength
variants.definition: Length of the lease for some Accommodation, either particular to some Offer or in some cases intrinsic to the property.

variants.name: LivingWithHealthAspect
variants.definition: Information about coping or life related to the topic.

variants.name: longitude
variants.definition: The longitude of a location. For example -122.08585 (WGS 84).

variants.name: MayTreatHealthAspect
variants.definition: Related topics may be treated by a Topic.

variants.name: MisconceptionsHealthAspect
variants.definition: Content about common misconceptions and myths that are related to a topic.

variants.name: numberOfBathroomsTotal
variants.definition: The total integer number of bathrooms in a some Accommodation, following real estate conventions as documented in RESO: "The simple sum of the number of bathrooms. For example for a property with two Full Bathrooms and one Half Bathroom, the Bathrooms Total Integer will be 3.". See also numberOfRooms.

variants.name: numberOfFullBathrooms
variants.definition: Number of full bathrooms - The total number of full and ¾ bathrooms in an Accommodation. This corresponds to the BathroomsFull field in RESO.

variants.name: OfferForLease
variants.definition: An OfferForLease in Schema.org represents an Offer to lease out something, i.e. an Offer whose businessFunction is lease out. See Good Relations for background on the underlying concepts.

variants.name: OfferForPurchase
variants.definition: An OfferForPurchase in Schema.org represents an Offer to sell something, i.e. an Offer whose businessFunction is sell. See Good Relations for background on the underlying concepts.

variants.name: OverviewHealthAspect
variants.definition: Overview of the content. Contains a summarized view of the topic with the most relevant information for an introduction.

variants.name: PatientExperienceHealthAspect
variants.definition: Content about the real life experience of patients or people that have lived a similar experience about the topic. May be forums, topics, Q-and-A and related material.

variants.name: PodcastEpisode
variants.definition: A single episode of a podcast series.

variants.name: PodcastSeason
variants.definition: A single season of a podcast. Many podcasts do not break down into separate seasons. In that case, PodcastSeries should be used.

variants.name: PodcastSeries
variants.definition: A podcast is an episodic series of digital audio or video files which a user can download and listen to.

variants.name: PreventionHealthAspect
variants.definition: Information about actions or measures that can be taken to avoid getting the topic or reaching a critical situation related to the topic.

variants.name: PrognosisHealthAspect
variants.definition: Typical progression and happenings of life course of the topic.

variants.name: RealEstateListing
variants.definition: A RealEstateListing is a listing that describes one or more real-estate Offers (whose businessFunction is typically to lease out, or to sell). The RealEstateListing type itself represents the overall listing, as manifested in some WebPage.

variants.name: RelatedTopicsHealthAspect
variants.definition: Other prominent or relevant topics tied to the main topic.

variants.name: RisksOrComplicationsHealthAspect
variants.definition: Information about the risk factors and possible complications that may follow a topic.

variants.name: ScreeningHealthAspect
variants.definition: Content about how to screen or further filter a topic.

variants.name: SeeDoctorHealthAspect
variants.definition: Information about questions that may be asked, when to see a professional, measures before seeing a doctor or content about the first consultation.

variants.name: SelfCareHealthAspect
variants.definition: Self care actions or measures that can be taken to sooth, health or avoid a topic. This may be carried at home and can be carried/managed by the person itself.

variants.name: SideEffectsHealthAspect
variants.definition: Side effects that can be observed from the usage of the topic.

variants.name: skills
variants.definition: A statement of knowledge, skill, ability, task or any other assertion expressing a competency that is desired or required to fulfill this role or to work in this occupation.

variants.name: StagesHealthAspect
variants.definition: Stages that can be observed from a topic.

variants.name: subtitleLanguage
variants.definition: Languages in which subtitles/captions are available, in IETF BCP 47 standard format.

variants.name: SymptomsHealthAspect
variants.definition: Symptoms or related symptoms of a Topic.

variants.name: totalJobOpenings
variants.definition: The number of positions open for this job posting. Use a positive integer. Do not use if the number of positions is unclear or not known.

variants.name: TreatmentsHealthAspect
variants.definition: Treatments or related therapies for a Topic.

variants.name: TypesHealthAspect
variants.definition: Categorization and other types related to a topic.

variants.name: UsageOrScheduleHealthAspect
variants.definition: Content about how, when, frequency and dosage of a topic.

variants.name: WebContent
variants.definition: WebContent is a type representing all WebPage, WebSite and WebPageElement content. It is sometimes the case that detailed distinctions between Web pages, sites and their parts is not always important or obvious. The WebContent type makes it easier to describe Web-addressable content without requiring such distinctions to always be stated. (The intent is that the existing types WebPage, WebSite and WebPageElement will eventually be declared as subtypes of WebContent.)

variants.name: webFeed
variants.definition: The URL for the feed associated with the podcast series. This is usually RSS or Atom.

variants.name: accommodationFloorPlan
variants.definition: A floorplan of some Accommodation.

variants.name: acquireLicensePage
variants.definition: Indicates a page documenting how licenses can be purchased or otherwise acquired, for the current item.

variants.name: AggregateOffer
variants.definition:
When a single product is associated with multiple offers (for example, the same pair of shoes is offered by different merchants), then AggregateOffer can be used.

Note: AggregateOffers are normally expected to associate multiple offers that all share the same defined businessFunction value, or default to http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Sell if businessFunction is not explicitly defined.

variants.name: amenityFeature
variants.definition: An amenity feature (e.g. a characteristic or service) of the Accommodation. This generic property does not make a statement about whether the feature is included in an offer for the main accommodation or available at extra costs.

variants.name: announcementLocation
variants.definition: Indicates a specific CivicStructure or LocalBusiness associated with the SpecialAnnouncement. For example, a specific testing facility or business with special opening hours. For a larger geographic region like a quarantine of an entire region, use spatialCoverage.

variants.name: applicationContact
variants.definition: Contact details for further information relevant to this job posting.

variants.name: applicationDeadline
variants.definition: The date at which the program stops collecting applications for the next enrollment cycle.

variants.name: applicationStartDate
variants.definition: The date at which the program begins collecting applications for the next enrollment cycle.

variants.name: audio
variants.definition: An embedded audio object.

variants.name: AuthenticContent
variants.definition: AuthenticMediaObject: An unaltered image that is presented in an accurate way.

variants.name: byDay
variants.definition: Defines the day(s) of the week on which a recurring Event takes place. May be specified using either DayOfWeek, or alternatively Text conforming to iCal's syntax for byDay recurrence rules

variants.name: category
variants.definition: A category for the item. Greater signs or slashes can be used to informally indicate a category hierarchy.

variants.name: CovidTestingFacility
variants.definition: A CovidTestingFacility is a MedicalClinic where testing for the COVID-19 Coronavirus disease is available. If the facility is being made available from an established Pharmacy, Hotel, or other non-medical organization, multiple types can be listed. This makes it easier to re-use existing schema.org information about that place e.g. contact info, address, opening hours. Note that in an emergency, such information may not always be reliable.

variants.name: datePosted
variants.definition: Publication date of an online listing.

variants.name: datePublished
variants.definition: Date of first broadcast/publication.

variants.name: dayOfWeek
variants.definition: The day of the week for which these opening hours are valid.

variants.name: diseasePreventionInfo
variants.definition: Information about disease prevention.

variants.name: diseaseSpreadStatistics
variants.definition: Statistical information about the spread of a disease, either as WebContent, or described directly as a Dataset, or the specific Observations in the dataset. When a WebContent URL is provided, the page indicated might also contain more such markup.

variants.name: duration
variants.definition: The duration of the item (movie, audio recording, event, etc.) in ISO 8601 date format.

variants.name: educationalProgramMode
variants.definition: Similar to courseMode, The medium or means of delivery of the program as a whole. The value may either be a text label (e.g. "online", "onsite" or "blended"; "synchronous" or "asynchronous"; "full-time" or "part-time") or a URL reference to a term from a controlled vocabulary (e.g. https://ceds.ed.gov/element/001311#Asynchronous ).

variants.name: employerOverview
variants.definition: A description of the employer, career opportunities and work environment for this position.

variants.name: endDate
variants.definition: The end date and time of the item (in ISO 8601 date format).

variants.name: eventAttendanceMode
variants.definition: The eventAttendanceMode of an event indicates whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix.

variants.name: EventAttendanceModeEnumeration
variants.definition: An EventAttendanceModeEnumeration value is one of potentially several modes of organising an event, relating to whether it is online or offline.

variants.name: EventMovedOnline
variants.definition: Indicates that the event was changed to allow online participation. See eventAttendanceMode for specifics of whether it is now fully or partially online.

variants.name: eventSchedule
variants.definition: Associates an Event with a Schedule. There are circumstances where it is preferable to share a schedule for a series of repeating events rather than data on the individual events themselves. For example, a website or application might prefer to publish a schedule for a weekly gym class rather than provide data on every event. A schedule could be processed by applications to add forthcoming events to a calendar. An Event that is associated with a Schedule using this property should not have startDate or endDate properties. These are instead defined within the associated Schedule, this avoids any ambiguity for clients using the data. The property might have repeated values to specify different schedules, e.g. for different months or seasons.

variants.name: financialAidEligible
variants.definition: A financial aid type or program which students may use to pay for tuition or fees associated with the program.

variants.name: FloorPlan
variants.definition: A FloorPlan is an explicit representation of a collection of similar accommodations, allowing the provision of common information (room counts, sizes, layout diagrams) and offers for rental or sale. In typical use, some ApartmentComplex has an accommodationFloorPlan which is a FloorPlan. A FloorPlan is always in the context of a particular place, either a larger ApartmentComplex or a single Apartment. The visual/spatial aspects of a floor plan (i.e. room layout, see wikipedia) can be indicated using image.

variants.name: floorSize
variants.definition:
The size of the accommodation, e.g. in square meter or squarefoot.
Typical unit code(s): MTK for square meter, FTK for square foot, or YDK for square yard

variants.name: gettingTestedInfo
variants.definition: Information about getting tested (for a MedicalCondition), e.g. in the context of a pandemic.

variants.name: Guide
variants.definition: Guide is a page or article that recommend specific products or services, or aspects of a thing for a user to consider. A Guide may represent a Buying Guide and detail aspects of products or services for a user to consider. A Guide may represent a Product Guide and recommend specific products or services. A Guide may represent a Ranked List and recommend specific products or services with ranking.

variants.name: hasDriveThroughService
variants.definition: Indicates whether some facility (e.g. FoodEstablishment, CovidTestingFacility) offers a service that can be used by driving through in a car. In the case of CovidTestingFacility such facilities could potentially help with social distancing from other potentially-infected users.

variants.name: hasMerchantReturnPolicy
variants.definition: Indicates a MerchantReturnPolicy that may be applicable.

variants.name: ImageGallery
variants.definition: Web page type: Image gallery page.

variants.name: industry
variants.definition: The industry associated with the job position.

variants.name: inLanguage
variants.definition: The language of the content or performance or used in an action. Please use one of the language codes from the IETF BCP 47 standard. See also availableLanguage.

variants.name: inStoreReturnsOffered
variants.definition: Are in-store returns offered?

variants.name: interactionStatistic
variants.definition: The number of interactions for the CreativeWork using the WebSite or SoftwareApplication. The most specific child type of InteractionCounter should be used.

variants.name: isPartOf
variants.definition: Indicates an item or CreativeWork that this item, or CreativeWork (in some sense), is part of.

variants.name: isPlanForApartment
variants.definition: Indicates some accommodation that this floor plan describes.

variants.name: isResizable
variants.definition: Whether the 3DModel allows resizing. For example, room layout applications often do not allow 3DModel elements to be resized to reflect reality.

variants.name: itemOffered
variants.definition: An item being offered (or demanded). The transactional nature of the offer or demand is documented using businessFunction, e.g. sell, lease etc. While several common expected types are listed explicitly in this definition, others can be used. Using a second type, such as Product or a subtype of Product, can clarify the nature of the offer.

variants.name: leaseLength
variants.definition: Length of the lease for some Accommodation, either particular to some Offer or in some cases intrinsic to the property.

variants.name: location
variants.definition: The location of for example where the event is happening, an organization is located, or where an action takes place.

variants.name: maintainer
variants.definition: A maintainer of a Dataset, software package (SoftwareApplication), or other Project. A maintainer is a Person or Organization that manages contributions to, and/or publication of, some (typically complex) artifact. It is common for distributions of software and data to be based on "upstream" sources. When maintainer is applied to a specific version of something e.g. a particular version or packaging of a Dataset, it is always possible that the upstream source has a different maintainer. The isBasedOn property can be used to indicate such relationships between datasets to make the different maintenance roles clear. Similarly in the case of software, a package may have dedicated maintainers working on integration into software distributions such as Ubuntu, as well as upstream maintainers of the underlying work.

variants.name: maximumEnrollment
variants.definition: The maximum number of students who may be enrolled in the program.

variants.name: maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity
variants.definition: The maximum physical attendee capacity of an Event whose eventAttendanceMode is OfflineEventAttendanceMode (or the offline aspects, in the case of a MixedEventAttendanceMode).

variants.name: maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity
variants.definition: The maximum physical attendee capacity of an Event whose eventAttendanceMode is OnlineEventAttendanceMode (or the online aspects, in the case of a MixedEventAttendanceMode).

variants.name: mediaAuthenticityCategory
variants.definition: Indicates a MediaManipulationRatingEnumeration classification of a media object (in the context of how it was published or shared).

variants.name: MediaGallery
variants.definition: Web page type: Media gallery page. A mixed-media page that can contains media such as images, videos, and other multimedia.

variants.name: MediaManipulationRatingEnumeration
variants.definition: (editorial work in progress, this definition is incomplete and unreviewed) MediaManipulationRatingEnumeration classifies a number of ways in which a media item (video, image, audio) can be manipulated, taking into account the context within which they are published or presented.

variants.name: MediaReview
variants.definition: (editorial work in progress, this definition is incomplete and unreviewed) A MediaReview is a more specialized form of Review dedicated to the evaluation of media content online, typically in the context of fact-checking and misinformation. For more general reviews of media in the broader sense, use UserReview, CriticReview or other Review types.

variants.name: merchantReturnDays
variants.definition: The merchantReturnDays property indicates the number of days (from purchase) within which relevant merchant return policy is applicable.

variants.name: MerchantReturnEnumeration
variants.definition: MerchantReturnEnumeration enumerates several kinds of product return policy. Note that this structure may not capture all aspects of the policy.

variants.name: MerchantReturnFiniteReturnWindow
variants.definition: MerchantReturnFiniteReturnWindow: there is a finite window for product returns.

variants.name: merchantReturnLink
variants.definition: Indicates a Web page or service by URL, for product return.

variants.name: MerchantReturnNotPermitted
variants.definition: MerchantReturnNotPermitted: product returns are not permitted.

variants.name: MerchantReturnPolicy
variants.definition: A MerchantReturnPolicy provides information about product return policies associated with an Organization or Product.

variants.name: MerchantReturnUnlimitedWindow
variants.definition: MerchantReturnUnlimitedWindow: there is an unlimited window for product returns.

variants.name: MerchantReturnUnspecified
variants.definition: MerchantReturnUnspecified: a product return policy is not specified here.

variants.name: MissingContext
variants.definition: MissingContext: ...

variants.name: MixedEventAttendanceMode
variants.definition: MixedEventAttendanceMode - an event that is conducted as a combination of both offline and online modes.

variants.name: newsUpdatesAndGuidelines
variants.definition: Indicates a page with news updates and guidelines. This could often be (but is not required to be) the main page containing SpecialAnnouncement markup on a site.

variants.name: numberOfAccommodationUnits
variants.definition: Indicates the total (available plus unavailable) number of accommodation units in an ApartmentComplex, or the number of accommodation units for a specific FloorPlan (within its specific ApartmentComplex). See also numberOfAvailableAccommodationUnits.

variants.name: numberOfAvailableAccommodationUnits
variants.definition: Indicates the number of available accommodation units in an ApartmentComplex, or the number of accommodation units for a specific FloorPlan (within its specific ApartmentComplex). See also numberOfAccommodationUnits.

variants.name: numberOfBathroomsTotal
variants.definition: The total integer number of bathrooms in a some Accommodation, following real estate conventions as documented in RESO: "The simple sum of the number of bathrooms. For example for a property with two Full Bathrooms and one Half Bathroom, the Bathrooms Total Integer will be 3.". See also numberOfRooms.

variants.name: numberOfBedrooms
variants.definition: The total integer number of bedrooms in a some Accommodation, ApartmentComplex or FloorPlan.

variants.name: numberOfCredits
variants.definition: The number of credits or units awarded by a Course or required to complete an EducationalOccupationalProgram.

variants.name: numberOfFullBathrooms
variants.definition: Number of full bathrooms - The total number of full and ¾ bathrooms in an Accommodation. This corresponds to the BathroomsFull field in RESO.

variants.name: numberOfPartialBathrooms
variants.definition: Number of partial bathrooms - The total number of half and ¼ bathrooms in an Accommodation. This corresponds to the BathroomsPartial field in RESO.

variants.name: numberOfRooms
variants.definition:
The number of rooms (excluding bathrooms and closets) of the accommodation or lodging business.
Typical unit code(s): ROM for room or C62 for no unit. The type of room can be put in the unitText property of the QuantitativeValue.

variants.name: occupationalCategory
variants.definition:
A category describing the job, preferably using a term from a taxonomy such as BLS O*NET-SOC, ISCO-08 or similar, with the property repeated for each applicable value. Ideally the taxonomy should be identified, and both the textual label and formal code for the category should be provided.

Note: for historical reasons, any textual label and formal code provided as a literal may be assumed to be from O*NET-SOC.

variants.name: Offer
variants.definition:
An offer to transfer some rights to an item or to provide a service — for example, an offer to sell tickets to an event, to rent the DVD of a movie, to stream a TV show over the internet, to repair a motorcycle, or to loan a book.

Note: As the businessFunction property, which identifies the form of offer (e.g. sell, lease, repair, dispose), defaults to http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Sell; an Offer without a defined businessFunction value can be assumed to be an offer to sell.

For GTIN-related fields, see Check Digit calculator and validation guide from GS1.

variants.name: offers
variants.definition: An offer to provide this item—for example, an offer to sell a product, rent the DVD of a movie, perform a service, or give away tickets to an event. Use businessFunction to indicate the kind of transaction offered, i.e. sell, lease, etc. This property can also be used to describe a Demand. While this property is listed as expected on a number of common types, it can be used in others. In that case, using a second type, such as Product or a subtype of Product, can clarify the nature of the offer.

variants.name: OfferShippingDetails
variants.definition: OfferShippingDetails - indicates the kinds of shipping options might be available for an online shopping offer.

variants.name: OfflineEventAttendanceMode
variants.definition: OfflineEventAttendanceMode - an event that is primarily conducted offline.

variants.name: OnlineEventAttendanceMode
variants.definition: OnlineEventAttendanceMode - an event that is primarily conducted online.

variants.name: petsAllowed
variants.definition: Indicates whether pets are allowed to enter the accommodation or lodging business. More detailed information can be put in a text value.

variants.name: phoneticText
variants.definition: Representation of a text textValue using the specified speechToTextMarkup. For example the city name of Houston in IPA: /ˈhjuːstən/.

variants.name: physicalRequirement
variants.definition: A description of the types of physical activity associated with the job. Defined terms such as those in O*net may be used, but note that there is no way to specify the level of ability as well as its nature when using a defined term.

variants.name: programType
variants.definition: The type of educational or occupational program. For example, classroom, internship, alternance, etc..

variants.name: PronounceableText
variants.definition: Data type: PronounceableText.

variants.name: publicTransportClosuresInfo
variants.definition: Information about public transport closures.

variants.name: quarantineGuidelines
variants.definition: Guidelines about quarantine rules, e.g. in the context of a pandemic.

variants.name: Recommendation
variants.definition: Recommendation is a type of Review that suggests or proposes something as the best option or best course of action. Recommendations may be for products or services, or other concrete things, as in the case of a ranked list or product guide. A Guide may list multiple recommendations for different categories. For example, in a Guide about which TVs to buy, the author may have several Recommendations.

variants.name: refundType
variants.definition: A refundType, from an enumerated list.

variants.name: returnFees
variants.definition: Indicates (via enumerated options) the return fees policy for a MerchantReturnPolicy

variants.name: returnPolicyCategory
variants.definition: A returnPolicyCategory expresses at most one of several enumerated kinds of return.

variants.name: reviewAspect
variants.definition: This Review or Rating is relevant to this part or facet of the itemReviewed.

variants.name: Schedule
variants.definition: A schedule defines a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring Event. At a minimum a schedule will specify repeatFrequency which describes the interval between occurences of the event. Additional information can be provided to specify the schedule more precisely. This includes identifying the day(s) of the week or month when the recurring event will take place, in addition to its start and end time. Schedules may also have start and end dates to indicate when they are active, e.g. to define a limited calendar of events.

variants.name: scheduleTimezone
variants.definition: Indicates the timezone for which the time(s) indicated in the Schedule are given. The value provided should be among those listed in the IANA Time Zone Database.

variants.name: schoolClosuresInfo
variants.definition: Information about school closures.

variants.name: SchoolDistrict
variants.definition: A School District is an administrative area for the administration of schools.

variants.name: season
variants.definition: A season in a media series.

variants.name: securityClearanceRequirement
variants.definition: A description of any security clearance requirements of the job.

variants.name: sensoryRequirement
variants.definition: A description of any sensory requirements and levels necessary to function on the job, including hearing and vision. Defined terms such as those in O*net may be used, but note that there is no way to specify the level of ability as well as its nature when using a defined term.

variants.name: shippingDestination
variants.definition: shippingDestination indicates the target region for an online shipping destination.

variants.name: SpecialAnnouncement
variants.definition:
A SpecialAnnouncement combines a simple date-stamped textual information update with contextualized Web links and other structured data. It represents an information update made by a locally-oriented organization, for example schools, pharmacies, healthcare providers, community groups, police, local government.

For work in progress guidelines on Coronavirus-related markup see this doc.

The motivating scenario for SpecialAnnouncement is the Coronavirus pandemic, and the initial vocabulary is oriented to this urgent situation. Schema.org expect to improve the markup iteratively as it is deployed and as feedback emerges from use. In addition to our usual Github entry, feedback comments can also be provided in this document.

While this schema is designed to communicate urgent crisis-related information, it is not the same as an emergency warning technology like CAP, although there may be overlaps. The intent is to cover the kinds of everyday practical information being posted to existing websites during an emergency situation.

Several kinds of information can be provided:

We encourage the provision of "name", "text", "datePosted", "expires" (if appropriate), "category" and "url" as a simple baseline. It is important to provide a value for "category" where possible, most ideally as a well known URL from Wikipedia or Wikidata. In the case of the 2019-2020 Coronavirus pandemic, this should be "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2019-20_coronavirus_pandemic" or "https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q81068910".

For many of the possible properties, values can either be simple links or an inline description, depending on whether a summary is available. For a link, provide just the URL of the appropriate page as the property's value. For an inline description, use a WebContent type, and provide the url as a property of that, alongside at least a simple "text" summary of the page. It is unlikely that a single SpecialAnnouncement will need all of the possible properties simultaneously.

We expect that in many cases the page referenced might contain more specialized structured data, e.g. contact info, openingHours, Event, FAQPage etc. By linking to those pages from a SpecialAnnouncement you can help make it clearer that the events are related to the situation (e.g. Coronavirus) indicated by the category property of the SpecialAnnouncement.

Many SpecialAnnouncements will relate to particular regions and to identifiable local organizations. Use spatialCoverage for the region, and announcementLocation to indicate specific LocalBusinesses and CivicStructures. If the announcement affects both a particular region and a specific location (for example, a library closure that serves an entire region), use both spatialCoverage and announcementLocation.

The about property can be used to indicate entities that are the focus of the announcement. We now recommend using about only for representing non-location entities (e.g. a Course or a RadioStation). For places, use announcementLocation and spatialCoverage. Consumers of this markup should be aware that the initial design encouraged the use of /about for locations too.

The basic content of SpecialAnnouncement is similar to that of an RSS or Atom feed. For publishers without such feeds, basic feed-like information can be shared by posting SpecialAnnouncement updates in a page, e.g. using JSON-LD. For sites with Atom/RSS functionality, you can point to a feed with the webFeed property. This can be a simple URL, or an inline DataFeed object, with encodingFormat providing media type information e.g. "application/rss+xml" or "application/atom+xml".

variants.name: speechToTextMarkup
variants.definition: Form of markup used. eg. SSML or IPA.

variants.name: sport
variants.definition: A type of sport (e.g. Baseball).

variants.name: startDate
variants.definition: The start date and time of the item (in ISO 8601 date format).

variants.name: termDuration
variants.definition: The amount of time in a term as defined by the institution. A term is a length of time where students take one or more classes. Semesters and quarters are common units for term.

variants.name: termsPerYear
variants.definition: The number of times terms of study are offered per year. Semesters and quarters are common units for term. For example, if the student can only take 2 semesters for the program in one year, then termsPerYear should be 2.

variants.name: textValue
variants.definition: Text value being annotated.

variants.name: timeOfDay
variants.definition: The time of day the program normally runs. For example, "evenings".

variants.name: tourBookingPage
variants.definition: A page providing information on how to book a tour of some Place, such as an Accommodation or ApartmentComplex in a real estate setting, as well as other kinds of tours as appropriate.

variants.name: trainingSalary
variants.definition: The estimated salary earned while in the program.

variants.name: travelBans
variants.definition: Information about travel bans, e.g. in the context of a pandemic.

variants.name: typicalCreditsPerTerm
variants.definition: The number of credits or units a full-time student would be expected to take in 1 term however 'term' is defined by the institution.

variants.name: usageInfo
variants.definition:
The schema.org usageInfo property indicates further information about a CreativeWork. This property is applicable both to works that are freely available and to those that require payment or other transactions. It can reference additional information e.g. community expectations on preferred linking and citation conventions, as well as purchasing details. For something that can be commercially licensed, usageInfo can provide detailed, resource-specific information about licensing options.

This property can be used alongside the license property which indicates license(s) applicable to some piece of content. The usageInfo property can provide information about other licensing options, e.g. acquiring commercial usage rights for an image that is also available under non-commercial creative commons licenses.

variants.name: VideoGallery
variants.definition: Web page type: Video gallery page.

variants.name: VirtualLocation
variants.definition: An online or virtual location for attending events. For example, one may attend an online seminar or educational event. While a virtual location may be used as the location of an event, virtual locations should not be confused with physical locations in the real world.

variants.name: webFeed
variants.definition: The URL for a feed, e.g. associated with a podcast series, blog, or series of date-stamped updates. This is usually RSS or Atom.

variants.name: yearBuilt
variants.definition: The year an Accommodation was constructed. This corresponds to the YearBuilt field in RESO.

variants.name: 3DModel
variants.definition: A 3D model represents some kind of 3D content, which may have encodings in one or more MediaObjects. Many 3D formats are available (e.g. see Wikipedia); specific encoding formats can be represented using the encodingFormat property applied to the relevant MediaObject. For the case of a single file published after Zip compression, the convention of appending '+zip' to the encodingFormat can be used. Geospatial, AR/VR, artistic/animation, gaming, engineering and scientific content can all be represented using 3DModel.

variants.name: addressCountry
variants.definition: The country. For example, USA. You can also provide the two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

variants.name: addressRegion
variants.definition: The region in which the locality is, and which is in the country. For example, California or another appropriate first-level Administrative division

variants.name: AlignmentObject
variants.definition:
An intangible item that describes an alignment between a learning resource and a node in an educational framework.

Should not be used where the nature of the alignment can be described using a simple property, for example to express that a resource teaches or assesses a competency.

variants.name: alignmentType
variants.definition: A category of alignment between the learning resource and the framework node. Recommended values include: 'requires', 'textComplexity', 'readingLevel', and 'educationalSubject'.

variants.name: assesses
variants.definition: The item being described is intended to assess the competency or learning outcome defined by the referenced term.

variants.name: BasicIncome
variants.definition: BasicIncome: this is a benefit for basic income.

variants.name: businessDays
variants.definition: Days of the week when the merchant typically operates, indicated via opening hours markup.

variants.name: BusinessSupport
variants.definition: BusinessSupport: this is a benefit for supporting businesses.

variants.name: category
variants.definition: A category for the item. Greater signs or slashes can be used to informally indicate a category hierarchy.

variants.name: CDCPMDRecord
variants.definition: A CDCPMDRecord is a data structure representing a record in a CDC tabular data format used for hospital data reporting. See documentation for details, and the linked CDC materials for authoritative definitions used as the source here.

variants.name: CharitableIncorporatedOrganization
variants.definition: CharitableIncorporatedOrganization: Non-profit type referring to a Charitable Incorporated Organization (UK).

variants.name: cutoffTime
variants.definition: Order cutoff time allows merchants to describe the time after which they will no longer process orders received on that day. For orders processed after cutoff time, one day gets added to the delivery time estimate. This property is expected to be most typically used via the ShippingRateSettings publication pattern. The time is indicated using the time notation from the ISO-8601 DateTime format, e.g. 14:45:15Z would represent a daily cutoff at 14:45h UTC.

variants.name: cvdCollectionDate
variants.definition: collectiondate - Date for which patient counts are reported.

variants.name: cvdFacilityCounty
variants.definition: Name of the County of the NHSN facility that this data record applies to. Use cvdFacilityId to identify the facility. To provide other details, healthcareReportingData can be used on a Hospital entry.

variants.name: cvdFacilityId
variants.definition: Identifier of the NHSN facility that this data record applies to. Use cvdFacilityCounty to indicate the county. To provide other details, healthcareReportingData can be used on a Hospital entry.

variants.name: cvdNumBeds
variants.definition: numbeds - HOSPITAL INPATIENT BEDS: Inpatient beds, including all staffed, licensed, and overflow (surge) beds used for inpatients.

variants.name: cvdNumBedsOcc
variants.definition: numbedsocc - HOSPITAL INPATIENT BED OCCUPANCY: Total number of staffed inpatient beds that are occupied.

variants.name: cvdNumC19Died
variants.definition: numc19died - DEATHS: Patients with suspected or confirmed COVID-19 who died in the hospital, ED, or any overflow location.

variants.name: cvdNumC19HOPats
variants.definition: numc19hopats - HOSPITAL ONSET: Patients hospitalized in an NHSN inpatient care location with onset of suspected or confirmed COVID-19 14 or more days after hospitalization.

variants.name: cvdNumC19HospPats
variants.definition: numc19hosppats - HOSPITALIZED: Patients currently hospitalized in an inpatient care location who have suspected or confirmed COVID-19.

variants.name: cvdNumC19MechVentPats
variants.definition: numc19mechventpats - HOSPITALIZED and VENTILATED: Patients hospitalized in an NHSN inpatient care location who have suspected or confirmed COVID-19 and are on a mechanical ventilator.

variants.name: cvdNumC19OFMechVentPats
variants.definition: numc19ofmechventpats - ED/OVERFLOW and VENTILATED: Patients with suspected or confirmed COVID-19 who are in the ED or any overflow location awaiting an inpatient bed and on a mechanical ventilator.

variants.name: cvdNumC19OverflowPats
variants.definition: numc19overflowpats - ED/OVERFLOW: Patients with suspected or confirmed COVID-19 who are in the ED or any overflow location awaiting an inpatient bed.

variants.name: cvdNumICUBeds
variants.definition: numicubeds - ICU BEDS: Total number of staffed inpatient intensive care unit (ICU) beds.

variants.name: cvdNumICUBedsOcc
variants.definition: numicubedsocc - ICU BED OCCUPANCY: Total number of staffed inpatient ICU beds that are occupied.

variants.name: cvdNumTotBeds
variants.definition: numtotbeds - ALL HOSPITAL BEDS: Total number of all Inpatient and outpatient beds, including all staffed,ICU, licensed, and overflow (surge) beds used for inpatients or outpatients.

variants.name: cvdNumVent
variants.definition: numvent - MECHANICAL VENTILATORS: Total number of ventilators available.

variants.name: cvdNumVentUse
variants.definition: numventuse - MECHANICAL VENTILATORS IN USE: Total number of ventilators in use.

variants.name: datePosted
variants.definition: Publication date of an online listing.

variants.name: DefinedRegion
variants.definition:
A DefinedRegion is a geographic area defined by potentially arbitrary (rather than political, administrative or natural geographical) criteria. Properties are provided for defining a region by reference to sets of postal codes.

Examples: a delivery destination when shopping. Region where regional pricing is configured.

Requirement 1: Country: US States: "NY", "CA"

Requirement 2: Country: US PostalCode Set: { [94000-94585], [97000, 97999], [13000, 13599]} { [12345, 12345], [78945, 78945], } Region = state, canton, prefecture, autonomous community...

variants.name: deliveryTime
variants.definition: The total delay between the receipt of the order and the goods reaching the final customer.

variants.name: DeliveryTimeSettings
variants.definition: A DeliveryTimeSettings represents re-usable pieces of shipping information, relating to timing. It is designed for publication on an URL that may be referenced via the shippingSettingsLink property of a OfferShippingSpecification. Several occurrences can be published, distinguished (and identified/referenced) by their different values for shippingLabel.

variants.name: DisabilitySupport
variants.definition: DisabilitySupport: this is a benefit for disability support.

variants.name: doesNotShip
variants.definition: Indicates, as part of an OfferShippingDetails, when shipping to a particular shippingDestination is not available.

variants.name: editEIDR
variants.definition:
An EIDR (Entertainment Identifier Registry) identifier representing a specific edit / edition for a work of film or television.

For example, the motion picture known as "Ghostbusters" whose titleEIDR is "10.5240/7EC7-228A-510A-053E-CBB8-J", has several edits e.g. "10.5240/1F2A-E1C5-680A-14C6-E76B-I" and "10.5240/8A35-3BEE-6497-5D12-9E4F-3".

Since schema.org types like Movie and TVEpisode can be used for both works and their multiple expressions, it is possible to use titleEIDR alone (for a general description), or alongside editEIDR for a more edit-specific description.

variants.name: educationalAlignment
variants.definition:
An alignment to an established educational framework.

This property should not be used where the nature of the alignment can be described using a simple property, for example to express that a resource teaches or assesses a competency.

variants.name: educationalLevel
variants.definition: The level in terms of progression through an educational or training context. Examples of educational levels include 'beginner', 'intermediate' or 'advanced', and formal sets of level indicators.

variants.name: EducationalOrganization
variants.definition: An educational organization.

variants.name: eligibilityToWorkRequirement
variants.definition: The legal requirements such as citizenship, visa and other documentation required for an applicant to this job.

variants.name: endTime
variants.definition:
The endTime of something. For a reserved event or service (e.g. FoodEstablishmentReservation), the time that it is expected to end. For actions that span a period of time, when the action was performed. e.g. John wrote a book from January to December. For media, including audio and video, it's the time offset of the end of a clip within a larger file.

Note that Event uses startDate/endDate instead of startTime/endTime, even when describing dates with times. This situation may be clarified in future revisions.

variants.name: freeShippingThreshold
variants.definition: A monetary value above which (or equal to) the shipping rate becomes free. Intended to be used via an OfferShippingSpecification with shippingSettingsLink matching this ShippingSettings.

variants.name: governmentBenefitsInfo
variants.definition: governmentBenefitsInfo provides information about government benefits associated with a SpecialAnnouncement.

variants.name: GovernmentBenefitsType
variants.definition: GovernmentBenefitsType enumerates several kinds of government benefits to support the COVID-19 situation. Note that this structure may not capture all benefits offered.

variants.name: Hackathon
variants.definition: A hackathon event.

variants.name: handlingTime
variants.definition: The typical delay between the receipt of the order and the goods either leaving the warehouse or being prepared for pickup, in case the delivery method is on site pickup. Typical properties: minValue, maxValue, unitCode (d for DAY).  This is by common convention assumed to mean business days (if a unitCode is used, coded as "d"), i.e. only counting days when the business normally operates.

variants.name: HealthCare
variants.definition: HealthCare: this is a benefit for health care.

variants.name: healthcareReportingData
variants.definition: Indicates data describing a hospital, e.g. a CDC CDCPMDRecord or as some kind of Dataset.

variants.name: isUnlabelledFallback
variants.definition: This can be marked 'true' to indicate that some published ShippingRateSettings are intended to apply to all OfferShippingDetails published by the same merchant, when referenced by a shippingSettingsLink in those settings. It is not meaningful to use a 'true' value for this property alongside a shippingLabel, since this property is for use with unlabelled ShippingRateSettings.

variants.name: jurisdiction
variants.definition: Indicates a legal jurisdiction, e.g. of some legislation, or where some government service is based.

variants.name: LimitedByGuaranteeCharity
variants.definition: LimitedByGuaranteeCharity: Non-profit type referring to a charitable company that is limited by guarantee (UK).

variants.name: NLNonprofitType
variants.definition: NLNonprofitType: Non-profit organization type originating from the Netherlands.

variants.name: Nonprofit501a
variants.definition: Nonprofit501a: Non-profit type referring to Farmers’ Cooperative Associations.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c1
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c1: Non-profit type referring to Corporations Organized Under Act of Congress, including Federal Credit Unions and National Farm Loan Associations.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c10
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c10: Non-profit type referring to Domestic Fraternal Societies and Associations.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c11
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c11: Non-profit type referring to Teachers' Retirement Fund Associations.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c12
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c12: Non-profit type referring to Benevolent Life Insurance Associations, Mutual Ditch or Irrigation Companies, Mutual or Cooperative Telephone Companies.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c13
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c13: Non-profit type referring to Cemetery Companies.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c14
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c14: Non-profit type referring to State-Chartered Credit Unions, Mutual Reserve Funds.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c15
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c15: Non-profit type referring to Mutual Insurance Companies or Associations.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c16
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c16: Non-profit type referring to Cooperative Organizations to Finance Crop Operations.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c17
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c17: Non-profit type referring to Supplemental Unemployment Benefit Trusts.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c18
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c18: Non-profit type referring to Employee Funded Pension Trust (created before 25 June 1959).

variants.name: Nonprofit501c19
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c19: Non-profit type referring to Post or Organization of Past or Present Members of the Armed Forces.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c2
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c2: Non-profit type referring to Title-holding Corporations for Exempt Organizations.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c20
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c20: Non-profit type referring to Group Legal Services Plan Organizations.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c21
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c21: Non-profit type referring to Black Lung Benefit Trusts.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c22
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c22: Non-profit type referring to Withdrawal Liability Payment Funds.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c23
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c23: Non-profit type referring to Veterans Organizations.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c24
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c24: Non-profit type referring to Section 4049 ERISA Trusts.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c25
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c25: Non-profit type referring to Real Property Title-Holding Corporations or Trusts with Multiple Parents.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c26
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c26: Non-profit type referring to State-Sponsored Organizations Providing Health Coverage for High-Risk Individuals.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c27
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c27: Non-profit type referring to State-Sponsored Workers' Compensation Reinsurance Organizations.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c28
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c28: Non-profit type referring to National Railroad Retirement Investment Trusts.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c3
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c3: Non-profit type referring to Religious, Educational, Charitable, Scientific, Literary, Testing for Public Safety, to Foster National or International Amateur Sports Competition, or Prevention of Cruelty to Children or Animals Organizations.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c4
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c4: Non-profit type referring to Civic Leagues, Social Welfare Organizations, and Local Associations of Employees.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c5
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c5: Non-profit type referring to Labor, Agricultural and Horticultural Organizations.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c6
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c6: Non-profit type referring to Business Leagues, Chambers of Commerce, Real Estate Boards.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c7
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c7: Non-profit type referring to Social and Recreational Clubs.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c8
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c8: Non-profit type referring to Fraternal Beneficiary Societies and Associations.

variants.name: Nonprofit501c9
variants.definition: Nonprofit501c9: Non-profit type referring to Voluntary Employee Beneficiary Associations.

variants.name: Nonprofit501d
variants.definition: Nonprofit501d: Non-profit type referring to Religious and Apostolic Associations.

variants.name: Nonprofit501e
variants.definition: Nonprofit501e: Non-profit type referring to Cooperative Hospital Service Organizations.

variants.name: Nonprofit501f
variants.definition: Nonprofit501f: Non-profit type referring to Cooperative Service Organizations.

variants.name: Nonprofit501k
variants.definition: Nonprofit501k: Non-profit type referring to Child Care Organizations.

variants.name: Nonprofit501n
variants.definition: Nonprofit501n: Non-profit type referring to Charitable Risk Pools.

variants.name: Nonprofit501q
variants.definition: Nonprofit501q: Non-profit type referring to Credit Counseling Organizations.

variants.name: Nonprofit527
variants.definition: Nonprofit527: Non-profit type referring to Political organizations.

variants.name: NonprofitANBI
variants.definition: NonprofitANBI: Non-profit type referring to a Public Benefit Organization (NL).

variants.name: NonprofitSBBI
variants.definition: NonprofitSBBI: Non-profit type referring to a Social Interest Promoting Institution (NL).

variants.name: nonprofitStatus
variants.definition: nonprofit Status indicates the legal status of a non-profit organization in its primary place of business.

variants.name: NonprofitType
variants.definition: NonprofitType enumerates several kinds of official non-profit types of which a non-profit organization can be.

variants.name: OfferShippingDetails
variants.definition:
OfferShippingDetails represents information about shipping destinations.

Multiple of these entities can be used to represent different shipping rates for different destinations:

One entity for Alaska/Hawaii. A different one for continental US.A different one for all France.

Multiple of these entities can be used to represent different shipping costs and delivery times.

Two entities that are identical but differ in rate and time:

e.g. Cheaper and slower: $5 in 5-7days or Fast and expensive: $15 in 1-2 days

variants.name: OneTimePayments
variants.definition: OneTimePayments: this is a benefit for one-time payments for individuals.

variants.name: PaidLeave
variants.definition: PaidLeave: this is a benefit for paid leave.

variants.name: ParentalSupport
variants.definition: ParentalSupport: this is a benefit for parental support.

variants.name: postalCode
variants.definition: The postal code. For example, 94043.

variants.name: postalCodeBegin
variants.definition: First postal code in a range (included).

variants.name: postalCodeEnd
variants.definition: Last postal code in the range (included). Needs to be after postalCodeBegin.

variants.name: postalCodePrefix
variants.definition: A defined range of postal codes indicated by a common textual prefix. Used for non-numeric systems such as UK.

variants.name: postalCodeRange
variants.definition: A defined range of postal codes.

variants.name: PostalCodeRangeSpecification
variants.definition: Indicates a range of postalcodes, usually defined as the set of valid codes between postalCodeBegin and postalCodeEnd, inclusively.

variants.name: serviceType
variants.definition: The type of service being offered, e.g. veterans' benefits, emergency relief, etc.

variants.name: ShippingDeliveryTime
variants.definition: ShippingDeliveryTime provides various pieces of information about delivery times for shipping.

variants.name: shippingDestination
variants.definition: indicates (possibly multiple) shipping destinations. These can be defined in several ways e.g. postalCode ranges.

variants.name: shippingDetails
variants.definition: Indicates information about the shipping policies and options associated with an Offer.

variants.name: shippingLabel
variants.definition: Label to match an OfferShippingDetails with a ShippingRateSettings (within the context of a shippingSettingsLink cross-reference).

variants.name: shippingRate
variants.definition: The shipping rate is the cost of shipping to the specified destination. Typically, the maxValue and currency values (of the MonetaryAmount) are most appropriate.

variants.name: ShippingRateSettings
variants.definition: A ShippingRateSettings represents re-usable pieces of shipping information. It is designed for publication on an URL that may be referenced via the shippingSettingsLink property of a OfferShippingSpecification. Several occurrences can be published, distinguished and matched (i.e. identified/referenced) by their different values for shippingLabel.

variants.name: shippingSettingsLink
variants.definition: Link to a page containing ShippingRateSettings and DeliveryTimeSettings details.

variants.name: startTime
variants.definition:
The startTime of something. For a reserved event or service (e.g. FoodEstablishmentReservation), the time that it is expected to start. For actions that span a period of time, when the action was performed. e.g. John wrote a book from January to December. For media, including audio and video, it's the time offset of the start of a clip within a larger file.

Note that Event uses startDate/endDate instead of startTime/endTime, even when describing dates with times. This situation may be clarified in future revisions.

variants.name: teaches
variants.definition: The item being described is intended to help a person learn the competency or learning outcome defined by the referenced term.

variants.name: titleEIDR
variants.definition:
An EIDR (Entertainment Identifier Registry) identifier representing at the most general/abstract level, a work of film or television.

For example, the motion picture known as "Ghostbusters" has a titleEIDR of "10.5240/7EC7-228A-510A-053E-CBB8-J". This title (or work) may have several variants, which EIDR calls "edits". See editEIDR.
