Many [[SpecialAnnouncement]]s will relate to particular regions and to identifiable local organizations. Use [[spatialCoverage]] for the region, and [[announcementLocation]] to indicate specific [[LocalBusiness]]es and [[CivicStructures]]. If the announcement affects both a particular region and a specific location (for example, a library closure that serves an entire region), use both [[spatialCoverage]] and [[announcementLocation]].

The [[about]] property can be used to indicate entities that are the focus of the announcement. We now recommend using [[about]] only
for representing non-location entities (e.g. a [[Course]] or a [[RadioStation]]). For places, use [[announcementLocation]] and [[spatialCoverage]]. Consumers of this markup should be aware that the initial design encouraged the use of /about for locations too.

The basic content of [[SpecialAnnouncement]] is similar to that of an [RSS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RSS) or [Atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom_(Web_standard)) feed. For publishers without such feeds, basic feed-like information can be shared by posting
[[SpecialAnnouncement]] updates in a page, e.g. using JSON-LD. For sites with Atom/RSS functionality, you can point to a feed
with the [[webFeed]] property. This can be a simple URL, or an inline [[DataFeed]] object, with [[encodingFormat]] providing
media type information e.g. "application/rss+xml" or "application/atom+xml".

variants.name: specialOpeningHoursSpecification
variants.definition: The special opening hours of a certain place.\n\nUse this to explicitly override general opening hours brought in scope by [[openingHoursSpecification]] or [[openingHours]].

variants.name: speechToTextMarkup
variants.definition: Form of markup used. eg. [SSML](https://www.w3.org/TR/speech-synthesis11) or [IPA](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Property:P898).

variants.name: speed
variants.definition:
The speed range of the vehicle. If the vehicle is powered by an engine, the upper limit of the speed range (indicated by [[maxValue]] should be the maximum speed achievable under regular conditions.

Typical unit code(s): KMH for km/h, HM for mile per hour (0.447 04 m/s), KNT for knot

*Note 1: Use [[minValue]] and [[maxValue]] to indicate the range. Typically, the minimal value is zero.
* Note 2: There are many different ways of measuring the speed range. You can link to information about how the given value has been determined using the [[valueReference]] property.

variants.name: SRP
variants.definition: Represents the suggested retail price ("SRP") of an offered product.

variants.name: startDate
variants.definition: The start date and time of the item (in [ISO 8601 date format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)).

variants.name: startOffset
variants.definition: The start time of the clip expressed as the number of seconds from the beginning of the work.

variants.name: startTime
variants.definition: The startTime of something. For a reserved event or service (e.g. FoodEstablishmentReservation), the time that it is expected to start. For actions that span a period of time, when the action was performed. e.g. John wrote a book from *January* to December. For media, including audio and video, it's the time offset of the start of a clip within a larger file.\n\nNote that Event uses startDate/endDate instead of startTime/endTime, even when describing dates with times. This situation may be clarified in future revisions.

variants.name: StatisticalPopulation
variants.definition:
A StatisticalPopulation is a set of instances of a certain given type that satisfy some set of constraints. The property [[populationType]] is used to specify the type. Any property that can be used on instances of that type can appear on the statistical population. For example, a [[StatisticalPopulation]] representing all [[Person]]s with a [[homeLocation]] of East Podunk California, would be described by applying the appropriate [[homeLocation]] and [[populationType]] properties to a [[StatisticalPopulation]] item that stands for that set of people.
The properties [[numConstraints]] and [[constrainingProperties]] are used to specify which of the populations properties are used to specify the population. Note that the sense of "population" used here is the general sense of a statistical
population, and does not imply that the population consists of people. For example, a [[populationType]] of [[Event]] or [[NewsArticle]] could be used. See also [[Observation]], and the [data and datasets](/docs/data-and-datasets.html) overview for more details.

variants.name: SubscribeAction
variants.definition:
The act of forming a personal connection with someone/something (object) unidirectionally/asymmetrically to get updates pushed to.

Related actions:

* [[FollowAction]]: Unlike FollowAction, SubscribeAction implies that the subscriber acts as a passive agent being constantly/actively pushed for updates.
* [[RegisterAction]]: Unlike RegisterAction, SubscribeAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object.
* [[JoinAction]]: Unlike JoinAction, SubscribeAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object.

variants.name: Subscription
variants.definition: Represents the subscription pricing component of the total price for an offered product

variants.name: subtitleLanguage
variants.definition: Languages in which subtitles/captions are available, in [IETF BCP 47 standard format](http://tools.ietf.org/html/bcp47).

variants.name: subTrip
variants.definition: Identifies a [[Trip]] that is a subTrip of this Trip.  For example Day 1, Day 2, etc. of a multi-day trip.

variants.name: Suite
variants.definition:
A suite in a hotel or other public accommodation, denotes a class of luxury accommodations, the key feature of which is multiple rooms (Source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suite_(hotel)).

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

variants.name: TakeAction
variants.definition:
The act of gaining ownership of an object from an origin. Reciprocal of GiveAction.

Related actions:

* [[GiveAction]]: The reciprocal of TakeAction.
* [[ReceiveAction]]: Unlike ReceiveAction, TakeAction implies that ownership has been transfered.

variants.name: TaxiReservation
variants.definition: A reservation for a taxi.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, use [[Offer]].

variants.name: temporal
variants.definition:
The "temporal" property can be used in cases where more specific properties
(e.g. [[temporalCoverage]], [[dateCreated]], [[dateModified]], [[datePublished]]) are not known to be appropriate.

variants.name: temporalCoverage
variants.definition:
The temporalCoverage of a CreativeWork indicates the period that the content applies to, i.e. that it describes, either as a DateTime or as a textual string indicating a time period in [ISO 8601 time interval format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601#Time_intervals). In
      the case of a Dataset it will typically indicate the relevant time period in a precise notation (e.g. for a 2011 census dataset, the year 2011 would be written "2011/2012"). Other forms of content e.g. ScholarlyArticle, Book, TVSeries or TVEpisode may indicate their temporalCoverage in broader terms - textually or via well-known URL.
      Written works such as books may sometimes have precise temporal coverage too, e.g. a work set in 1939 - 1945 can be indicated in ISO 8601 interval format format via "1939/1945".

Open-ended date ranges can be written with ".." in place of the end date. For example, "2015-11/.." indicates a range beginning in November 2015 and with no specified final date. This is tentative and might be updated in future when ISO 8601 is officially updated.

variants.name: termCode
variants.definition: A code that identifies this [[DefinedTerm]] within a [[DefinedTermSet]]

variants.name: Time
variants.definition: A point in time recurring on multiple days in the form hh:mm:ss[Z|(+|-)hh:mm] (see [XML schema for details](http://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-2/#time)).

variants.name: titleEIDR
variants.definition:
An [EIDR](https://eidr.org/) (Entertainment Identifier Registry) [[identifier]] representing at the most general/abstract level, a work of film or television.

For example, the motion picture known as "Ghostbusters" has a titleEIDR of  "10.5240/7EC7-228A-510A-053E-CBB8-J". This title (or work) may have several variants, which EIDR calls "edits". See [[editEIDR]].

Since schema.org types like [[Movie]] and [[TVEpisode]] can be used for both works and their multiple expressions, it is possible to use [[titleEIDR]] alone (for a general description), or alongside [[editEIDR]] for a more edit-specific description.

variants.name: tocContinuation
variants.definition: A [[HyperTocEntry]] can have a [[tocContinuation]] indicated, which is another [[HyperTocEntry]] that would be the default next item to play or render.

variants.name: tocEntry
variants.definition: Indicates a [[HyperTocEntry]] in a [[HyperToc]].

variants.name: tongueWeight
variants.definition:
The permitted vertical load (TWR) of a trailer attached to the vehicle. Also referred to as Tongue Load Rating (TLR) or Vertical Load Rating (VLR)

Typical unit code(s): KGM for kilogram, LBR for pound

* Note 1: You can indicate additional information in the [[name]] of the [[QuantitativeValue]] node.
* Note 2: You may also link to a [[QualitativeValue]] node that provides additional information using [[valueReference]].
* Note 3: Note that you can use [[minValue]] and [[maxValue]] to indicate ranges.

variants.name: torque
variants.definition:
The torque (turning force) of the vehicle's engine.

Typical unit code(s): NU for newton metre (N m), F17 for pound-force per foot, or F48 for pound-force per inch

* Note 1: You can link to information about how the given value has been determined (e.g. reference RPM) using the [[valueReference]] property.
* Note 2: You can use [[minValue]] and [[maxValue]] to indicate ranges.

variants.name: totalPrice
variants.definition:
The total price for the reservation or ticket, including applicable taxes, shipping, etc.

Usage guidelines:

* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similiar Unicode symbols.
* Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.

variants.name: totalTime
variants.definition: The total time required to perform instructions or a direction (including time to prepare the supplies), in [ISO 8601 duration format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601).

variants.name: tourBookingPage
variants.definition: A page providing information on how to book a tour of some [[Place]], such as an [[Accommodation]] or [[ApartmentComplex]] in a real estate setting, as well as other kinds of tours as appropriate.

variants.name: TouristAttraction
variants.definition: A tourist attraction.  In principle any Thing can be a [[TouristAttraction]], from a [[Mountain]] and [[LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings]] to a [[LocalBusiness]].  This Type can be used on its own to describe a general [[TouristAttraction]], or be used as an [[additionalType]] to add tourist attraction properties to any other type.  (See examples below)

variants.name: TouristDestination
variants.definition:
A tourist destination. In principle any [[Place]] can be a [[TouristDestination]] from a [[City]], [[Region]] or [[Country]] to an [[AmusementPark]] or [[Hotel]]. This Type can be used on its own to describe a general [[TouristDestination]], or be used as an [[additionalType]] to add tourist relevant properties to any other [[Place]].  A [[TouristDestination]] is defined as a [[Place]] that contains, or is colocated with, one or more [[TouristAttraction]]s, often linked by a similar theme or interest to a particular [[touristType]]. The [UNWTO](http://www2.unwto.org/) defines Destination (main destination of a tourism trip) as the place visited that is central to the decision to take the trip.
  (See examples below).

variants.name: TouristTrip
variants.definition:
A tourist trip. A created itinerary of visits to one or more places of interest ([[TouristAttraction]]/[[TouristDestination]]) often linked by a similar theme, geographic area, or interest to a particular [[touristType]]. The [UNWTO](http://www2.unwto.org/) defines tourism trip as the Trip taken by visitors.
  (See examples below).

variants.name: touristType
variants.definition: Attraction suitable for type(s) of tourist. eg. Children, visitors from a particular country, etc.

variants.name: TrackAction
variants.definition:
An agent tracks an object for updates.

Related actions:

* [[FollowAction]]: Unlike FollowAction, TrackAction refers to the interest on the location of innanimates objects.
* [[SubscribeAction]]: Unlike SubscribeAction, TrackAction refers to  the interest on the location of innanimate objects.

variants.name: trailerWeight
variants.definition:
The permitted weight of a trailer attached to the vehicle.

Typical unit code(s): KGM for kilogram, LBR for pound
* Note 1: You can indicate additional information in the [[name]] of the [[QuantitativeValue]] node.
* Note 2: You may also link to a [[QualitativeValue]] node that provides additional information using [[valueReference]].
* Note 3: Note that you can use [[minValue]] and [[maxValue]] to indicate ranges.

variants.name: TrainReservation
variants.definition: A reservation for train travel.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, use [[Offer]].

variants.name: transitTimeLabel
variants.definition: Label to match an [[OfferShippingDetails]] with a [[DeliveryTimeSettings]] (within the context of a [[shippingSettingsLink]] cross-reference).

variants.name: unnamedSourcesPolicy
variants.definition: For an [[Organization]] (typically a [[NewsMediaOrganization]]), a statement about policy on use of unnamed sources and the decision process required.

variants.name: UnRegisterAction
variants.definition:
The act of un-registering from a service.

Related actions:

* [[RegisterAction]]: antonym of UnRegisterAction.
* [[LeaveAction]]: Unlike LeaveAction, UnRegisterAction implies that you are unregistering from a service you werer previously registered, rather than leaving a team/group of people.

variants.name: upvoteCount
variants.definition: The number of upvotes this question, answer or comment has received from the community.

variants.name: usageInfo
variants.definition:
The schema.org [[usageInfo]] property indicates further information about a [[CreativeWork]]. This property is applicable both to works that are freely available and to those that require payment or other transactions. It can reference additional information e.g. community expectations on preferred linking and citation conventions, as well as purchasing details. For something that can be commercially licensed, usageInfo can provide detailed, resource-specific information about licensing options.

This property can be used alongside the license property which indicates license(s) applicable to some piece of content. The usageInfo property can provide information about other licensing options, e.g. acquiring commercial usage rights for an image that is also available under non-commercial creative commons licenses.

variants.name: UserBlocks
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].

variants.name: UserCheckins
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].

variants.name: UserComments
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].

variants.name: UserDownloads
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].

variants.name: UserInteraction
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].

variants.name: UserLikes
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].

variants.name: UserPageVisits
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].

variants.name: UserPlays
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].

variants.name: UserPlusOnes
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].

variants.name: UserReview
variants.definition: A review created by an end-user (e.g. consumer, purchaser, attendee etc.), in contrast with [[CriticReview]].

variants.name: UserTweets
variants.definition: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].

variants.name: usesHealthPlanIdStandard
variants.definition: The standard for interpreting thePlan ID. The preferred is "HIOS". See the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services for more details.

variants.name: utterances
variants.definition: Text of an utterances (spoken words, lyrics etc.) that occurs at a certain section of a media object, represented as a [[HyperTocEntry]].

variants.name: value
variants.definition:
The value of the quantitative value or property value node.

* For [[QuantitativeValue]] and [[MonetaryAmount]], the recommended type for values is 'Number'.
* For [[PropertyValue]], it can be 'Text;', 'Number', 'Boolean', or 'StructuredValue'.
* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similiar Unicode symbols.
* Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.

variants.name: variantCover
variants.definition:
A description of the variant cover
    	for the issue, if the issue is a variant printing. For example, "Bryan Hitch
    	Variant Cover" or "2nd Printing Variant".

variants.name: variesBy
variants.definition: Indicates the property or properties by which the variants in a [[ProductGroup]] vary, e.g. their size, color etc. Schema.org properties can be referenced by their short name e.g. "color"; terms defined elsewhere can be referenced with their URIs.

variants.name: vehicleSeatingCapacity
variants.definition: The number of passengers that can be seated in the vehicle, both in terms of the physical space available, and in terms of limitations set by law.\n\nTypical unit code(s): C62 for persons.

variants.name: verificationFactCheckingPolicy
variants.definition: Disclosure about verification and fact-checking processes for a [[NewsMediaOrganization]] or other fact-checking [[Organization]].

variants.name: WarrantyScope
variants.definition:
A range of of services that will be provided to a customer free of charge in case of a defect or malfunction of a product.

Commonly used values:

* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Labor-BringIn
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PartsAndLabor-BringIn
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PartsAndLabor-PickUp

variants.name: WebContent
variants.definition: WebContent is a type representing all [[WebPage]], [[WebSite]] and [[WebPageElement]] content. It is sometimes the case that detailed distinctions between Web pages, sites and their parts is not always important or obvious. The  [[WebContent]] type makes it easier to describe Web-addressable content without requiring such distinctions to always be stated. (The intent is that the existing types [[WebPage]], [[WebSite]] and [[WebPageElement]] will eventually be declared as subtypes of [[WebContent]].)

variants.name: weightTotal
variants.definition:
The permitted total weight of the loaded vehicle, including passengers and cargo and the weight of the empty vehicle.

Typical unit code(s): KGM for kilogram, LBR for pound

* Note 1: You can indicate additional information in the [[name]] of the [[QuantitativeValue]] node.
* Note 2: You may also link to a [[QualitativeValue]] node that provides additional information using [[valueReference]].
* Note 3: Note that you can use [[minValue]] and [[maxValue]] to indicate ranges.

variants.name: wheelbase
variants.definition: The distance between the centers of the front and rear wheels.\n\nTypical unit code(s): CMT for centimeters, MTR for meters, INH for inches, FOT for foot/feet

variants.name: xpath
variants.definition: An XPath, e.g. of a [[SpeakableSpecification]] or [[WebPageElement]]. In the latter case, multiple matches within a page can constitute a single conceptual "Web page element".

variants.name: yearBuilt
variants.definition: The year an [[Accommodation]] was constructed. This corresponds to the [YearBuilt field in RESO](https://ddwiki.reso.org/display/DDW17/YearBuilt+Field).

variants.name: ActivationFee
variants.definition: Represents the activation fee part of the total price for an offered product, for example a cellphone contract.

variants.name: AllergiesHealthAspect
variants.definition: Content about the allergy-related aspects of a health topic.

variants.name: BackOrder
variants.definition: Indicates that the item is available on back order.

variants.name: beneficiaryBank
variants.definition: A bank or bank’s branch, financial institution or international financial institution operating the beneficiary’s bank account or releasing funds for the beneficiary.

variants.name: billingDuration
variants.definition: Specifies for how long this price (or price component) will be billed. Can be used, for example, to model the contractual duration of a subscription or payment plan. Type can be either a Duration or a Number (in which case the unit of measurement, for example month, is specified by the unitCode property).

variants.name: billingStart
variants.definition: Specifies after how much time this price (or price component) becomes valid and billing starts. Can be used, for example, to model a price increase after the first year of a subscription. The unit of measurement is specified by the unitCode property.

variants.name: BodyMeasurementArm
variants.definition: Arm length (measured between arms/shoulder line intersection and the prominent wrist bone). Used, for example, to fit shirts.

variants.name: BodyMeasurementBust
variants.definition: Maximum girth of bust. Used, for example, to fit women's suits.

variants.name: BodyMeasurementChest
variants.definition: Maximum girth of chest. Used, for example, to fit men's suits.

variants.name: BodyMeasurementFoot
variants.definition: Foot length (measured between end of the most prominent toe and the most prominent part of the heel). Used, for example, to measure socks.

variants.name: BodyMeasurementHand
variants.definition: Maximum hand girth (measured over the knuckles of the open right hand excluding thumb, fingers together). Used, for example, to fit gloves.

variants.name: BodyMeasurementHead
variants.definition: Maximum girth of head above the ears. Used, for example, to fit hats.

variants.name: BodyMeasurementHeight
variants.definition: Body height (measured between crown of head and soles of feet). Used, for example, to fit jackets.

variants.name: BodyMeasurementHips
variants.definition: Girth of hips (measured around the buttocks). Used, for example, to fit skirts.

variants.name: BodyMeasurementInsideLeg
variants.definition: Inside leg (measured between crotch and soles of feet). Used, for example, to fit pants.

variants.name: BodyMeasurementNeck
variants.definition: Girth of neck. Used, for example, to fit shirts.

variants.name: BodyMeasurementTypeEnumeration
variants.definition: Enumerates types (or dimensions) of a person's body measurements, for example for fitting of clothes.

variants.name: BodyMeasurementUnderbust
variants.definition: Girth of body just below the bust. Used, for example, to fit women's swimwear.

variants.name: BodyMeasurementWaist
variants.definition: Girth of natural waistline (between hip bones and lower ribs). Used, for example, to fit pants.

variants.name: BodyMeasurementWeight
variants.definition: Body weight. Used, for example, to measure pantyhose.

variants.name: broadcastSignalModulation
variants.definition: The modulation (e.g. FM, AM, etc) used by a particular broadcast service.

variants.name: byDay
variants.definition: Defines the day(s) of the week on which a recurring [[Event]] takes place. May be specified using either [[DayOfWeek]], or alternatively [[Text]] conforming to iCal's syntax for byDay recurrence rules.

variants.name: Claim
variants.definition:
A [[Claim]] in Schema.org represents a specific, factually-oriented claim that could be the [[itemReviewed]] in a [[ClaimReview]]. The content of a claim can be summarized with the [[text]] property. Variations on well known claims can have their common identity indicated via [[sameAs]] links, and summarized with a [[name]]. Ideally, a [[Claim]] description includes enough contextual information to minimize the risk of ambiguity or inclarity. In practice, many claims are better understood in the context in which they appear or the interpretations provided by claim reviews.

  Beyond [[ClaimReview]], the Claim type can be associated with related creative works - for example a [[ScholarlyArticle]] or [[Question]] might be [[about]] some [[Claim]].

  At this time, Schema.org does not define any types of relationship between claims. This is a natural area for future exploration.

variants.name: CleaningFee
variants.definition: Represents the cleaning fee part of the total price for an offered product, for example a vacation rental.

variants.name: CommunityHealth
variants.definition: A field of public health focusing on improving health characteristics of a defined population in relation with their geographical or environment areas.

variants.name: costCurrency
variants.definition: The currency (in 3-letter of the drug cost. See: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217.

variants.name: DecontextualizedContent
variants.definition:
Content coded 'missing context' in a [[MediaReview]], considered in the context of how it was published or shared.

For a [[VideoObject]] to be 'missing context': Presenting unaltered video in an inaccurate manner that misrepresents the footage. For example, using incorrect dates or locations, altering the transcript or sharing brief clips from a longer video to mislead viewers. (A video rated 'original' can also be missing context.)

For an [[ImageObject]] to be 'missing context': Presenting unaltered images in an inaccurate manner to misrepresent the image and mislead the viewer. For example, a common tactic is using an unaltered image but saying it came from a different time or place. (An image rated 'original' can also be missing context.)

For an [[ImageObject]] with embedded text to be 'missing context': An unaltered image presented in an inaccurate manner to misrepresent the image and mislead the viewer. For example, a common tactic is using an unaltered image but saying it came from a different time or place. (An 'original' image with inaccurate text would generally fall in this category.)

For an [[AudioObject]] to be 'missing context': Unaltered audio presented in an inaccurate manner that misrepresents it. For example, using incorrect dates or locations, or sharing brief clips from a longer recording to mislead viewers. (Audio rated “original” can also be missing context.)

variants.name: Dermatologic
variants.definition: Something relating to or practicing dermatology.

variants.name: DietNutrition
variants.definition: Dietetic and nutrition as a medical specialty.

variants.name: DistanceFee
variants.definition: Represents the distance fee (e.g., price per km or mile) part of the total price for an offered product, for example a car rental.

variants.name: Downpayment
variants.definition: Represents the downpayment (up-front payment) price component of the total price for an offered product that has additional installment payments.

variants.name: drug
variants.definition: Specifying a drug or medicine used in a medication procedure.

variants.name: duration
variants.definition: The duration of the item (movie, audio recording, event, etc.) in [ISO 8601 date format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601).

variants.name: EditedOrCroppedContent
variants.definition:
Content coded 'edited or cropped content' in a [[MediaReview]], considered in the context of how it was published or shared.

For a [[VideoObject]] to be 'edited or cropped content': The video has been edited or rearranged. This category applies to time edits, including editing multiple videos together to alter the story being told or editing out large portions from a video.

For an [[ImageObject]] to be 'edited or cropped content': Presenting a part of an image from a larger whole to mislead the viewer.

For an [[ImageObject]] with embedded text to be 'edited or cropped content': Presenting a part of an image from a larger whole to mislead the viewer.

For an [[AudioObject]] to be 'edited or cropped content': The audio has been edited or rearranged. This category applies to time edits, including editing multiple audio clips together to alter the story being told or editing out large portions from the recording.

variants.name: EffectivenessHealthAspect
variants.definition: Content about the effectiveness-related aspects of a health topic.

variants.name: EnergyConsumptionDetails
variants.definition: EnergyConsumptionDetails represents information related to the energy efficiency of a product that consumes energy. The information that can be provided is based on international regulations such as for example [EU directive 2017/1369](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2017/1369/oj) for energy labeling and the [Energy labeling rule](https://www.ftc.gov/enforcement/rules/rulemaking-regulatory-reform-proceedings/energy-water-use-labeling-consumer) under the Energy Policy and Conservation Act (EPCA) in the US.

variants.name: EnergyStarCertified
variants.definition: Represents EnergyStar certification.

variants.name: EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
variants.definition: Used to indicate whether a product is EnergyStar certified.

variants.name: EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryA
variants.definition: Represents EU Energy Efficiency Class A as defined in EU energy labeling regulations.

variants.name: EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryA1Plus
variants.definition: Represents EU Energy Efficiency Class A+ as defined in EU energy labeling regulations.

variants.name: EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryA2Plus
variants.definition: Represents EU Energy Efficiency Class A++ as defined in EU energy labeling regulations.

variants.name: EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryA3Plus
variants.definition: Represents EU Energy Efficiency Class A+++ as defined in EU energy labeling regulations.

variants.name: EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryB
variants.definition: Represents EU Energy Efficiency Class B as defined in EU energy labeling regulations.

variants.name: EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryC
variants.definition: Represents EU Energy Efficiency Class C as defined in EU energy labeling regulations.

variants.name: EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryD
variants.definition: Represents EU Energy Efficiency Class D as defined in EU energy labeling regulations.

variants.name: EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryE
variants.definition: Represents EU Energy Efficiency Class E as defined in EU energy labeling regulations.

variants.name: EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryF
variants.definition: Represents EU Energy Efficiency Class F as defined in EU energy labeling regulations.

variants.name: EUEnergyEfficiencyCategoryG
variants.definition: Represents EU Energy Efficiency Class G as defined in EU energy labeling regulations.

variants.name: EUEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
variants.definition: Enumerates the EU energy efficiency classes A-G as well as A+, A++, and A+++ as defined in EU directive 2017/1369.

variants.name: experienceInPlaceOfEducation
variants.definition: Indicates whether a [[JobPosting]] will accept experience (as indicated by [[OccupationalExperienceRequirements]]) in place of its formal educational qualifications (as indicated by [[educationRequirements]]). If true, indicates that satisfying one of these requirements is sufficient.

variants.name: experienceRequirements
variants.definition: Description of skills and experience needed for the position or Occupation.

variants.name: GettingAccessHealthAspect
variants.definition: Content that discusses practical and policy aspects for getting access to specific kinds of healthcare (e.g. distribution mechanisms for vaccines).

variants.name: gtin8
variants.definition: The GTIN-8 code of the product, or the product to which the offer refers. This code is also known as EAN/UCC-8 or 8-digit EAN. See [GS1 GTIN Summary](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin) for more details.

variants.name: hasEnergyConsumptionDetails
variants.definition: Defines the energy efficiency Category (also known as "class" or "rating") for a product according to an international energy efficiency standard.

variants.name: hasEnergyEfficiencyCategory
variants.definition: Defines the energy efficiency Category (which could be either a rating out of range of values or a yes/no certification) for a product according to an international energy efficiency standard.

variants.name: hasMeasurement
variants.definition: A product measurement, for example the inseam of pants, the wheel size of a bicycle, or the gauge of a screw. Usually an exact measurement, but can also be a range of measurements for adjustable products, for example belts and ski bindings.

variants.name: HowItWorksHealthAspect
variants.definition: Content that discusses and explains how a particular health-related topic works, e.g. in terms of mechanisms and underlying science.

variants.name: ineligibleRegion
variants.definition: The ISO 3166-1 (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) or ISO 3166-2 code, the place, or the GeoShape for the geo-political region(s) for which the offer or delivery charge specification is not valid, e.g. a region where the transaction is not allowed.\n\nSee also [[eligibleRegion]].

variants.name: IngredientsHealthAspect
variants.definition: Content discussing ingredients-related aspects of a health topic.

variants.name: Installment
variants.definition: Represents the installment pricing component of the total price for an offered product.

variants.name: isLiveBroadcast
variants.definition: True if the broadcast is of a live event.

variants.name: LaboratoryScience
variants.definition: A medical science pertaining to chemical, hematological, immunologic, microscopic, or bacteriological diagnostic analyses or research.

variants.name: LearningResource
variants.definition:
The LearningResource type can be used to indicate [[CreativeWork]]s (whether physical or digital) that have a particular and explicit orientation towards learning, education, skill acquisition, and other educational purposes.

[[LearningResource]] is expected to be used as an addition to a primary type such as [[Book]], [[VideoObject]], [[Product]] etc.

[[EducationEvent]] serves a similar purpose for event-like things (e.g. a [[Trip]]). A [[LearningResource]] may be created as a result of an [[EducationEvent]], for example by recording one.

variants.name: marginOfError
variants.definition: A marginOfError for an [[Observation]].

variants.name: MeasurementTypeEnumeration
variants.definition: Enumeration of common measurement types (or dimensions), for example "chest" for a person, "inseam" for pants, "gauge" for screws, or "wheel" for bicycles.

variants.name: MediaManipulationRatingEnumeration
variants.definition: Codes for use with the [[mediaAuthenticityCategory]] property, indicating the authenticity of a media object (in the context of how it was published or shared). In general these codes are not mutually exclusive, although some combinations (such as 'original' versus 'transformed', 'edited' and 'staged') would be contradictory if applied in the same [[MediaReview]]. Note that the application of these codes is with regard to a piece of media shared or published in a particular context.

variants.name: MediaReview
variants.definition:
A [[MediaReview]] is a more specialized form of Review dedicated to the evaluation of media content online, typically in the context of fact-checking and misinformation.
    For more general reviews of media in the broader sense, use [[UserReview]], [[CriticReview]] or other [[Review]] types. This definition is
    a work in progress. While the [[MediaManipulationRatingEnumeration]] list reflects significant community review amongst fact-checkers and others working
    to combat misinformation, the specific structures for representing media objects, their versions and publication context, is still evolving. Similarly, best practices for the relationship between [[MediaReview]] and [[ClaimReview]] markup has not yet been finalized.

variants.name: monthsOfExperience
variants.definition: Indicates the minimal number of months of experience required for a position.

variants.name: MortgageLoan
variants.definition: A loan in which property or real estate is used as collateral. (A loan securitized against some real estate).

variants.name: OccupationalExperienceRequirements
variants.definition: Indicates employment-related experience requirements, e.g. [[monthsOfExperience]].

variants.name: OfferShippingDetails
variants.definition:
OfferShippingDetails represents information about shipping destinations.

Multiple of these entities can be used to represent different shipping rates for different destinations:

One entity for Alaska/Hawaii. A different one for continental US.A different one for all France.

Multiple of these entities can be used to represent different shipping costs and delivery times.

Two entities that are identical but differ in rate and time:

e.g. Cheaper and slower: $5 in 5-7days
or Fast and expensive: $15 in 1-2 days.

variants.name: OriginalMediaContent
variants.definition:
Content coded 'as original media content' in a [[MediaReview]], considered in the context of how it was published or shared.

For a [[VideoObject]] to be 'original': No evidence the footage has been misleadingly altered or manipulated, though it may contain false or misleading claims.

For an [[ImageObject]] to be 'original': No evidence the image has been misleadingly altered or manipulated, though it may still contain false or misleading claims.

For an [[ImageObject]] with embedded text to be 'original': No evidence the image has been misleadingly altered or manipulated, though it may still contain false or misleading claims.

For an [[AudioObject]] to be 'original': No evidence the audio has been misleadingly altered or manipulated, though it may contain false or misleading claims.

variants.name: PregnancyHealthAspect
variants.definition: Content discussing pregnancy-related aspects of a health topic.

variants.name: repeatFrequency
variants.definition:
Defines the frequency at which [[Event]]s will occur according to a schedule [[Schedule]]. The intervals between
      events should be defined as a [[Duration]] of time.

variants.name: SafetyHealthAspect
variants.definition: Content about the safety-related aspects of a health topic.

variants.name: SatireOrParodyContent
variants.definition:
Content coded 'satire or content' in a [[MediaReview]], considered in the context of how it was published or shared.

For a [[VideoObject]] to be 'satire or parody content': A video that was created as political or humorous commentary and is presented in that context. (Reshares of satire/parody content that do not include relevant context are more likely to fall under the “missing context” rating.)

For an [[ImageObject]] to be 'satire or parody content': An image that was created as political or humorous commentary and is presented in that context. (Reshares of satire/parody content that do not include relevant context are more likely to fall under the “missing context” rating.)

For an [[ImageObject]] with embedded text to be 'satire or parody content': An image that was created as political or humorous commentary and is presented in that context. (Reshares of satire/parody content that do not include relevant context are more likely to fall under the “missing context” rating.)

For an [[AudioObject]] to be 'satire or parody content': Audio that was created as political or humorous commentary and is presented in that context. (Reshares of satire/parody content that do not include relevant context are more likely to fall under the “missing context” rating.)

variants.name: schemaVersion
variants.definition:
Indicates (by URL or string) a particular version of a schema used in some CreativeWork. This property was created primarily to
    indicate the use of a specific schema.org release, e.g. ```10.0``` as a simple string, or more explicitly via URL, ```https://schema.org/docs/releases.html#v10.0```. There may be situations in which other schemas might usefully be referenced this way, e.g. ```http://dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dces/1999-07-02/``` but this has not been carefully explored in the community.

variants.name: size
variants.definition: A standardized size of a product or creative work, specified either through a simple textual string (for example 'XL', '32Wx34L'), a  QuantitativeValue with a unitCode, or a comprehensive and structured [[SizeSpecification]]; in other cases, the [[width]], [[height]], [[depth]] and [[weight]] properties may be more applicable.

variants.name: sizeGroup
variants.definition: The size group (also known as "size type") for a product's size. Size groups are common in the fashion industry to define size segments and suggested audiences for wearable products. Multiple values can be combined, for example "men's big and tall", "petite maternity" or "regular"

variants.name: SizeGroupEnumeration
variants.definition: Enumerates common size groups for various product categories.

variants.name: SizeSpecification
variants.definition: Size related properties of a product, typically a size code ([[name]]) and optionally a [[sizeSystem]], [[sizeGroup]], and product measurements ([[hasMeasurement]]). In addition, the intended audience can be defined through [[suggestedAge]], [[suggestedGender]], and suggested body measurements ([[suggestedMeasurement]]).

variants.name: sizeSystem
variants.definition: The size system used to identify a product's size. Typically either a standard (for example, "GS1" or "ISO-EN13402"), country code (for example "US" or "JP"), or a measuring system (for example "Metric" or "Imperial").

variants.name: SizeSystemEnumeration
variants.definition: Enumerates common size systems for different categories of products, for example "EN-13402" or "UK" for wearables or "Imperial" for screws.

variants.name: SizeSystemImperial
variants.definition: Imperial size system.

variants.name: SizeSystemMetric
variants.definition: Metric size system.

variants.name: SpecialAnnouncement
variants.definition:
A SpecialAnnouncement combines a simple date-stamped textual information update
      with contextualized Web links and other structured data.  It represents an information update made by a
      locally-oriented organization, for example schools, pharmacies, healthcare providers,  community groups, police,
      local government.

For work in progress guidelines on Coronavirus-related markup see [this doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14ikaGCKxo50rRM7nvKSlbUpjyIk2WMQd3IkB1lItlrM/edit#).

The motivating scenario for SpecialAnnouncement is the [Coronavirus pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_coronavirus_pandemic), and the initial vocabulary is oriented to this urgent situation. Schema.org
expect to improve the markup iteratively as it is deployed and as feedback emerges from use. In addition to our
usual [Github entry](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/2490), feedback comments can also be provided in [this document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fpdFFxk8s87CWwACs53SGkYv3aafSxz_DTtOQxMrBJQ/edit#).


While this schema is designed to communicate urgent crisis-related information, it is not the same as an emergency warning technology like [CAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Alerting_Protocol), although there may be overlaps. The intent is to cover
the kinds of everyday practical information being posted to existing websites during an emergency situation.

Several kinds of information can be provided:

We encourage the provision of "name", "text", "datePosted", "expires" (if appropriate), "category" and
"url" as a simple baseline. It is important to provide a value for "category" where possible, most ideally as a well known
URL from Wikipedia or Wikidata. In the case of the 2019-2020 Coronavirus pandemic, this should be "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2019-20\_coronavirus\_pandemic" or "https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q81068910".

For many of the possible properties, values can either be simple links or an inline description, depending on whether a summary is available. For a link, provide just the URL of the appropriate page as the property's value. For an inline description, use a [[WebContent]] type, and provide the url as a property of that, alongside at least a simple "[[text]]" summary of the page. It is
unlikely that a single SpecialAnnouncement will need all of the possible properties simultaneously.

We expect that in many cases the page referenced might contain more specialized structured data, e.g. contact info, [[openingHours]], [[Event]], [[FAQPage]] etc. By linking to those pages from a [[SpecialAnnouncement]] you can help make it clearer that the events are related to the situation (e.g. Coronavirus) indicated by the [[category]] property of the [[SpecialAnnouncement]].

Many [[SpecialAnnouncement]]s will relate to particular regions and to identifiable local organizations. Use [[spatialCoverage]] for the region, and [[announcementLocation]] to indicate specific [[LocalBusiness]]es and [[CivicStructure]]s. If the announcement affects both a particular region and a specific location (for example, a library closure that serves an entire region), use both [[spatialCoverage]] and [[announcementLocation]].

The [[about]] property can be used to indicate entities that are the focus of the announcement. We now recommend using [[about]] only
for representing non-location entities (e.g. a [[Course]] or a [[RadioStation]]). For places, use [[announcementLocation]] and [[spatialCoverage]]. Consumers of this markup should be aware that the initial design encouraged the use of /about for locations too.

The basic content of [[SpecialAnnouncement]] is similar to that of an [RSS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RSS) or [Atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom_(Web_standard)) feed. For publishers without such feeds, basic feed-like information can be shared by posting
[[SpecialAnnouncement]] updates in a page, e.g. using JSON-LD. For sites with Atom/RSS functionality, you can point to a feed
with the [[webFeed]] property. This can be a simple URL, or an inline [[DataFeed]] object, with [[encodingFormat]] providing
media type information e.g. "application/rss+xml" or "application/atom+xml".

variants.name: StagedContent
variants.definition:
Content coded 'staged content' in a [[MediaReview]], considered in the context of how it was published or shared.

For a [[VideoObject]] to be 'staged content': A video that has been created using actors or similarly contrived.

For an [[ImageObject]] to be 'staged content': An image that was created using actors or similarly contrived, such as a screenshot of a fake tweet.

For an [[ImageObject]] with embedded text to be 'staged content': An image that was created using actors or similarly contrived, such as a screenshot of a fake tweet.

For an [[AudioObject]] to be 'staged content': Audio that has been created using actors or similarly contrived.

variants.name: StatisticalPopulation
variants.definition:
A StatisticalPopulation is a set of instances of a certain given type that satisfy some set of constraints. The property [[populationType]] is used to specify the type. Any property that can be used on instances of that type can appear on the statistical population. For example, a [[StatisticalPopulation]] representing all [[Person]]s with a [[homeLocation]] of East Podunk California, would be described by applying the appropriate [[homeLocation]] and [[populationType]] properties to a [[StatisticalPopulation]] item that stands for that set of people.
The properties [[numConstraints]] and [[constrainingProperty]] are used to specify which of the populations properties are used to specify the population. Note that the sense of "population" used here is the general sense of a statistical
population, and does not imply that the population consists of people. For example, a [[populationType]] of [[Event]] or [[NewsArticle]] could be used. See also [[Observation]], and the [data and datasets](/docs/data-and-datasets.html) overview for more details.

variants.name: Subscription
variants.definition: Represents the subscription pricing component of the total price for an offered product.

variants.name: suggestedAge
variants.definition: The age or age range for the intended audience or person, for example 3-12 months for infants, 1-5 years for toddlers.

variants.name: suggestedGender
variants.definition: The suggested gender of the intended person or audience, for example "male", "female", or "unisex".

variants.name: suggestedMaxAge
variants.definition: Maximum recommended age in years for the audience or user.

variants.name: suggestedMeasurement
variants.definition: A suggested range of body measurements for the intended audience or person, for example inseam between 32 and 34 inches or height between 170 and 190 cm. Typically found on a size chart for wearable products.

variants.name: suggestedMinAge
variants.definition: Minimum recommended age in years for the audience or user.

variants.name: TouristDestination
variants.definition:
A tourist destination. In principle any [[Place]] can be a [[TouristDestination]] from a [[City]], Region or [[Country]] to an [[AmusementPark]] or [[Hotel]]. This Type can be used on its own to describe a general [[TouristDestination]], or be used as an [[additionalType]] to add tourist relevant properties to any other [[Place]].  A [[TouristDestination]] is defined as a [[Place]] that contains, or is colocated with, one or more [[TouristAttraction]]s, often linked by a similar theme or interest to a particular [[touristType]]. The [UNWTO](http://www2.unwto.org/) defines Destination (main destination of a tourism trip) as the place visited that is central to the decision to take the trip.
  (See examples below).

variants.name: TransformedContent
variants.definition:
Content coded 'transformed content' in a [[MediaReview]], considered in the context of how it was published or shared.

For a [[VideoObject]] to be 'transformed content':  or all of the video has been manipulated to transform the footage itself. This category includes using tools like the Adobe Suite to change the speed of the video, add or remove visual elements or dub audio. Deepfakes are also a subset of transformation.

For an [[ImageObject]] to be transformed content': Adding or deleting visual elements to give the image a different meaning with the intention to mislead.

For an [[ImageObject]] with embedded text to be 'transformed content': Adding or deleting visual elements to give the image a different meaning with the intention to mislead.

For an [[AudioObject]] to be 'transformed content': Part or all of the audio has been manipulated to alter the words or sounds, or the audio has been synthetically generated, such as to create a sound-alike voice.

variants.name: valueReference
variants.definition: A secondary value that provides additional information on the original value, e.g. a reference temperature or a type of measurement.

variants.name: WearableMeasurementBack
variants.definition: Measurement of the back section, for example of a jacket

variants.name: WearableMeasurementChestOrBust
variants.definition: Measurement of the chest/bust section, for example of a suit

variants.name: WearableMeasurementCollar
variants.definition: Measurement of the collar, for example of a shirt

variants.name: WearableMeasurementCup
variants.definition: Measurement of the cup, for example of a bra

variants.name: WearableMeasurementHeight
variants.definition: Measurement of the height, for example the heel height of a shoe

variants.name: WearableMeasurementHips
variants.definition: Measurement of the hip section, for example of a skirt

variants.name: WearableMeasurementInseam
variants.definition: Measurement of the inseam, for example of pants

variants.name: WearableMeasurementLength
variants.definition: Represents the length, for example of a dress

variants.name: WearableMeasurementOutsideLeg
variants.definition: Measurement of the outside leg, for example of pants

variants.name: WearableMeasurementSleeve
variants.definition: Measurement of the sleeve length, for example of a shirt

variants.name: WearableMeasurementTypeEnumeration
variants.definition: Enumerates common types of measurement for wearables products.

variants.name: WearableMeasurementWaist
variants.definition: Measurement of the waist section, for example of pants

variants.name: WearableMeasurementWidth
variants.definition: Measurement of the width, for example of shoes

variants.name: WearableSizeGroupBig
variants.definition: Size group "Big" for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeGroupBoys
variants.definition: Size group "Boys" for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeGroupEnumeration
variants.definition: Enumerates common size groups (also known as "size types") for wearable products.

variants.name: WearableSizeGroupExtraShort
variants.definition: Size group "Extra Short" for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeGroupExtraTall
variants.definition: Size group "Extra Tall" for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeGroupGirls
variants.definition: Size group "Girls" for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeGroupHusky
variants.definition: Size group "Husky" (or "Stocky") for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeGroupInfants
variants.definition: Size group "Infants" for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeGroupJuniors
variants.definition: Size group "Juniors" for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeGroupMaternity
variants.definition: Size group "Maternity" for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeGroupMens
variants.definition: Size group "Mens" for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeGroupMisses
variants.definition: Size group "Misses" (also known as "Missy") for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeGroupPetite
variants.definition: Size group "Petite" for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeGroupPlus
variants.definition: Size group "Plus" for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeGroupRegular
variants.definition: Size group "Regular" for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeGroupShort
variants.definition: Size group "Short" for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeGroupTall
variants.definition: Size group "Tall" for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeGroupWomens
variants.definition: Size group "Womens" for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeSystemAU
variants.definition: Australian size system for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeSystemBR
variants.definition: Brazilian size system for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeSystemCN
variants.definition: Chinese size system for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeSystemContinental
variants.definition: Continental size system for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeSystemDE
variants.definition: German size system for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeSystemEN13402
variants.definition: EN 13402 (joint European standard for size labelling of clothes).

variants.name: WearableSizeSystemEnumeration
variants.definition: Enumerates common size systems specific for wearable products

variants.name: WearableSizeSystemEurope
variants.definition: European size system for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeSystemFR
variants.definition: French size system for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeSystemGS1
variants.definition: GS1 (formerly NRF) size system for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeSystemIT
variants.definition: Italian size system for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeSystemJP
variants.definition: Japanese size system for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeSystemMX
variants.definition: Mexican size system for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeSystemUK
variants.definition: United Kingdom size system for wearables.

variants.name: WearableSizeSystemUS
variants.definition: United States size system for wearables.

variants.name: WebContent
variants.definition: WebContent is a type representing all [[WebPage]], [[WebSite]] and [[WebPageElement]] content. It is sometimes the case that detailed distinctions between Web pages, sites and their parts is not always important or obvious. The  [[WebContent]] type makes it easier to describe Web-addressable content without requiring such distinctions to always be stated. (The intent is that the existing types [[WebPage]], [[WebSite]] and [[WebPageElement]] will eventually be declared as subtypes of [[WebContent]]).

variants.name: actor
variants.definition: An actor, e.g. in tv, radio, movie, video games etc., or in an event. Actors can be associated with individual items or with a series, episode, clip.

variants.name: additionalProperty
variants.definition: A property-value pair representing an additional characteristics of the entitity, e.g. a product feature or another characteristic for which there is no matching property in schema.org.\n\nNote: Publishers should be aware that applications designed to use specific schema.org properties (e.g. https://schema.org/width, https://schema.org/color, https://schema.org/gtin13, ...) will typically expect such data to be provided using those properties, rather than using the generic property/value mechanism.

variants.name: alternativeOf
variants.definition: Another gene which is a variation of this one.

variants.name: archivedAt
variants.definition: Indicates a page or other link involved in archival of a [[CreativeWork]]. In the case of [[MediaReview]], the items in a [[MediaReviewItem]] may often become inaccessible, but be archived by archival, journalistic, activist, or law enforcement organizations. In such cases, the referenced page may not directly publish the content.

variants.name: associatedClaimReview
variants.definition: An associated [[ClaimReview]], related by specific common content, topic or claim. The expectation is that this property would be most typically used in cases where a single activity is conducting both claim reviews and media reviews, in which case [[relatedMediaReview]] would commonly be used on a [[ClaimReview]], while [[relatedClaimReview]] would be used on [[MediaReview]].

variants.name: associatedDisease
variants.definition: Disease associated to this BioChemEntity. Such disease can be a MedicalCondition or a URL. If you want to add an evidence supporting the association, please use PropertyValue.

variants.name: associatedMediaReview
variants.definition: An associated [[MediaReview]], related by specific common content, topic or claim. The expectation is that this property would be most typically used in cases where a single activity is conducting both claim reviews and media reviews, in which case [[relatedMediaReview]] would commonly be used on a [[ClaimReview]], while [[relatedClaimReview]] would be used on [[MediaReview]].

variants.name: associatedReview
variants.definition: An associated [[Review]].

variants.name: AudioObjectSnapshot
variants.definition: A specific and exact (byte-for-byte) version of an [[AudioObject]]. Two byte-for-byte identical files, for the purposes of this type, considered identical. If they have different embedded metadata the files will differ. Different external facts about the files, e.g. creator or dateCreated that aren't represented in their actual content, do not affect this notion of identity.

variants.name: BioChemEntity
variants.definition: Any biological, chemical, or biochemical thing. For example: a protein; a gene; a chemical; a synthetic chemical.

variants.name: bioChemInteraction
variants.definition: A BioChemEntity that is known to interact with this item.

variants.name: bioChemSimilarity
variants.definition: A similar BioChemEntity, e.g., obtained by fingerprint similarity algorithms.

variants.name: biologicalRole
variants.definition: A role played by the BioChemEntity within a biological context.

variants.name: Blog
variants.definition: A [blog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blog), sometimes known as a "weblog". Note that the individual posts ([[BlogPosting]]s) in a [[Blog]] are often colloqually referred to by the same term.

variants.name: blogPosts
variants.definition: Indicates a post that is part of a [[Blog]]. Note that historically, what we term a "Blog" was once known as a "weblog", and that what we term a "BlogPosting" is now often colloquially referred to as a "blog".

variants.name: buyer
variants.definition: A sub property of participant. The participant/person/organization that bought the object.

variants.name: chemicalComposition
variants.definition: The chemical composition describes the identity and relative ratio of the chemical elements that make up the substance.

variants.name: chemicalRole
variants.definition: A role played by the BioChemEntity within a chemical context.

variants.name: ChemicalSubstance
variants.definition: A chemical substance is 'a portion of matter of constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same type or of different types' (source: [ChEBI:59999](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/searchId.do?chebiId=59999)).

variants.name: childTaxon
variants.definition: Closest child taxa of the taxon in question.

variants.name: claimInterpreter
variants.definition:
For a [[Claim]] interpreted from [[MediaObject]] content
    sed to indicate a claim contained, implied or refined from the content of a [[MediaObject]].

variants.name: countryOfAssembly
variants.definition: The place where the product was assembled.

variants.name: countryOfLastProcessing
variants.definition: The place where the item (typically [[Product]]) was last processed and tested before importation.

variants.name: countryOfOrigin
variants.definition:
The country of origin of something, including products as well as creative  works such as movie and TV content.

In the case of TV and movie, this would be the country of the principle offices of the production company or individual responsible for the movie. For other kinds of [[CreativeWork]] it is difficult to provide fully general guidance, and properties such as [[contentLocation]] and [[locationCreated]] may be more applicable.

In the case of products, the country of origin of the product. The exact interpretation of this may vary by context and product type, and cannot be fully enumerated here.

variants.name: customerRemorseReturnFees
variants.definition: The type of return fees if the product is returned due to customer remorse.

variants.name: customerRemorseReturnLabelSource
variants.definition: The method (from an enumeration) by which the customer obtains a return shipping label for a product returned due to customer remorse.

variants.name: customerRemorseReturnShippingFeesAmount
variants.definition: The amount of shipping costs if a product is returned due to customer remorse. Applicable when property [[customerRemorseReturnFees]] equals [[ReturnShippingFees]].

variants.name: directApply
variants.definition: Indicates whether an [[url]] that is associated with a [[JobPosting]] enables direct application for the job, via the posting website. A job posting is considered to have directApply of [[True]] if an application process for the specified job can be directly initiated via the url(s) given (noting that e.g. multiple internet domains might nevertheless be involved at an implementation level). A value of [[False]] is appropriate if there is no clear path to applying directly online for the specified job, navigating directly from the JobPosting url(s) supplied.

variants.name: embeddedTextCaption
variants.definition: Represents textual captioning from a [[MediaObject]], e.g. text of a 'meme'.

variants.name: encodesBioChemEntity
variants.definition: Another BioChemEntity encoded by this one.

variants.name: endDate
variants.definition: The end date and time of the item (in [ISO 8601 date format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)).

variants.name: endTime
variants.definition: The endTime of something. For a reserved event or service (e.g. FoodEstablishmentReservation), the time that it is expected to end. For actions that span a period of time, when the action was performed. e.g. John wrote a book from January to *December*. For media, including audio and video, it's the time offset of the end of a clip within a larger file.\n\nNote that Event uses startDate/endDate instead of startTime/endTime, even when describing dates with times. This situation may be clarified in future revisions.

variants.name: ExchangeRefund
variants.definition: Specifies that a refund can be done as an exchange for the same product.

variants.name: expressedIn
variants.definition: Tissue, organ, biological sample, etc in which activity of this gene has been observed experimentally. For example brain, digestive system.

variants.name: FreeReturn
variants.definition: Specifies that product returns are free of charge for the customer.

variants.name: FullRefund
variants.definition: Specifies that a refund can be done in the full amount the customer paid for the product

variants.name: Gene
variants.definition: A discrete unit of inheritance which affects one or more biological traits (Source: [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene)). Examples include FOXP2 (Forkhead box protein P2), SCARNA21 (small Cajal body-specific RNA 21), A- (agouti genotype).

variants.name: hasBioChemEntityPart
variants.definition: Indicates a BioChemEntity that (in some sense) has this BioChemEntity as a part.

variants.name: hasBioPolymerSequence
variants.definition: A symbolic representation of a BioChemEnity. For example, a nucleotide sequence of a Gene or an amino acid sequence of a Protein.

variants.name: hasDefinedTerm
variants.definition: A Defined Term contained in this term set.

variants.name: hasMerchantReturnPolicy
variants.definition: Specifies a MerchantReturnPolicy that may be applicable.

variants.name: hasMolecularFunction
variants.definition: Molecular function performed by this BioChemEntity; please use PropertyValue if you want to include any evidence.

variants.name: hasRepresentation
variants.definition: A common representation such as a protein sequence or chemical structure for this entity. For images use schema.org/image.

variants.name: ImageObjectSnapshot
variants.definition: A specific and exact (byte-for-byte) version of an [[ImageObject]]. Two byte-for-byte identical files, for the purposes of this type, considered identical. If they have different embedded metadata (e.g. XMP, EXIF) the files will differ. Different external facts about the files, e.g. creator or dateCreated that aren't represented in their actual content, do not affect this notion of identity.

variants.name: inChI
variants.definition: Non-proprietary identifier for molecular entity that can be used in printed and electronic data sources thus enabling easier linking of diverse data compilations.

variants.name: inChIKey
variants.definition: InChIKey is a hashed version of the full InChI (using the SHA-256 algorithm).

variants.name: inStoreReturnsOffered
variants.definition: Are in-store returns offered? (for more advanced return methods use the [[returnMethod]] property)

variants.name: interpretedAsClaim
variants.definition: Used to indicate a specific claim contained, implied, translated or refined from the content of a [[MediaObject]] or other [[CreativeWork]]. The interpreting party can be indicated using [[claimInterpreter]].

variants.name: isEncodedByBioChemEntity
variants.definition: Another BioChemEntity encoding by this one.

variants.name: isInvolvedInBiologicalProcess
variants.definition: Biological process this BioChemEntity is involved in; please use PropertyValue if you want to include any evidence.

variants.name: isLocatedInSubcellularLocation
variants.definition: Subcellular location where this BioChemEntity is located; please use PropertyValue if you want to include any evidence.

variants.name: isPartOfBioChemEntity
variants.definition: Indicates a BioChemEntity that is (in some sense) a part of this BioChemEntity.

variants.name: itemCondition
variants.definition: A predefined value from OfferItemCondition specifying the condition of the product or service, or the products or services included in the offer. Also used for product return policies to specify the condition of products accepted for returns.

variants.name: itemDefectReturnFees
variants.definition: The type of return fees for returns of defect products.

variants.name: itemDefectReturnLabelSource
variants.definition: The method (from an enumeration) by which the customer obtains a return shipping label for a defect product.

variants.name: itemDefectReturnShippingFeesAmount
variants.definition: Amount of shipping costs for defect product returns. Applicable when property [[itemDefectReturnFees]] equals [[ReturnShippingFees]].

variants.name: iupacName
variants.definition: Systematic method of naming chemical compounds as recommended by the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC).

variants.name: LiveBlogPosting
variants.definition: A [[LiveBlogPosting]] is a [[BlogPosting]] intended to provide a rolling textual coverage of an ongoing event through continuous updates.

variants.name: location
variants.definition: The location of, for example, where an event is happening, where an organization is located, or where an action takes place.

variants.name: mediaItemAppearance
variants.definition: In the context of a [[MediaReview]], indicates specific media item(s) that are grouped using a [[MediaReviewItem]].

variants.name: MediaReviewItem
variants.definition: Represents an item or group of closely related items treated as a unit for the sake of evaluation in a [[MediaReview]]. Authorship etc. apply to the items rather than to the curation/grouping or reviewing party.

variants.name: merchantReturnDays
variants.definition: Specifies either a fixed return date or the number of days (from the delivery date) that a product can be returned. Used when the [[returnPolicyCategory]] property is specified as [[MerchantReturnFiniteReturnWindow]].

variants.name: MerchantReturnEnumeration
variants.definition: Enumerates several kinds of product return policies.

variants.name: MerchantReturnFiniteReturnWindow
variants.definition: Specifies that there is a finite window for product returns.

variants.name: merchantReturnLink
variants.definition: Specifies a Web page or service by URL, for product returns.

variants.name: MerchantReturnNotPermitted
variants.definition: Specifies that product returns are not permitted.

variants.name: MerchantReturnPolicy
variants.definition: A MerchantReturnPolicy provides information about product return policies associated with an [[Organization]], [[Product]], or [[Offer]].

variants.name: MerchantReturnPolicySeasonalOverride
variants.definition: A seasonal override of a return policy, for example used for holidays.

variants.name: MerchantReturnUnlimitedWindow
variants.definition: Specifies that there is an unlimited window for product returns.

variants.name: MerchantReturnUnspecified
variants.definition: Specifies that a product return policy is not provided.

variants.name: MolecularEntity
variants.definition: Any constitutionally or isotopically distinct atom, molecule, ion, ion pair, radical, radical ion, complex, conformer etc., identifiable as a separately distinguishable entity.

variants.name: molecularFormula
variants.definition: The empirical formula is the simplest whole number ratio of all the atoms in a molecule.

variants.name: molecularWeight
variants.definition: This is the molecular weight of the entity being described, not of the parent. Units should be included in the form '<Number> <unit>', for example '12 amu' or as '<QuantitativeValue>.

variants.name: monoisotopicMolecularWeight
variants.definition: The monoisotopic mass is the sum of the masses of the atoms in a molecule using the unbound, ground-state, rest mass of the principal (most abundant) isotope for each element instead of the isotopic average mass. Please include the units the form '<Number> <unit>', for example '770.230488 g/mol' or as '<QuantitativeValue>.

variants.name: negativeNotes
variants.definition: Indicates, in the context of a [[Review]] (e.g. framed as 'pro' vs 'con' considerations), negative considerations - either as unstructured text, or a list.

variants.name: originalMediaContextDescription
variants.definition: Describes, in a [[MediaReview]] when dealing with [[DecontextualizedContent]], background information that can contribute to better interpretation of the [[MediaObject]].

variants.name: originalMediaLink
variants.definition: Link to the page containing an original version of the content, or directly to an online copy of the original [[MediaObject]] content, e.g. video file.

variants.name: OriginalShippingFees
variants.definition: Specifies that the customer must pay the original shipping costs when returning a product.

variants.name: parentTaxon
variants.definition: Closest parent taxon of the taxon in question.

variants.name: Play
variants.definition: A play is a form of literature, usually consisting of dialogue between characters, intended for theatrical performance rather than just reading. Note: A performance of a Play would be a [[TheaterEvent]] or [[BroadcastEvent]] - the *Play* being the [[workPerformed]].

variants.name: positiveNotes
variants.definition: Indicates, in the context of a [[Review]] (e.g. framed as 'pro' vs 'con' considerations), positive considerations - either as unstructured text, or a list.

variants.name: potentialUse
variants.definition: Intended use of the BioChemEntity by humans.

variants.name: Protein
variants.definition: Protein is here used in its widest possible definition, as classes of amino acid based molecules. Amyloid-beta Protein in human (UniProt P05067), eukaryota (e.g. an OrthoDB group) or even a single molecule that one can point to are all of type schema:Protein. A protein can thus be a subclass of another protein, e.g. schema:Protein as a UniProt record can have multiple isoforms inside it which would also be schema:Protein. They can be imagined, synthetic, hypothetical or naturally occurring.

variants.name: refundType
variants.definition: A refund type, from an enumerated list.

variants.name: RefundTypeEnumeration
variants.definition: Enumerates several kinds of product return refund types.

variants.name: ResearchOrganization
variants.definition: A Research Organization (e.g. scientific institute, research company).

variants.name: restockingFee
variants.definition: Use [[MonetaryAmount]] to specify a fixed restocking fee for product returns, or use [[Number]] to specify a percentage of the product price paid by the customer.

variants.name: RestockingFees
variants.definition: Specifies that the customer must pay a restocking fee when returning a product

variants.name: ReturnAtKiosk
variants.definition: Specifies that product returns must be made at a kiosk.

variants.name: ReturnByMail
variants.definition: Specifies that product returns must to be done by mail.

variants.name: returnFees
variants.definition: The type of return fees for purchased products (for any return reason)

variants.name: ReturnFeesCustomerResponsibility
variants.definition: Specifies that product returns must be paid for, and are the responsibility of, the customer.

variants.name: ReturnFeesEnumeration
variants.definition: Enumerates several kinds of policies for product return fees.

variants.name: ReturnInStore
variants.definition: Specifies that product returns must be made in a store.

variants.name: ReturnLabelCustomerResponsibility
variants.definition: Indicated that creating a return label is the responsibility of the customer.

variants.name: ReturnLabelDownloadAndPrint
variants.definition: Indicated that a return label must be downloaded and printed by the customer.

variants.name: ReturnLabelInBox
variants.definition: Specifies that a return label will be provided by the seller in the shipping box.

variants.name: returnLabelSource
variants.definition: The method (from an enumeration) by which the customer obtains a return shipping label for a product returned for any reason.

variants.name: ReturnLabelSourceEnumeration
variants.definition: Enumerates several types of return labels for product returns.

variants.name: returnMethod
variants.definition: The type of return method offered, specified from an enumeration.

variants.name: ReturnMethodEnumeration
variants.definition: Enumerates several types of product return methods.

variants.name: returnPolicyCategory
variants.definition: Specifies an applicable return policy (from an enumeration).

variants.name: returnPolicyCountry
variants.definition: The country where the product has to be sent to for returns, for example "Ireland" using the [[name]] property of [[Country]]. You can also provide the two-letter [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1). Note that this can be different from the country where the product was originally shipped from or sent too.

variants.name: returnPolicySeasonalOverride
variants.definition: Seasonal override of a return policy.

variants.name: ReturnShippingFees
variants.definition: Specifies that the customer must pay the return shipping costs when returning a product

variants.name: returnShippingFeesAmount
variants.definition: Amount of shipping costs for product returns (for any reason). Applicable when property [[returnFees]] equals [[ReturnShippingFees]].
